Aneurysm should be distinguished from ectasia, which represents a diffuse dilation of the aorta less than 50 percent of normal aorta diameter.
Comment: Aneurysm is considered a severe (pathological) form of dilatation of a segment of a blood vessel. In clinical practice, dilatation and aneurysm are occasionally used interchangably. In this subhierarchy, we therefore use aneurysm as the primary label and list dilatation as a broad synonym.
Synonym: Bulge in wall of large artery that carries blood away from heart

Name: Accelerated atherosclerosis
Def: Atherosclerosis which occurs in a person with certain risk factors (e.g., SLE, diabetes, smoking, hypertension, hypercholesterolaemia, family history of early heart disease) at an earlier age than would occur in another person without those risk factors.

Name: Dilatation of the cerebral artery
Def: The presence of a localized dilatation or ballooning of a cerebral artery.
Comment: Aneurysm is considered a severe form of dilatation.

Name: Extracranial internal carotid artery dissection
Def: A separation (dissection) of the layers of the extracranial portion of the internal carotid artery wall.

Name: Arteriovenous fistula
Def: An abnormal connection between an artery and vein.

Name: Vascular tortuosity
Def: Abnormal twisting of arteries or veins.

Name: Peripheral arterial stenosis
Def: Narrowing of peripheral arteries with reduction of blood flow to the limbs. This feature may be quantified as an ankle-brachial index of less than 0.9, and may be manifested clinically as claudication.
Comment: The ankle-brachial index (ABI; the ratio of systolic blood pressure in the ankle to that in the arm), is a measure of occlusion of peripheral arteries in the leg. Peripheral arterial stenosis may be observed with atherosclerosis and with increased intima media thickness as seen in diseases such as pseudoxanthoma elasticum. The most common cause of peripheral arterial stenosis in patients over 40 years of age is atherosclerosis. Cerebral and coronary arteries are by definition not included in peripheral artery disease.

Name: Pulmonary arteriovenous fistulas
Def: A rare vascular anomaly with a direct communication between pulmonary artery and pulmonary vein without an intervening capillary bed.

Name: obsolete Dilatation of the descending aorta
Generalized arterial tortuosity
Def: Abnormal tortuous (i.e., twisted) form of arteries affecting most or all arteries.

Name: Descending thoracic aorta aneurysm
Def: An abnormal localized widening (dilatation) of the descending thoracic aorta.
Synonym: Dilatation of the descending thoracic aorta

Name: Absent pulmonary artery
Def: A congenital defect with aplasia (absence) of one of the right or left pulmonary artery.
Comment: This is a rare feature that has been observed in recessive lethal osteogenesis imperfecta with mutation in CRTAP.

Name: Pulmonary artery sling
Def: An anomalous origin of the left pulmonary artery, such that it arises from the posterior aspect of the right pulmonary artery and passes between the trachea and esophagus to reach the left hilum.

Name: Thoracic aorta calcification
Def: An accumulation of calcium and phosphate in arteries with mineral deposits in the intimal or medial layer of the vessel wall in the thoracic aorta.

Name: Calcification of the aorta
Def: Calcification, that is, pathological deposition of calcium salts in the aorta.
Comment: Note that the phrase "aortic calcification" is mainly used to describe calcification of the aortic valve rather than of the aorta itself.

Name: Pulmonary arterial medial hypertrophy
Def: Increase in mass of the tunica media of the arteries in the pulmonary circulation.
Synonym: Hypertrophy of the pulmonary artery wall

Name: Medial calcification of large arteries
Def: Calcification, that is, pathological deposition of calcium salts in the tunica media of large (conduit) arteries.

Name: Recurrent cerebral hemorrhage
Def: Recurrent bleeding into the parenchyma of the brain.

Name: Peripheral pulmonary artery stenosis
Def: Stenosis of a peripheral branch of the pulmonary artery.

Name: Ascending tubular aorta aneurysm
Def: An abnormal localized widening (dilatation) of the tubular part of the ascending aorta.
Comment: Aneurysm is considered a severe form of dilatation.
Synonym: Aneurysm of the ascending tubular aorta
Bulging of wall of large artery located above heart

Name: Pulmonary artery hypoplasia
Def: Underdevelopment of the pulmonary artery.

Name: Elevated mean arterial pressure
Def: An abnormal increase in the average blood pressure in an individual during a single cardiac cycle.

Name: Coarctation of abdominal aorta
Def: Coarctation of the aorta is a narrowing or constriction of a segment of the abdominal aorta.

Name: Erlenmeyer flask deformity of the femurs
Def: Flaring of distal femur.
Synonym: Erlenmeyer flask deformity of distal femur

Name: Bilateral radial aplasia
Def: Missing radius bone on both sides associated with congenital failure of development.

Name: Metaphyseal sclerosis
Def: Abnormally increased density of metaphyseal bone.
Synonym: Increased bone density in wide portion of long bone

Name: Metaphyseal rarefaction
Def: Reduction in density of metaphyseal bony tissue.

Name: Mesomelic leg shortening
Def: Shortening of the middle parts of the leg in relation to the upper and terminal segments.

Name: Rhizomelic arm shortening
Def: Disproportionate shortening of the proximal segment of the arm (i.e. the humerus).

Name: Slender long bones with narrow diaphyses
Def: Reduced diameter of a long bone with a more pronounced reduction of the diameter of the diaphysis of the long bones.
Synonym: Slender long bones with narrow shaft

Name: Multicentric ossification of proximal humeral epiphyses
Recurrent patellar dislocation
Def: Patellar dislocation occurring repeated times.

Name: Aplasia/Hypoplasia of the capital femoral epiphysis
Def: Absence or underdevelopment of the proximal epiphysis of the femur.
Synonym: Absent/small end part of innermost thighbone
Absent/underdeveloped end part of innermost thighbone

Name: Flattened proximal radial epiphyses
Def: An abnormally flat form of the proximal epiphysis of the radius.

Name: Femoral bowing present at birth, straightening with time
Def: Congenital onset bending or abnormal curvature of the femur that normalizes with age.
Comment: This feature can be diagnosed based on the medical history of congenital femoral bowing with spontaneous improvement.
Synonym: Bowing of thighbone at birth, straightening with time

Name: Dumbbell-shaped humerus
Def: The humerus is shortened and displays flaring (widening) of the metaphyses.
Synonym: Dumbbell-shaped long bone in upper arm

Name: Osteomyelitis leading to amputation due to slow healing fractures
Mesomelic arm shortening
Def: Shortening of the middle parts of the arm in relation to the upper and terminal segments.

Name: Dysplastic distal radial epiphyses
Def: Abnormally developed (dysplastic) distal epiphysis of the radius.

Name: Diaphyseal thickening
Synonym: Thickening of shaft or central part of long bones

Name: Hypoplastic distal humeri
Def: Underdevelopment of the distal portion of the humerus.

Name: Widened proximal tibial metaphyses
Synonym: Wide innermost wide portion of shankbone bone
Wide innermost wide portion of shinbone bone

Name: Distal ulnar hypoplasia
Def: Underdevelopment of the distal portion of the ulna.

Name: Shortening of all phalanges of the toes
Def: Developmental hypoplasia (shortening) of all phalanges of the foot.

Name: Unilateral ulnar hypoplasia
Def: Underdevelopment of the ulna on only one side.

Name: Proximal radio-ulnar synostosis
Def: An abnormal osseous union (fusion) between the proximal portions of the radius and the ulna.

Name: Multiple long-bone exostoses
Def: Multiple exostoses originating in long bones.
Synonym: Multiple exostoses of long tubular bones

Name: Irregular capital femoral epiphysis
Def: Irregular surface of the normally relatively smooth capital femoral epiphysis.
Synonym: Irregular end part of innermost thighbone

Name: Proximal humeral metaphyseal irregularity
Def: Irregularity of the normally smooth surface of the metaphysis at the proximal end of the humerus (at the shoulder).

Name: Diaphyseal cortical sclerosis
Def: An elevation in bone density of the cortex of one or more diaphyses. Sclerosis is normally detected on a radiograph as an area of increased opacity.

Name: Anterolateral radial head dislocation
Def: A dislocation of the head of the radius from its socket in the elbow joint in an anterolateral direction.

Name: Metaphyseal spurs
Def: Bony outgrowths that extend laterally from the margin of the metaphysis.

Name: Fragmented, irregular epiphyses
Synonym: Fragmented, irregular end part of bone

Name: Cone-shaped epiphyses fused within their metaphyses
Synonym: Cone-shaped end part of long bone fused within their wide portion of wide bone

Name: Proximal fibular overgrowth
Def: Overgrowth of the proximal part of the fibula.
Synonym: Overgrowth of innermost part of calf bone

Name: Proximal radial head dislocation
Def: A dislocation of the head of the radius from its socket in the elbow joint in an proximal direction.

Name: Hyperextensibility at wrists
Def: The ability of the wrist joints to move beyond their normal range of motion.

Name: Anterior radial head dislocation
Def: A dislocation of the head of the radius from its socket in the elbow joint in an anterior direction.

Name: Limited knee flexion/extension
Def: A limited ability of the knee joint extension and flexion.

Name: Abnormal metaphyseal trabeculation
Def: An abnormality of the pattern of trabecula (small interconnecting rods of bone) in a metaphyseal region of bone.

Name: Lateral femoral bowing
Def: A lateral bending or abnormal curvature of the femur.

Name: Streaky metaphyseal sclerosis
Def: The presence of streaks (bands) of abnormally increased density of metaphyseal bone.
Synonym: Streak increase in bone density in wide portion of wide bone

Name: Absent proximal radial epiphyses
Def: Absence of the proximal radial epiphysis.

Name: Distal femoral bowing
Def: A bending or abnormal curvature of the distal portion of the femur.

Name: Premature birth following premature rupture of fetal membranes
High-frequency hearing impairment
Def: A type of hearing impairment affecting primarily the higher frequencies of sound (3,000 to 6,000 Hz).
Comment: High frequency hearing impairment often involves loss of ability to hear consonants such as s, f, t, and z, even though vowels can be heard normally.

Name: Cochlear degeneration
Def: Deterioration or loss of the tissues of the cochlea.

Name: Calcification of the auricular cartilage
Def: Ossification affecting the external ear cartilage.

Name: Hypoplastic nasal septum
Def: Underdevelopment of the nasal septum.
Synonym: Decreased size of septum of nose

Name: Abnormal nasal morphology
Comment: This is a category for overall abnormal morphology that may be replaced later with more exact descriptions.

Name: Abnormality of the vertebral endplates
Def: Any abnormality of the vertebral end plates, which are the top and bottom portions of the vertebral bodies that interface with the vertebral discs.

Name: Abnormal sacrum morphology
Def: An abnormality of the sacral bone.
Comment: The sacrum is the large, roughly triangular bone at the base of the verterbal column that is formed by fusion of the five sacral vertebrae S1 to S5.

Name: Abnormality of the intervertebral disk
Def: An abnormality of the intervertebral disk.
Comment: Any abnormality of the fibrocartilaginous structures that are located between adjacent vertebral bodies.

Name: Abnormality of the Achilles tendon
Def: An abnormality of the Achilles tendon.

Name: Atrial fibrillation
Def: An atrial arrhythmia characterized by disorganized atrial activity without discrete P waves on the surface EKG, but instead by an undulating baseline or more sharply circumscribed atrial deflections of varying amplitude an frequency ranging from 350 to 600 per minute.
Comment: The ventricular response to atrial fibrillation is irregularly irregular because of the large number of atrial impulses that transit the atrioventricular node, making the ventricle partially refractory to further impulses. Atrial fibrillation can cause a number of manifestations including excessive ventricular response with angina pectoris or hypotension in susceptible individuals, syncope, systemic embolization, fatigue, or anxiety. These features should be coded separately.
Synonym: Quivering upper heart chambers resulting in irregular heartbeat

Name: obsolete Dilatation of the ascending aorta
Abdominal aortic aneurysm
Def: An abnormal localized widening (dilatation) of the abdominal aorta.

Name: Aortic arch aneurysm
Def: An abnormal localized widening (dilatation) of the aortic arch.

Name: obsolete Abnormalities of the peripheral arteries
Supraventricular arrhythmia
Def: A type of arrhythmia that originates above the ventricles, whereby the electrical impulse propagates down the normal His Purkinje system similar to normal sinus rhythm.
Comment: Supraventricular arrhythmia includes atrial arrhythmias (atrial tachycardia, atrial flutter, atrial fibrillation), atrioventricular nodal reentrant tachycardia, junctional ectopic tachycardia, atrioventricular reentrant tachycardia (Wolf-Parkinson-White Syndrome), orthodromic or antidromic. Supraventricular arrhythmia is distinct from ventricular tachycardia, which originates in the ventricles.

Name: Arterial tortuosity
Def: Abnormal tortuous (i.e., twisted) form of arteries.

Name: Elevated diastolic blood pressure
Def: Abnormal increase in diastolic blood pressure.
Comment: Normal diastolic blood pressure is less than 80 mmHg.

Name: Abnormal cardiac atrium morphology
Def: Any structural abnormality of a cardiac atrium.

Name: Posterior scalloping of vertebral bodies
Def: An excessive concavity of the posterior surface of one or more vertebral bodies.
Comment: The posterior vertebral scalloping sign appears on a lateral radiograph of the spine as an exaggeration of the normal concavity of the posterior surface of one or more vertebral bodies. Neurofibromatosis may be associated with marked scalloping of the posterior borders of the vertebral bodies resulting from intraspinal tumors.

Name: Pericardial constriction
Def: Compression of the heart caused by rigid, thickened, or fused pericardial membranes.

Name: Right ventricular dilatation
Def: Enlargement of the chamber of the right ventricle.

Name: Absence of the pulmonary valve
Def: Refers to the specific combination of defects with a severely dysplastic pulmonary valve and massively dilated branch pulmonary arteries.
Comment: The distinctive feature of APVS is the airway obstruction caused by tracheobronchial compression that results from massive dilatation of the main pulmonary artery (PA) and its first- and second-order branches. Consequential tracheomalacia and bronchomalacia determine the timing and severity of respiratory compromise, as well as the morbidity and mortality of these patients.

Name: Abnormal T-wave
Def: An abnormality of the T wave on the electrocardiogram, which mainly represents the repolarization of the ventricles.

Name: Mitral annular calcification
Def: Mitral annular calcification (MAC) results from progressive calcium deposition along and beneath the mitral valve annulus.
Comment: MAC is a common degenerative process involving the fibrous annulus of the mitral valve, and is generally an incidental finding associated with aging. This term applies if MAC occurs at a substantially younger age than usual.

Name: Anomalous origin of right pulmonary artery from ascending aorta
Def: The right pulmonary artery originates from the ascending aorta in the presence of a pulmonary valve and main pulmonary artery.

Name: Ventricular septal hypertrophy
Def: The dividing wall between left and right sides of the heart, thickens and bulges into the left ventricle.

Name: Coronary artery stenosis
Def: Abnormal narrowing of the coronary artery.

Name: Cardiac valve calcification
Def: Abnormal calcification of a cardiac valve.

Name: Pulmonary valve defects
Def: Any defect in the valve connecting the heart and the pulmonary artery.

Name: Abnormal atrioventricular conduction
Def: An impairment of the electrical continuity between the atria and ventricles.

Name: Preductal coarctation of the aorta
Def: Narrowing or constriction of the aorta localized proximal to the ductus arteriosus, i.e., to the preductal region of aortic arch.
Comment: Blood flow to the aorta distal to the coarctation may be dependent on a patent ductus arteriosus, and hence closure of the ductus arteriosus can lead to serious ischemia of the affected tissues.

Name: Histiocytoid cardiomyopathy
Def: A type of cardiomyopathy characterized pathologically by hamartomatous lesions of cardiac Purkinje cells.
Comment: This HPO term intends to refer to the histological changes that characterize histiocytoid cardiomyopthy. The disease entity Histiocytoid cardiomyopathy is a rare arrhythmogenic disorder characterized by incessant ventricular tachycardia, cardiomegaly, and often sudden death by age 2 years.

Name: Ventricular escape rhythm
Def: A ventircular escape rhythm occurs whenever higher-lever pacemakers in AV junction or sinus node fail to control ventricular activation. Escape rate is usually 20-40 bpm, often associated with broad QRS complexes (at least 120 ms).

Name: Hypoplastic left atrium
Def: Underdeveloped, small left heart atrium

Name: Concentric hypertrophic cardiomyopathy
Def: Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy with an symmetrical and concentric pattern of hypertrophy.

Name: Total anomalous pulmonary venous return
Def: Total anomalous pulmonary venous return refers to a congenital malformation in which all four pulmonary veins do not connect normally to the left atrium, but instead drain abnormally to the right atrium.
Comment: Pulmonary veins drain through abnormal connections to the right atrium.

Name: Left ventricular dysfunction
Def: Inability of the left ventricle to perform its normal physiologic function. Failure is either due to an inability to contract the left ventricle or the inability to relax completely and fill with blood during diastole.

Name: Dysplastic pulmonary valve
Def: A congenital malformation of the pulmonary valve characterized by leaflet deformation.

Name: Shortened PR interval
Def: Reduced time for the PR interval (beginning of the P wave to the beginning of the QRS complex). In adults, normal values are 120 to 200 ms long.

Name: Elevated right atrial pressure
Def: An abnormal increase in magnitude of the pressure in the right atrium.
Comment: Elevated mean right atrial pressure (RAP) can be measured by cardiac catheterization.

Name: Complete heart block with broad QRS complexes
Def: A type of third degree heart block in which the escape rhythm arises at a relatively low part of the conduction system (below the atrioventricular node), which produces a wide QRS complex.

Name: Left posterior fascicular block
Def: Conduction block in the posterior division of the left bundle branch of the bundle of His.

Name: Membranous subvalvular aortic stenosis
Def: Subvalvular stenosis is caused by a diaphragm-like membrane. The stenosis is clinically manifested like any other form of aortic stenosis but is often associated with some aortic insufficiency.
Comment: An important feature in the differential diagnosis between valvular and subvalvular aortic stenosis is the fact that no ejection sound is present in the latter.

Name: Dysplastic aortic valve
Def: A congenital malformation of the aortic valve characterized by leaflet deformation.

Name: Premature arteriosclerosis
Def: Arteriosclerosis occurring at an age that is younger than usual.

Name: Complete heart block with narrow QRS complexes
Def: A type of third degree heart block in which the escape rhythm arises at the atrioventricular node, which produces a narrow QRS complex.

Name: Tricuspid regurgitation
Def: Failure of the tricuspid valve to close sufficiently upon contraction of the right ventricle, causing blood to regurgitate (flow backward) into the right atrium.
Comment: This term should not be applied to Ebstein's anomaly of the tricuspid valve (see HP:0010316).

Name: Premature coronary artery atherosclerosis
Def: Reduction of the diameter of the coronary arteries as the result of an accumulation of atheromatous plaques within the walls of the coronary arteries before age of 45.

Name: Bicuspid pulmonary valve
Def: The presence of a bicuspid pulmonary valve.
Comment: The pulmonary valve normally has three cusps (flaps), that is, it is normally tricuspid.

Name: Pericardial lymphangiectasia
Def: An abnormal dilatation of lymph vessels in the pericardium.

Name: Prolonged QTc interval
Def: A longer than normal interval (corrected for heart rate) between the Q and T waves in the heart's cycle. Prolonged QTc can cause premature action potentials during late phase depolarizations thereby leading to ventricular arrhythmias and ventricular fibrillations.

Name: Global systolic dysfunction
Def: A reduced ejection fraction and an enlarged left ventricle chamber, the latter by an increased resistance to filling with increased filling pressures. Systolic dysfunction is clinically associated with left ventricular failure in the presence of marked cardiomegaly.

Name: Flattened metatarsal heads
Def: Abnormally flat shape of the heads of the metatarsal bones.
Comment: The metatarsal heads articulate with the proximal phalanges of the toes.
Synonym: Flattened head of long bone of foot

Name: Generalized morning stiffness
Def: A sensation of stiffness in the joints that occurs following waking up in the morning.

Name: Stiff interphalangeal joints
Def: Interphalangeal joint stiffness is a perceived sensation of tightness in the interphalangeal joints when attempting to move them after a period of inactivity.

Name: Aplasia of the abdominal wall musculature
Def: Absence of the abdominal musculature.

Name: Helicobacter pylori infection
Def: A recurrent infection of the GI tract with helicobacter pylori, a gram-negative, microaerophilic bacterium usually found in the stomach.
Comment: The bacterial pathogen Helicobacter pylori has co-evolved with humans and colonizes approximately half of the human population, but only causes overt gastric disease in a subset of infected hosts.

Name: Spontaneous esophageal perforation
Def: The occurrence of the full-thickness tear (perforation) of the wall of the esophagus.
Comment: Esophageal perforation can lead to retained gastric contents, saliva, bile, and other substances entering the mediastinum, resulting in mediastinitis, which in turn may lead to sepsis.

Name: Pancreatic pseudocyst
Def: Cyst-like space not lined by epithelium and contained within the pancreas. Pancreatic pseudocysts are often associated with pancreatitis.

Name: Gastric hypertrophy
Def: Hypertrophy of the stomach.

Name: Secretory diarrhea
Def: Watery voluminous diarrhea resulting from an imbalance between ion and water secretion and absorption.

Name: Intrahepatic bile duct cysts
Def: The presence of cyst of the intrahepatic bile duct.

Name: Hypoplastic colon
Def: Underdevelopment of the colon.

Name: Anal mucosal leukoplakia
Def: Leukoplakia is a precancerous dermatosis of mucous membranes analogous Leukoplakia is basically a chronic inflammatory hypertrophy in which anaplasia and malignant dyskeratosis may develop and subsequently advance to an invasive squamous cell cancer. The clinical diagnosis of primary anal leukoplakia is indicated by single or multiple slightly raised,irregular, marginated, grayish-white keratinized' patches in the anal canal. Tissue biopsy is necessary for confirmation.

Name: Pancreatic calcification
Def: The presence of abnormal calcium deposition lesions in the pancreas.

Name: Intestinal obstruction
Def: Blockage or impairment of the normal flow of the contents of the intestine towards the anal canal.

Name: Frequent Giardia lamblia infestation
Def: Increased susceptibility to Giardia lamblia infection of the intestine, as manifested by a medical history of multiple episodes of Giardia lamblia intestinal infection.

Name: Impaired mastication
Def: An abnormal reduction in the ability to masticate (chew), i.e., in the ability to crush and ground food in preparation for swallowing.
Comment: Chewing and swallowing are interrelated. The act of chewing plays a fundamental role in the process of swallowing food. Mastication prepares food for swallowing by breaking it into small particles. Accordingly, loss of teeth has been associated with swallowing difficulties. Chewing difficulties may be caused by loss of teeth, partial dentures, or by tooth pain. Swallowing difficulties, in contrast, are often characterized by difficulties swallowing liquids, reflux, throat spasms, choking on dry food, or dysphagia.

Name: Anoperineal fistula
Def: The presence of a fistula (abnormal tunnel) between the anal canal and the perineum.

Name: Absence of intrinsic factor
Def: Absence of gastric intrinsic factor, which is normally produced by the parietal cells of the stomach, and is required for the absorption of vitamin B12.
Comment: This feature can be ascertained by immunoassay of gastric juices.
Synonym: Intrinsic factor absent from gastric juice

Name: Bowel diverticulosis
Def: The presence of multiple diverticula of the intestine.

Name: Rectal abscess
Def: A collection of pus in the area of the rectum.

Name: Intestinal edema
Def: Accumulation of cell free, noninflammatony fluid within the wall of the intestinal tract producing uniform thickening of the mucosal folds.
Comment: This finding can be observed upon abdominal radiography. The bowel lumen may be slightly dilated. Secondary to the fluid accumulation, there are anatomic and motor alterations in the intestine which are reflected in the roentgenogram.

Name: Adenomatous colonic polyposis
Def: Presence of multiple adenomatous polyps in the colon.

Name: Biliary tract obstruction
Def: Obstruction affecting the biliary tree.

Name: Chronic gastritis
Def: A chronic form of gastritis.

Name: Pancreatic dysplasia
Def: The presence of developmental dysplasia of the pancreas.
Comment: Dysplasia is defined in MPATH as a distortion or deficiency of the tissue or cellular architecture.

Name: Hypoplasia of the gallbladder
Def: The presence of a hypoplastic gallbladder.

Name: Jejunal atresia
Def: A developmental defect resulting in abnormal closure, or atresia of the tubular structure of the jejunum.

Name: Chronic calcifying pancreatitis
Def: A form of chronic pancreatitis that is characterized by calcification.

Name: Degenerative liver disease
Def: The presence of degenerative changes of the liver.

Name: Total intestinal aganglionosis
Def: A congenital defect characterized by the lack of ganglion cells in the entire intestine, i.e., the aganglionic segment comprises the entire large and small bowel.

Name: Extrahepatic biliary duct atresia
Def: Atresia in the extrahepatic bile duct.

Name: Partial abdominal muscle agenesis
Def: Failure to form of portions of the abdominal musculature.

Name: Gastrointestinal infarctions
Synonym: Death of digestive organ tissue due to poor blood supply

Name: Intestinal hypoplasia
Def: Developmental hypoplasia of the intestine.

Name: Giant hypertrophic gastritis
Def: A type of gastritis characterized by excessive proliferation of the gastric mucosa and diffuse thickening of the gastric mucosal folds.

Name: Hypoplasia of the abdominal wall musculature
Def: Underdevelopment of the abdominal musculature.

Name: Intrahepatic biliary atresia
Def: Atresia in the intrahepatic bile duct.

Name: Absence of pectoralis minor muscle
Def: Aplasia (congenital absence) of the pectoralis minor.

Name: Unilateral absence of pectoralis major muscle
Def: Aplasia (congenital absence) of the pectoralis minor on only one side of the chest.
Synonym: Unilateral aplasia of pectoralis major muscle

Name: Abnormal facility in opposing the shoulders
Joint hemorrhage
Def: Hemorrhage occurring within a joint.

Name: Gastritis
Def: The presence of inflammation of the gastric mucous membrane.

Name: Abnormality of the gallbladder
Def: An abnormality of the gallbladder.

Name: Abnormality of the jejunum
Def: An abnormality of the jejunum, i.e., of the middle section of the small intestine.

Name: Intestinal polyp
Def: A discrete abnormal tissue mass that protrudes into the lumen of the intestine and is attached to the intestinal wall either by a stalk, pedunculus, or a broad base.

Name: Premature delivery because of cervical insufficiency or membrane fragility
Spontaneous abortion
Def: A pregnancy that ends at a stage in which the fetus is incapable of surviving on its own, defined as the spontaneous loss of a fetus before the 20th week of pregnancy.

Name: Prominent nasolabial fold
Def: Exaggerated bulkiness of the crease or fold of skin running from the lateral margin of the nose, where nasal base meets the skin of the face, to a point just lateral to the corner of the mouth (cheilion, or commissure).

Name: Absent nasal septal cartilage
Def: Lack of the cartilage of the nasal septum.
Synonym: Failure of development of nasal septal cartilage

Name: Hypoplastic nasal tip
Synonym: Decreased size of tip of nose

Name: Depressed nasal bridge
Def: Posterior positioning of the nasal root in relation to the overall facial profile for age.
Comment: The adjective "depressed" here does not indicate an active process but a status. A depressed nasal bridge can occur irrespective of the width of the nasal bridge, and the width should be assessed independently. In infancy, the nasal bridge is relatively more posterior than in the older person. The term depressed nasal bridge should only be used when the bridge is more posterior than is typical for age and ethnic background.

Name: Hypoplastic nasal bridge
Synonym: Decreased size of bridge of nose

Name: Abnormality of the nares
Def: Abnormality of the nostril.

Name: Internal carotid artery hypoplasia
Synonym: Decreased size of internal carotid artery

Name: Intimal thickening in the coronary arteries
Arterial dissection
Def: A separation (dissection) of the layers of an artery.

Name: Pseudocoarctation of the aorta
Def: Pseudocoarctation is a congenital anomaly of kinking, or buckling, of the aorta without a pressure gradient across the lesion. It is characterized by elongation and kinking of the aorta at the level of the ligamentum arteriosum.
Comment: Note that the ligamentum arteriosum, which develops from the ductus arteriosus, is attached to the superior surface of the pulmonary artery and the inferior surface of the aortic arch.

Name: Premature occlusive vascular stenosis
Def: Peripheral arterial stenosis with onset before the age of 50 years.

Name: obsolete Atrioventricular canal defect with right ventricle aorta and pulmonary atresia
Persistent left superior vena cava
Def: A rare congenital vascular anomaly that results when the left superior cardinal vein caudal to the innominate vein fails to regress.

Name: Carotid artery tortuosity
Def: Abnormal tortuous (i.e., twisted) form of the carotid arteries.

Name: Aortic arch calcification
Def: Calcification, that is, pathological deposition of calcium salts in the arch of aorta.

Name: Cerebral venous thrombosis
Def: Formation of a blood clot (thrombus) inside a cerebral vein, causing the obstruction of blood flow.

Name: Capillary hemangioma
Def: The presence of a capillary hemangioma, which are hemangiomas with small endothelial spaces.

Name: Large vessel vasculitis
Def: A type of vasculitis (inflammation of blood vessel walls) affecting large arteries such as the aorta and branches of the aorta.

Name: Pulmonary aterial intimal fibrosis
Def: Formation of excess fibrous connective tissue in the tunica intima (innermost layer) of arteries in the pulmonary circulation.
Comment: Some causes of intimal fibrosis are hypertension, intimal fibroplasia, arterial atheroma, and CADASIL syndrome.

Name: Arterial fibromuscular dysplasia
Def: An arterial lesion that is characterized by either intimal fibroplasia, with neointimal lesions of cells and matrix deposition, or medial fibroplasia, in which there is loss of smooth muscle cells and increased deposition of collagen and proteoglycans in the medial layer.
Comment: Fibromuscular dysplasia (FMD) is distinct from atherosclerotic lesions in that FMD lesions do not contain inflammatory cells or lipids. Instead, the pathology of FMD. FMD can result in arterial stenosis or occlusion, and less commonly, arterial dissection or aneurysm formation. FMD can affect almost any artery but most commonly affects the renal arteries, presenting as hypertension, and the carotid and vertebral arteries, leading to ischemic stroke, transient ischemic attacks, headaches, and pulsatile tinnitus.

Name: Anomalous branches of internal carotid artery
Increased pulmonary vascular resistance
Comment: Pulmonary vascular resistance (PVR) more than 3 wood units, as defined by the current definition of pulmonary hypertension. 95% of individuals have a PVR of less than 2.4 wood units.

Name: Cerebral vasculitis
Def: Inflammation of the blood vessels within the brain.

Name: Lack of facial subcutaneous fat
Synonym: Lack of facial fat below the skin

Name: Mandibulofacial dysostosis
Def: A type of craniofacial dysostosis associated with abnormalities of the external ears, mirognathia, macrostomia, coloboma of the lower eyelid, and cleft palate. This is a bundled term that is left in the HPO now for convenience with legacy annotations but should not be used for new annotations.

Name: Hemifacial hypertrophy
Def: Unilateral overgrowth of facial tissues, including muscles, bones and skin.
Synonym: Increase in size of half of face

Name: Disturbance of facial expression
Def: An abnormality of the gestures or movements executed with the facial muscles with which emotions such as fear, joy, sadness, surprise, and disgust can be expressed.

Name: Extension of hair growth on temples to lateral eyebrow
Def: A pattern of hair growth in which there is hair extending from the temples to the lateral eyebrows.
Synonym: Unusual hairline with hair growth on temples extending to lateral eyebrow

Name: Hypoplastic philtrum
Def: Underdevelopment of the philtrum.

Name: Progeroid facial appearance
Def: A degree of wrinkling of the facial skin that is more than expected for the age of the individual, leading to a prematurely aged appearance.

Name: Recurrent mandibular subluxations
Def: Recurrent partial dislocations of the mandible.

Name: Sparse lateral eyebrow
Def: Decreased density/number and/or decreased diameter of lateral eyebrow hairs.
Comment: Abnormal sparseness of the eyebrows laterally.
Synonym: Limited hair on end of eyebrow

Name: Abnormality of complement system
Def: An abnormality of the complement system.
Comment: The complement system represents a family of over 25 serum proteins and cell surface receptors that act in a cascade manner leading to innate functions such as inflammation and enhancement of adaptive immunity. Three general pathways, i.e. classical, lectin and alternative, activate the complement system.

Name: Autonomic bladder dysfunction
Def: Abnormal bladder function (increased urge or frequency of urination or urge incontinence) resulting from abnormal functioning of the autonomic nervous system.

Name: Hypoplasia of the bladder
Def: Underdevelopment of the urinary bladder.

Name: Abnormal carotid artery morphology
Def: Any structural abnormality of the carotid arteries, including the common carotid artery and its' arterial branches.

Name: Abnormal vena cava morphology
Def: An abnormality of the structure of the veins that return deoxygenated blood from the body into the heart, i.e., the superior vena cava and the inferior vena cava.

Name: Inspiratory stridor
Def: Inspiratory stridor is a high pitched sound upon inspiration that is generally related to laryngeal abnormalities.

Name: Hypoplasia of the epiglottis
Def: Hypoplasia of the epiglottis.

Name: Severe T-cell immunodeficiency
Def: A primary immune deficiency that is characterized by defects or deficiencies of T-lymphocytes that causes specific susceptibility to intracellular micro-organisms.
Comment: Several diseases are classified as severe T cell immunodeficiencies: severe combined immunodeficiency syndrome (SCID), reticular dysgenesis, thymic dysplasia (Nezelof syndrome), combined immunodeficiency disease (CID), and Wiskott-Aldrich syndrome (WAS).

Name: Recurrent herpes
Def: Increased susceptibility to herpesvirus, as manifested by recurrent episodes of herpesvirus.

Name: Lack of T cell function
Def: Complete inability of T cells to perform their functions in cell-mediated immunity.

Name: Decreased serum complement factor I
Def: A reduced level of the complement component Factor I in circulation.

Name: Defective B cell differentiation
Def: Reduced functionality of the process in which a precursor cell type acquires the specialized features of a B cell. A B cell is a lymphocyte of B lineage with the phenotype CD19-positive and capable of B cell mediated immunity.

Name: Aplasia of the thymus
Def: Absence of the thymus. This feature may be appreciated by the lack of a thymic shadow upon radiographic examination.

Name: Susceptibility to chickenpox
Def: Increased susceptibility to chicken pox, as manifested by recurrent episodes of chicken pox.

Name: Humoral immunodeficiency
Def: A general term referring to a defect in immunity resulting from impaired antibody production.
Comment: If possible it is preferable to use a precise description of the observed manifestations leading to the inference of humoral immunodeficiency.

Name: Severe B lymphocytopenia
Def: A severe form of B lymphocytopenia in which the count of B cells is very low or absent.

Name: Recurrent streptococcus pneumoniae infections
Def: Increased susceptibility to streptococcus pneumoniae infections as manifested by a history of recurrent infections by streptococcus pneumoniae.

Name: Abnormality of humoral immunity
Def: An abnormality of the humoral immune system, which comprises antibodies produced by B cells as well as the complement system.

Name: Decreased serum complement factor H
Def: A reduced level of the complement component Factor H in circulation.

Name: Abnormality of B cell physiology
Def: An abnormality of the physiological functioning of B cells.
Comment: This term refers to any abnormality of the B cells, which play a role in the humoral immune response. The main functions of B cells are to produce antibodies, to perform the role of antigen presenting cells, and to develop into memory cells.

Name: Cellular immunodeficiency
Def: An immunodeficiency characterized by defective cell-mediated immunity or humoral immunity.

Name: Recurrent Haemophilus influenzae infections
Def: Increased susceptibility to Haemophilus influenzae infections as manifested by recurrent episodes of infection by Haemophilus influenzae.

Name: Recurrent meningococcal disease
Def: Recurrent infections by Neisseria meningitidis (one of the most common causes of bacterial meningitis), which is also known as meningococcus.
Synonym: Increased susceptibility to neisseria meningitidis infections

Name: Defective B cell activation
Def: A reduced ability of a B cell to become activated, i.e., the change in morphology and behavior of

Name: Recurrent protozoan infections
Def: Increased susceptibility to protozoan infections, as manifested by recurrent episodes of protozoan infection.

Name: Combined immunodeficiency
Def: A group of phenotypically heterogeneous genetic disorders characterized by profound deficiencies of T- and B-cell function, which predispose the patients to both infectious and noninfectious complications.

Name: Depletion of components of the alternative complement pathway
Def: An abnormal reduction in the components of the alternative complement pathway, such as the C3 protein or its cleavage products.

Name: Recurrent opportunistic infections
Def: Increased susceptibility to opportunistic infections, as manifested by recurrent episodes of infection by opportunistic agents, i.e., by microorganisms that do not usually cause disease in a healthy host, but are able to infect a host with a compromised immune system.

Name: Susceptibility to coronavirus 229e
Def: Increased susceptibility to coronavirus 229e, as manifested by recurrent episodes of coronavirus 229e.

Name: Reduction of neutrophil motility
Def: An abnormal reduction of the cell motility of neutrophils.

Name: Recurrent candida infections
Def: An increased susceptibility to candida infections, as manifested by a history of recurrent episodes of candida infections.

Name: Decrease in T cell count
Def: An abnormally low count of T cells.
Synonym: Decreased numbers of circulating T cells

Name: Increased B cell count
Def: An abnormal increase from the normal count of B cells.

Name: Recurrent bacterial skin infections
Def: Increased susceptibility to bacterial infections of the skin, as manifested by recurrent episodes of infectious dermatitis.
Comment: Infectious dermatitis may manifest as impetigo, multiple purulent blisters, erythema, lymphadenopathy near the site of infection.

Name: Decreased proportion of CD4-positive T cells
Def: A decreased proportion of circulating CD4-positive helper T cells relative to total T cell count.

Name: obsolete Markedly reduced T cell function
Chronic intestinal candidiasis
Def: Persistent overgrowth of Candida albicans in the gastrointestinal tract.

Name: Increased alpha-globulin
Def: An abnormally increased level of circulationg alpha-globulin. Alpha globulins are a group of serum proteins defined by their mobility on serum electrophoresis. The alpha1-protein fraction is comprised of alpha1-antitrypsin, thyroid-binding globulin, and transcortin. Ceruloplasmin, alpha2-macroglobulin, and haptoglobin contribute to the alpha2-protein band. The alpha2 component is increased as an acute-phase reactant.

Name: Decreased proportion of CD8-positive T cells
Def: A decreased proportion of circulating CD8-positive, alpha-beta T cells relative to total number of T cells.
Synonym: Decreased proportion of CD8+ T cells

Name: Decreased serum complement factor B
Def: A reduced level of the complement component factor B in circulation.

Name: Decreased T cell activation
Def: Decreased or impaired activation of T cells in response to a mitogen, cytokine, chemokine, cellular ligand, or an antigen for which it is specific.

Name: Recurrent gram-negative bacterial infections
Def: Increased susceptibility to infection by gram-negative bacteria, as manifested by a medical history of repeated or frequent infections by these agents.
Comment: Gram-negative bacteria have a unique outer membrane, a thinner layer of peptidoglycan compared to gram-positive bacteria, and a periplasmic space between the cell wall and the membrane.

Name: Decreased serum complement C3
Def: A reduced level of the complement component C3 in circulation.

Name: Absence of CD8-positive T cells
Def: Lack of detectible CD8-positive T cells

Name: Dysfunctional alternative complement pathway
Def: An abnormality of the functioning of any aspect of the alternative complement pathway.

Name: Absent specific antibody response
Def: Absence of specific immunoglobulins directed against a specific antigen or microorganism.

Name: Recurrent sinopulmonary infections
Def: An increased susceptibility to infections involving both the paranasal sinuses and the lungs, as manifested by a history of recurrent sinopulmonary infections.

Name: Recurrent systemic pyogenic infections
Def: Increased susceptibility to systemic pyogenic infections, as manifested by recurrent episodes of systemic pyogenic infections.

Name: Recurrent Neisserial infections
Def: Recurrent infections by bacteria of the genus Neisseria, including N. meningitidis (one of the most common causes of bacterial meningitis).

Name: Transient hypogammaglobulinemia of infancy
Def: At birth, newborns are endowed with maternal antibodies. IgG production normally begins at the age of two months. A delay in recovery from this physiological hypogammaglobulinemia between the 3rd and the 6th month of life, and of recovery period between 18 and 36 months defines transient newborn hypogammaglobulinemia.

Name: Impaired T cell function
Def: Abnormally reduced ability of T cells to perform their functions in cell-mediated immunity.

Name: Recurrent infections in infancy and early childhood
Def: Recurrent infections at an early age with improvement in later childhood.

Name: Maxillozygomatic hypoplasia
Def: Hypoplasia of the maxillozygomatic complex.
Synonym: Decreased projection of zygomaticomaxillary bone complex
Decreased size of zygomaticomaxillary bone complex

Name: Sclerotic cranial sutures
Def: An increased density in the cranial sutures following obliteration.

Name: Widely patent coronal suture
Def: The presence of a coronal suture (the cranial suture that separates the frontal and parietal bones) that is not ossified but rather wide open at an age when it is normally closed.

Name: Obtuse angle of mandible
Def: Abnormally flat (obtuse) angle of the mandible. The angle of the mandibular, located at the junction between the body and the ramus of the mandible, is normally close to being a right angle. This terms describes an abnormal increase of this angle such that the mandible appears flatter than normal.
Comment: See PMID:17213440 Figure 1G for an example of an obtuse mandibular angle.

Name: Calvarial osteosclerosis
Def: An increase in bone density affecting the calvaria (roof of the skull).

Name: Absent/hypoplastic paranasal sinuses
Def: Aplasia or hypoplasia of the paranasal sinuses.

Name: Absent ethmoidal sinuses
Def: Lack (aplasia) of the ethmoidal sinus.
Synonym: Failure of development of ethmoid sinuses

Name: Premature closure of fontanelles
Def: Normally, the posterior and lateral fontanelles are obliterated by about six months after birth, the anterior fontanelle closes by about the middle of the second year. This term refers to the situation in which the fontanelles close at an inappropriately early time point.
Synonym: Early closure of the bregma sutures
Early closure of the cranial sutures
Premature closure of the bregma sutures
Premature closure of the cranial sutures

Name: Calcification of falx cerebri
Def: The presence of calcium deposition in the falx cerebri.

Name: Craniofacial osteosclerosis
Def: Abnormally increased density of craniofacial bone tissue.

Name: Facial hyperostosis
Def: Excessive growth (overgrowth) of the facial bones, that is of the facial skeleton.
Synonym: Increase in size of the facial bones

Name: Hypoplasia of the frontal bone
Def: Underdevelopment of the frontal bone.
Synonym: Decreased size of bone of forehead

Name: Flat occiput
Def: Reduced convexity of the occiput (posterior part of skull).
Comment: Reduced convexity of the occiput gives an appearance of flattening. There are no objective measures for convexity of the occiput, and evaluation depends heavily on the experience of the observer. This finding may or may not be accompanied by Brachycephaly (which should be coded separately), and may be observed more frequently when an infant is placed to sleep on his/her back. Occipital plagiocephaly can result from fusion or sclerosis of the lambdoid suture. If unilateral, this is accompanied by unilateral occipital flattening and bulging of the ispilateral frontal bone.

Name: Fusion of middle ear ossicles
Def: Bony fusion of malleus, incus, and stapes.

Name: Decreased calvarial ossification
Def: Abnormal reduction in ossification of the calvaria (roof of the skull consisting of the frontal bone, parietal bones, temporal bones, and occipital bone).

Name: Widely patent sagittal suture
Def: The presence of a sagittal suture (the cranial suture that separates the left and right parietal bones) that is not ossified but rather wide open at an age when it is normally closed.

Name: Progressive sclerosis of skull base
Def: Progressively increasing bone density of the skull base without significant changes in bony contour.

Name: Decreased circulating total IgE
Def: An abnormally decreased level of immunoglobulin E (IgE) in blood.

Name: Abnormality of the alternative complement pathway
Def: A deviation in any aspect of the alternative complement pathway.
Comment: The alternative complement pathway is one of three complement pathways, which is an innate component of the immune system's natural defense against infections. The alternative complement pathway has three unique components, factor B, factor D, and properdin. {xref="PMID:16424154"}

Name: Abnormal epiglottis morphology
Def: An abnormality of the epiglottis.

Name: Postnatal microcephaly
Def: Head circumference which falls below 2 standard deviations below the mean for age and gender because of insufficient head growth after birth.
Synonym: Development of small head that was not present at birth

Name: Small fontanelle
Def: A fontanelle that is small for age.

Name: Prominent metopic ridge
Def: Vertical bony ridge positioned in the midline of the forehead.
Comment: The ridge may extend from the hairline to the glabella or may be partial. The frontal suture of the skull is a dense connective tissue structure that divides the two halves of the frontal bone of the skull in infants and children and usually undergoes closure by the age of six years. A persistent frontal suture is known as a metopic suture or sutura frontalis persistens. This can lead to a ridged appearance of the forehead.

Name: Postnatal macrocephaly
Def: The postnatal development of an abnormally large skull (macrocephaly).

Name: Metopic suture patent to nasal root
Def: The frontal suture divides the two halves of the frontal bone in infants and usually fuses by the age of six years. The suture runs from the bregma (the point on the skull at which the coronal suture is intersected perpendicularly by the sagittal suture) to the nasion or nasal root. This term applies if the suture is widely patent from bregma to nasal root.
Comment: This feature is a characteristic of Schinzel-Giedion midface retraction syndrome.

Name: Midline skin dimples over anterior/posterior fontanelles
Chronic myelogenous leukemia
Def: A myeloproliferative disorder characterized by increased proliferation of the granulocytic cell line without the loss of their capacity to differentiate.

Name: Hemoglobin Barts
Def: Normal adult hemoglobin is composed of two chains each of alpha and beta globin. Hb Barts (Hemoglobin Barts) is a tetramer with four gamma globin chains, and is essentially pathognomonic for one or another form of alpha thalassemia. Hb Barts has an extremely high affinity for oxygen, resulting in almost no oxygen delivery to the tissues.
Comment: Hb Bart is normally not present in adult blood. It makes up about 85-90 percent of hemoglobin in Hb Bart hydrops fetalis syndrome, and about 2-5 percent in HbH disease.

Name: Monoclonal immunoglobulin M proteinemia
Def: Presence of a monoclonal immunoglobulin M protein in the serum.
Comment: This is a characteristic feature of Waldenstrom macroglobulinemia (WM), which is defined as a B-cell lymphoplasmacytic lymphoma, characterized by monoclonal immunoglobulin M protein in the serum and infiltration of bone marrow with lymphoplasmacytic cells.

Name: Transient erythroblastopenia
Def: A transient reduction in the number of erythroblasts in the circulation.
Comment: An erythroblast, the immediate precursor of a normal erythrocyte which, still retains a cell nucleus.
Synonym: Transient decrease in blood erythrocyte number

Name: Heinz body anemia
Def: Anemia characterized by abnormal intracellular inclusions, composed of denatured hemoglobin, found on the membrane of red blood cells.

Name: Impaired neutrophil killing of staphylococci
Def: A reduction in the ability of neutrophils to kill the gram-positive bacteria, staphylococcus, which is commonly known as staph.

Name: Increased megakaryocyte count
Def: Increased megakaryocyte number, i.e., of platelet precursor cells, present in the bone marrow.

Name: T-cell lymphoma/leukemia
Def: A type of T-cell lymphoma in which cancerous T-cells may present in the blood (leukemia), lymph nodes (lymphoma), skin or in multiple areas.
Comment: T-cell lymphoma/leukemia is linked to infection by the human T-cell lymphotropic virus 1 (HTLV-1).

Name: Increased mean corpuscular volume
Def: Larger than normal size of erythrocytes.
Comment: Macrocytosis refers to a mean cell volume (MCV) greater than 100 fL. If macrocytosis is an isolated abnormality, the amount of hemoglobin in the cell increases proportionately, so the mean cell hemoglobin concentration (MCHC) remains within normal limits.

Name: Chronic disseminated intravascular coagulation
Def: A chronic form of disseminated intravascular coagulation in which a persistent weak or intermittent activating stimulus is present and destruction and production of coagulation factors and platelets are balanced.

Name: Disseminated intravascular coagulation
Def: Disseminated intravascular coagulation is characterized by the widespread activation of coagulation, which results in the intravascular formation of fibrin and ultimately thrombotic occlusion of small and midsize vessels.
Comment: DIC is a complex syndrome in which there is pathological generation of thrombin and diffuse intravascular clot formation. DIC may occur as acute decompensated or chronic compensated form. In acute decompensated DIC, there is a sudden massive exposure of tissue factor over a brief time period; Intravascular coagulation can also compromise the blood supply to organs and, in conjunction with hemodynamic and metabolic derangements, may contribute to the failure of multiple organs. At the same time, the use and subsequent depletion of platelets and coagulation proteins resulting from the ongoing coagulation may induce severe bleeding. Chronic DIC, also known as compensated DIC, results from a persistent weak or intermittent activating stimulus. Under such conditions, destruction and production of coagulation factors and platelets are balanced.

Name: Pyridoxine-responsive sideroblastic anemia
Def: A type of sideroblastic anemia that is alleviated by pyridoxine (vitamin B-6) treatment.

Name: Lymphoid leukemia
Def: A malignant lymphocytic neoplasm of B-cell or T-cell lineage involving primarily the bone marrow and the peripheral blood. This category includes precursor or acute lymphoblastic leukemias and chronic leukemias.

Name: Reduced kininogen activity
Def: Reduction in the amount of kininogen, which functions as a cofactor in the contact phase of the intrinsic blood coagulation cascade.
Comment: Kininogen is cleaved into the following 6 chains: 1) Kininogen-1 heavy chain; 2) T-kinin; 3) Bradykinin; 4) Lysyl-bradykinin; 5) Kininogen-1 light chain; and 6) Low molecular weight growth-promoting factor.

Name: Bone marrow hypocellularity
Def: A reduced number of hematopoietic cells present in the bone marrow relative to marrow fat.

Name: Biphenotypic acute leukaemia
Def: A type of actue leukemia with features characteristic of both the myeloid and lymphoid lineages. These leukemias are for this reason are designated mixed-lineage, hybrid or biphenotypic acute leukemias.

Name: Transient myeloproliferative syndrome
Def: A unique clonal neoplastic disorder that is linked to trisomy 21, is restricted to neonatal period, and spontaneously regresses. It often has characteristics of megakaryocytic lineage and is associated with GATA1 mutations in myeloblasts.

Name: Exercise-induced hemolysis
Def: A form of hemolytic anemia that can be triggered by exertion.

Name: Decreased mean platelet volume
Def: Average platelet volume below the lower limit of the normal reference interval.
Comment: Mean platelet volume (MPV) is a measure of the average size of platelets, with a typical reference range of 7.5 to 11.5 femtoliters (fL).

Name: T cell chronic lymphocytic lymphoma/leukemia
Def: A form of lymphoid leukemia or lymphoma in which too many T-cell lymphoblasts are found in the blood, bone marrow, and tissues. Leukemia or lymphoma classification depends on which feature is more prominent.

Name: Red blood cell keratocytosis
Def: A form of poikilocytosis in which the abnormally shaped erythrocytes have notches that results in projections that look like horns.
Comment: Kerato- is derived from the Greek word for horn.
Synonym: Distorted red blood cells resembling keratocytes

Name: Congenital agranulocytosis
Def: Congenital onset of a marked decrease in the number of granulocytes.

Name: Prolonged whole-blood clotting time
Def: An abnormal prolongation (delay) in the time required by whole blood to produce a visible clot.

Name: Reduced protein C activity
Def: An abnormality of coagulation related to a decreased concentration of vitamin K-dependent protein C. Protein C is activated to protein Ca by thrombin bound to thrombomodulin. Activated protein C degrades factors VIIIa and Va.
Comment: Protein C can function as an anticoagulant by irreversibly proteolytically inactivating Factor Va and Factor VIIIa. Therefore, a defect in protein C is associated with an increased risk of thrombosis.

Name: Myeloproliferative disorder
Def: Proliferation (excess production) of hemopoietically active tissue or of tissue which has embryonic hemopoietic potential.
Comment: There are four main myeloproliferative disroders, 1) chronic myelogenous leukemia (CML); 2) Polycythemia vera; 3) Essential thrombocytosis; and 4) Myelofibrosis.

Name: Megakaryocytopenia
Def: A reduced count of megakaryocytes.
Comment: Megakaryocytes are giant cells in the bone marrow. Mature blood platelets are released from the cytoplasm of megakaryocytes.

Name: obsolete Congenital neutropenia
Def: A form of neutropenia with congenital onset.
Comment: This term was obsoleted - for annotation of congenital neutropenia, please use the class HP_0001875 Neutropenia and the Modifier Congenital Onset.
Synonym: Low blood neutrophil level since birth

Name: Chronic lymphatic leukemia
Def: A chronic lymphocytic/lymphatic/lymphoblastic leukemia (CLL) is a neoplastic disease characterized by proliferation and accumulation (blood, marrow and lymphoid organs) of morphologically mature but immunologically dysfunctional lymphocytes. A CLL is always a B-cell lymphocytic leukemia as there are no reports of cases of T-cell lymphocytic leukemias.

Name: Abnormality of the metopic suture
Def: The frontal suture divides the two halves of the frontal bone of the skull in infants and children and generally undergoes fusion by the age of six. A persistent frontal suture is referred to as a \

Name: Abnormality of the zygomatic arch
Def: An abnormality of the zygomatic arch, also known as the cheek bone.
Comment: The zygomatic arch is formed by the zygomatic process of temporal bone and the temporal process of the zygomatic bone.

Name: Chronic leukemia
Def: A slowly progressing leukemia characterized by a clonal (malignant) proliferation of maturing and mature myeloid cells or mature lymphocytes. When the clonal cellular population is composed of myeloid cells, the process is called chronic myelogenous leukemia. When the clonal cellular population is composed of lymphocytes, it is classified as chronic lymphocytic leukemia, hairy cell leukemia, or T-cell large granular lymphocyte leukemia.

Name: Imbalanced hemoglobin synthesis
Def: Normal hemoglobin synthesis is characterized by production of equal amounts of alpha and beta globins. This term refers to a deviation from this pattern and is the main characteristic of the various forms of thalassemia.
Comment: While imbalanced hemoglobin synthesis can be inferred from other findings including those of hemoglobin electrophoresis, the determination of this feature requires investigation of hemoglobin synthesis in vitro, e.g., by incubation of washed peripheral blood erythrocytes and bone marrow cells with radioactively labeled leucine followed by column chromatography.

Name: Abnormality of bone marrow cell morphology
Def: An anomaly of the form or number of cells in the bone marrow.
Synonym: Anomaly of the bone marrow cells

Name: Multiple renal cysts
Def: The presence of many cysts in the kidney.

Name: Decreased numbers of nephrons
Def: A reduction in the count of nephrons per kidney.

Name: Absence of renal corticomedullary differentiation
Def: A lack of differentiation between renal cortex and medulla on diagnostic imaging.

Name: Reduced renal corticomedullary differentiation
Def: Reduced differentiation between renal cortex and medulla on diagnostic imaging.
Synonym: Loss of definition of corticomedullary differentiation

Name: Renal magnesium wasting
Def: High urine magnesium in the presence of hypomagnesemia.

Name: Increased renal tubular phosphate reabsorption
Synonym: Increased percent tubular reabsorption of phosphorus

Name: Non-acidotic proximal tubulopathy
Def: A type of proximal renal tubulopathy characterized by resorption defects leading to glycosuria, aminoaciduria, tubular proteinuria, renal hypophosphatemia, and urate tubular hyporeabsorption without bicarbonate loss.

Name: Tubulointerstitial fibrosis
Def: A progressive detrimental connective tissue deposition (fibrosis) on the kidney parenchyma involving the tubules and interstitial tissue of the kidney.
Comment: This finding is usually shown by renal biopsy. Fibrosis involves an excess accumulation of extracellular matrix and usually results in loss of function when normal tissue is replaced with scar tissue. Tubulointerstitial renal fibrosis, characterized as a progressive detrimental connective tissue deposition on the kidney parenchyma, appears to be a harmful process leading inevitably to renal function deterioration, independently of the primary renal disease which causes the original kidney injury. Epithelial to Mesenchymal Transition (EMT) of tubular epithelial cells which are transformed to mesenchymal fibroblasts migrating to adjacent interstitial parenchyma constitutes the principal mechanism of renal fibrosis along with local and circulating cells. (PMID:20011086)

Name: Impaired reabsorption of chloride
Def: Any impairment of reabsorption of chloride by the kidney in order to not lose too much chloride in the urine.

Name: Duplication of renal pelvis
Def: A duplication of the renal pelvis.

Name: Tubular basement membrane disintegration
Def: DIsruption and breaking up of the basement membrane of the tubules of the kidney.
Comment: Throughout the rest of the nephron, tubule epithelial cells are attached to the tubular basement membrane that overlies the subjacent interstitial connective tissue. The disruption of cell-basement membrane adhesion results in loss of cell orientation, abnormal cell function, and can lead to tissue destruction.
Synonym: Disintegration of the tubular basement membrane

Name: Renal cell carcinoma
Def: A type of carcinoma of the kidney with origin in the epithelium of the proximal convoluted renal tubule.
Comment: Renal cell carcinoma (also known as hypernephroma) is the most common form of kidney cancer arising from the proximal renal tubule. The tissue of origin for renal cell carcinoma is the proximal renal tubular epithelium. Renal cell carcinoma can be classified as 1) clear cell carcinoma, 2) papillary carcinoma, 3) chromophobe renal carcinoma, and 4) collecting duct carcinoma.
Synonym: Cancer starting in small tubes in kidneys

Name: Patchy palmoplantar keratoderma
Def: A focal type of palmoplantar keratoderma in which only certain areas of the palms and soles are affected.
Comment: Patchy palmoplantar keratoderma may develop at sites of recurrent friction.

Name: Giant melanosomes in melanocytes
Def: The presence of large spherical melanosomes (1 to 6 micrometer in diameter) in the cytoplasm of melanocytes.
Comment: Giant melanosomes can be seen in cafe-au-lait spots and other melanocytic disorders. Giant melanosome and giant melanosome are synonymous. Macromelanosomes can be detected by electron microscopy of the skin.

Name: Macular hypopigmented whorls, streaks, and patches
Congenital alopecia totalis
Def: Loss of all scalp hair with congenital onset.

Name: Facial telangiectasia in butterfly midface distribution
Def: Telangiectases (small dilated blood vessels) located near the surface of the skin in a butterfly midface distribution.

Name: Congenital giant melanocytic nevus
Def: The giant congenital nevus is greater than 8 cm in size, pigmented and often hairy. A giant congenital nevus is smaller in infants and children, but it usually continues to grow with the child.
Comment: Between 4% and 6% of these lesions will develop into a malignant melanoma.

Name: Large cafe-au-lait macules with irregular margins
Def: Large hypermelanotic macules with jagged borders.
Comment: This type of lesionk is observed in McCune Albright syndrome. The cafe-au-lait macules are larger than those seen in neurofibromatosis, and have more irregular borders. The borders of these macules have been compared to the coast of Maine, whereas the cafe-au-lait spots in neurofibromatosis type 1 have been compared to the coast of California.

Name: Bilobate gallbladder
Def: The presence of a bilobed gallbladder, related to a duplication of the gallbladder primordium.
Comment: During the fifth or early sixth embryonic week, occasionally, the gallbladder primordium bifurcates and results in duplication of gallbladder. Duplication results from a split primordium whilst a true accessory gallbladder results from an extra primordium. There are no specific symptoms or signs associated with multiple gallbladders.

Name: Aplasia/hypoplasia of the femur
Def: Absence or underdevelopment of the femur.

Name: Accelerated skeletal maturation
Def: An abnormally increased rate of skeletal maturation. Accelerated skeletal maturation can be diagnosed on the basis of an estimation of the bone age from radiographs of specific bones in the human body.

Name: Thoracolumbar kyphosis
Def: Hyperconvexity of the thoracolumbar spine producing a rounded or humped appearance.

Name: Hypermobility of interphalangeal joints
Def: The ability of the interphalangeal joints to move beyond their normal range of motion.

Name: Broad long bones
Def: Increased cross-section (diameter) of the long bones. Note that widening may primarily affect specific regions of long bones (e.g., diaphysis or metaphysis), but this should be coded separately.

Name: Absent ossification of calvaria
Def: Absent ossification of the calvaria (vault of the skull).

Name: Osteoporosis of vertebrae
Def: Osteoporosis affecting predominantly the vertebrae.

Name: Posterior fusion of lumbosacral vertebrae
Def: Bony fusion of the posterior part of the L5 vertebral body with the sacrum.

Name: Type D brachydactyly
Def: This type of brachydactyly is characterized by short and broad terminal phalanges of the thumbs and big toes.

Name: Decreased anterioposterior diameter of lumbar vertebral bodies
Hyperextensible hand joints
Def: The ability of the joints of the hand to move beyond their normal range of motion.

Name: Short 3rd toe
Def: Underdevelopment (hypoplasia) of the third toe.

Name: Intervertebral disk calcification
Def: The presence of abnormal calcium deposition of the intervertebral disk.

Name: Bilateral ulnar hypoplasia
Def: Underdevelopment of the ulna on both sides.
Comment: May be a symmetric finding.

Name: Cutaneous syndactyly between fingers 2 and 5
Def: A soft tissue continuity in the anteroposterior axis between the second to the fifth fingers that extends distally to at least the level of the proximal interphalangeal joints.

Name: Cortical sclerosis
Def: Sclerosis (abnormal hardening) of cortical bone, characterized by increased radiodensity.

Name: Moderate generalized osteoporosis
Def: Moderate osteoporosis.

Name: Multiple digital exostoses
Def: Multiple exostoses originating in the fingers and toes.
Comment: This feature is characteristic of metachondromatosis (MIM:156250).

Name: Positional foot deformity
Def: A foot deformity resulting due to an abnormality affecting the muscle and soft tissue. In contrast if the bones of the foot are affected the term structural foot deformity applies.

Name: Salmonella osteomyelitis
Def: Osteomyelitis caused by infection with the bacteria, salmonella.

Name: Massively thickened long bone cortices
Def: Extreme thickening of the cortex of long bones.

Name: Os odontoideum
Def: Separation of the odontoid process from the body of the axis.
Comment: With os odontoideum, the caudal fragment of the odontoid process may provide deficient stability for the atlantoaxial joint and lead to subsequent instability or dislocation and neurological deficits.

Name: Bilateral intracranial calcifications
Def: Deposition of calcium salts on both sides of the brain.

Name: Dupuytren contracture
Def: An abnormality of the hand resulting from contracture of the palmar fascia with a fixed flexion deformity of the metacarpophalangeal (MCP) joints and the proximal interphalangeal (PIP) joints.
Comment: A Dupuytren contracture usually affects the fourth and fifth digits (the ring and small fingers). Affected persons are not able to extend the 4th and 5th fingers.

Name: Tongue-like lumbar vertebral deformities
Def: A tongue-like protusion from the anterior aspect of lumbar vertebral bodies.

Name: Distal arthrogryposis
Def: A form of arthrogryposis primarily affecting the hands and the feet.

Name: Patchy osteosclerosis
Def: Patchy (irregular) increase in bone density. This can take on many forms depending on severity and distribution as can be seen on x-rays.
Synonym: Patchy increase of bone mineral density

Name: Deformed humeral heads
Synonym: Deformed head of long bone in upper arm

Name: Dysplastic distal thumb phalanges with a central hole
Joint hyperflexibility
Def: Increased mobility and flexibility in the joint due to the tension in tissues such as ligaments and muscles.
Synonym: Joints move beyond expected range of motion

Name: Partial fusion of proximal row of carpal bones
Synonym: Partial fusion of innermost row of wrist bones

Name: Postaxial polydactyly type A
Def: Supernumerary digits located at the ulnar side of the hand with a complete extra finger and extra metacarpal.

Name: Increased bone density with cystic changes
Bilateral triphalangeal thumbs
Def: A bilateral form of triphalangeal thumb.

Name: Flattened knee epiphyses
Synonym: Flattened end part of knee bone

Name: Shortening of all metacarpals
Def: Abnormal reduction in length of all metacarpal bones.

Name: Hyperextensible thumb
Def: The ability of the thumb joints to move beyond their normal range of motion.

Name: Nonopposable triphalangeal thumb
Def: A form of triphalangeal thumb that cannot be placed opposite the fingers of the same hand.

Name: Cortical irregularity
Def: An abnormal irregularity of cortical bone.

Name: Spinal stenosis with reduced interpedicular distance
Def: An abnormal narrowing of the spinal canal related to a reduction in the interpedicular distance (i.e., the distance measured between the pedicles on frontal [coronal] imaging).
Comment: The pedicles are two short, thick processes that connect the body of the vertebrae to the arch.
Synonym: Spinal stenosis due to short pedicles

Name: Short tibia
Def: Underdevelopment (reduced size) of the tibia.

Name: Posterior subluxation of radial head
Def: Partial dislocation of the head of the radius in the posterior direction.

Name: Avascular necrosis of the capital femoral epiphysis
Def: Avascular necrosis of the proximal epiphysis of the femur occurring in growing children and caused by an interruption of the blood supply to the head of the femur close to the hip joint. The necrosis is characteristically associated with flattening of the femoral head, for which reason the term coxa plana has been used to refer to this feature in the medical literature.
Comment: In medical parlance, this is often referred to as Legg Calve Perthes disease. Here, the name 'Avascular necrosis of the capital femoral epiphysis' is preferred to emphasize that the term refers to a phenotypic feature rather than a disease entity. Avascular necrosis of the femoral head may result in pain in the hip, limp, stiffness and reduced range of motion, and some degree of atrophy of the affected leg. The phrase Legg Perthes syndrome or Legg Calve Perthes disease is also used to refer to a number of diseases, including the idiopathic form and a form that is related to mutation in the COL2A1 gene (MIM 150600). Legg-Calve-Perthes disease usually occurs in boys 4 to 10 years old, and is clinically characterized by limping, hip stiffness, limited range of motion, and can result in restriction of growth of the affected leg and wasting of the muscles of the upper thigh.

Name: obsolete Generalized osteoporosis with pathologic fractures
Osteosclerosis of the base of the skull
Def: An increase in bone density affecting the basicranium (base of the skull).
Comment: Bundled term. Consider obsoleting it and splitting of osteosclerosis of base of skull.

Name: Contractures of the joints of the lower limbs
Neonatal epiphyseal stippling
Def: The presence of abnormal punctate (speckled, dot-like) calcifications in one or more epiphyses during the neonatal period.
Synonym: Speckled calcifications in bone end parts in neonates

Name: Basilar impression
Def: Abnormal elevation of the floor of the posterior fossa including occipital condyles and foramen magnum.

Name: Small flat posterior fossa
Def: An abnormally small and flat configuration of the posterior cranial fossa.
Synonym: Small and flat posterior fossa of skull
Small and flat posterior skull bones

Name: 2-4 toe cutaneous syndactyly
Def: A soft tissue continuity in the anteroposterior axis between the toes 2, 3, and 4.
Synonym: Soft tissue syndactyly of toes 2, 3, and 4
Webbed second, third and fourth toes

Name: Fifth finger distal phalanx clinodactyly
Def: Bending or curvature of the distal phalanx of little finger in the radial direction (i.e., towards the 4th finger).
Synonym: Curvature of outermost bone of little finger
Curvature of outermost bone of pinkie finger
Curvature of outermost bone of pinky finger

Name: Aplasia/Hypoplasia of the tibia
Def: Absence or underdevelopment of the tibia.

Name: Short forearm
Def: Underdevelopment of both forearm bones, the ulna and the radius, resulting in a shortened forearm.

Name: Absent fourth finger distal interphalangeal crease
Def: Absence of the distal interphalangeal flexion creases of the fourth finger.
Synonym: No fourth finger distal interphalangeal crease

Name: Lumbar platyspondyly
Def: A flattened vertebral body shape with reduced distance beween the vertebral endplates affecting the lumbar spine.

Name: Generalized osteosclerosis
Def: An abnormal increase of bone mineral density with generalized involvement of the skeleton.
Synonym: Increased bone density in skeletal bones

Name: Short mandibular condyles
Synonym: Bilateral hypoplasia of condylar process of mandible
Bilateral hypoplasia of mandibular condylar head
Bilateral hypoplasia of mandibular condylar neck
Decreased height of condylar process of mandible
Decreased length of condylar process of mandible

Name: Cortical thickening of long bone diaphyses
Def: Abnormal thickening of the cortex of the diaphyseal region of long bones.

Name: Short humerus
Def: Underdevelopment of the humerus.
Synonym: Short long bone of upper arm

Name: Shortening of all distal phalanges of the toes
Def: Abnormally short distal phalanx of toe of all toes.
Synonym: Shortening of all outermost bone of the toes

Name: Posterior radial head dislocation
Def: A dislocation of the head of the radius from its socket in the elbow joint in an posterior direction.

Name: Absent distal phalanges
Def: Aplasia (absence) of the distal phalanges.

Name: Supernumerary ribs
Def: The presence of more than 12 rib pairs.

Name: Postaxial polysyndactyly of foot
Def: Combined syndactyly and polydactyly of the foot on the lateral side (i.e., on the side of the little toe).

Name: Short middle phalanx of finger
Def: Short (hypoplastic) middle phalanx of finger, affecting one or more fingers.
Synonym: Hypoplasia of the middle phalanges of the hand

Name: Clinodactyly of the 2nd toe
Def: Bending or curvature of a second toe in the tibial direction (i.e., towards the big toe).

Name: Flexion contracture of toe
Def: One or more bent (flexed) toe joints that cannot be straightened actively or passively.

Name: Dysharmonic delayed bone age
Def: A type of dysharmonic skeletal maturation in which there is a delay in skeletal maturation whose degree differs markedly in different bones.

Name: obsolete Joint swelling onset late infancy
obsolete Joint dislocations in young adult
Calcific stippling of infantile cartilaginous skeleton
Rounded middle phalanx of finger
Def: An abnormally round shape of the middle phalanx of the finger.

Name: Bifid thumb distal phalanx
Def: Cleft (split into two parts) distal phalanx of thumb.

Name: Diffuse cerebral calcification
Def: Generalized deposition of calcium salts within the brain.

Name: Multiple prenatal fractures
Def: The presence of bone fractures in the prenatal period that are diagnosed at birth or before.
Synonym: Numerous multiple fractures present at birth
Numerous multiple fractures that are present at birth

Name: Ulnar radial head dislocation
Def: A dislocation of the head of the radius from its socket in the elbow joint in an ulnar direction.

Name: Type E brachydactyly
Def: In type E brachydactyly, shortening of the fingers is mainly in the metacarpals and metatarsals.

Name: Pseudoarthrosis
Def: A pathologic entity characterized by a developmental defect in a long bone leading to bending and pathologic fracture, with inability to form a normal bony callus with subsequent fibrous nonunion, leading to the pseudarthrosis (or \

Name: Opposable triphalangeal thumb
Def: A form of triphalangeal thumb that can be placed opposite the fingers of the same hand.

Name: Metaphyseal enchondromatosis
Def: An enchondroma is a benign growth of cartilage that develops within the medullary cavity of bone. Enchondromatosis refers to the presence of multiple enchondromas, and this term refers to the presence of multiple enchondromas within the medulla of metaphyseal bone. Radiographically an enchondroma presents a an oval, linear, or pyramidal osteolytic (radiolucent) lesion with well defined margins.

Name: Metaphyseal chondrodysplasia
Def: An abnormality of skeletal development characterized by a disturbance of the metaphysis and its histological structure with relatively normal epiphyses and vertebrae.
Comment: The term metaphyseal chondrodysplasia is usually used to describe a disease but is often also used to describe the corresponding phenotypic appearance. This use is retained in the HPO for convenience, but if possible a precise phenotypic description is preferred.

Name: Brachytelomesophalangy
Def: Disproportionately short middle and distal phalanges compared to the hand/foot.
Synonym: Progressive brachydactyly of middle and distal phalanges
Short middle and distal phalanges of digits ii through v

Name: Polysyndactyly of hallux
Def: Combined syndactyly and polydactyly of the great toe.

Name: Progressive flexion contractures
Def: Progressively worsening joint contractures.

Name: Enlarged sagittal diameter of the cervical canal
Congenital finger flexion contractures
Def: Multiple bent (flexed) finger joints that cannot be straightened actively or passively.

Name: Metacarpophalangeal synostosis
