Def: Fusion of a metacarpal bone with the proximal phalanx of the finger distal to it across the corresponding metacarpophalangeal joint.
Synonym: Fused long bone of hand with innermost finger bone

Name: Absent ossification of cervical vertebral bodies
Def: A lack of bone mineralization of one or more body of cervical vertebra.

Name: Aphalangy of the hands
Def: Absence of a digit or of one or more phalanges of a finger.

Name: Hyperostosis cranialis interna
Def: Bony overgrowth of the internal (endosteal) surface of the calvaria and the base of skull.
Synonym: Enlargement of the inner surface of the skull bones
Excessive growth of inner surface of the skull bones
Hyperostosis of the internal surface of the cranial bone
Hyperostosis of the internal surface of the cranial bones
Hypertrophy of the internal surface of the cranial bones
Increased ossification of the internal surface of the cranial bones
Overgrowth of the inner surface of the skull bones
Overgrowth of the inside of the skull
Thick inner surface of the skull bones
Thick internal surface of the cranial bones

Name: Progressive forearm bowing
Def: Progressive bending or abnormal curvature of the forearm skeleton.

Name: Proximal tibial and fibular fusion
Synonym: Fusion of innermost shinbone and calf bone

Name: Double first metacarpals
Def: Duplication of the metacarpal I bones.

Name: Radial deviation of thumb terminal phalanx
Severe generalized osteoporosis
Def: Severe degree of osteoporosis.

Name: Metaphyseal dysostosis
Def: Abnormal mineralization of the metaphyseal area of bones.

Name: Fifth metacarpal with ulnar notch
Def: Presence of an angular or V -shaped indentation on the ulnar side of the fifth metacarpal bone (i.e., on the sides towards the fifth finger).
Synonym: Fifth metacarpal notched on ulnar side

Name: Abnormal cervical curvature
Def: The presence of an abnormal curvature of the cervical vertebral column.

Name: Delayed pneumatization of the mastoid process
Def: An abnormally reduced degree of pneumatization (i.e., formation of air cells) in the mastoid process with respect to age-dependent norms.

Name: Rhomboid or triangular shaped 5th finger middle phalanx
Def: Rhomboid or triangular shaped 5th (little) finger middle phalanx.
Synonym: Rhomboid or triangular shaped fifth finger middle phalanx

Name: Biliary atresia
Def: Atresia of the biliary tree.

Name: Abnormality of metacarpal epiphyses
Synonym: Abnormality of end part of long bone of hand

Name: Aplasia/Hypoplasia involving the metacarpal bones
Def: Aplasia or Hypoplasia affecting the metacarpal bones.

Name: Abnormal metacarpal morphology
Def: Irregularly shaped metacarpal bones of varying degree.
Synonym: Abnormal shape of long bones of hand

Name: Supernumerary metacarpal bones
Def: The presence of more than the normal number of metacarpal bones.

Name: Abnormal finger phalanx morphology
Def: Abnormalities affecting the phalanx of finger.
Comment: This category is a supercategory for abnormalties affect phalanges of the hand.
Synonym: Abnormal form of phalanges of the hand
Abnormality of the phalanges of the hand

Name: Abnormal epiphysis morphology of the phalanges of the hand
Def: Abnormality of one or all of the epiphyses of the phalanges of the hand. Note that this includes the epiphysis of the 1st metacarpal. In contrast to the metacarpals 2-5, the first metacarpal is embryologically of phalangeal origin and as such equivalent to the proximal phalanges of the digits 2-5 (whereas the proximal phalanx of the thumb is equivalent to the middle phalanges of the other digits).
Synonym: Abnormality of the end part of the hand bones
Abnormality of the epiphyses of the fingers
Abnormality of the epiphyses of the phalanges of the hand

Name: obsolete Abnormal ossification of hand bones
Abnormal hand morphology
Def: Any structural anomaly of the hand.
Comment: This is a category to be used for general descriptions of hand dysmorphology. In time, it should be replaced by more accurate descriptions.

Name: Abnormalities of the metaphyses of the hand
Synonym: Abnormality of the wide portion of the hand bone

Name: Abnormality of the epiphyses of the hand
Def: Any abnormality of the epiphyses of the phalanges or metacarpal bones.
Synonym: Abnormality of the end part of the hand bone

Name: Abnormalities of the diaphyses of the hand
Synonym: Abnormalities of shaft of long bone of the hand

Name: Abnormality of hand cortical bone
Def: An anomaly of the outer shell (cortex) of a hand bone.
Synonym: Abnormality of the cortex of hand bones

Name: Aplasia/hypoplasia involving bones of the hand
Def: Absence (due to failure to form) or underdevelopment of the bones of the hand.

Name: Synostosis involving the fibula
Synonym: Bone fusion involving the calf bones

Name: Abnormality of epiphysis morphology
Def: An anomaly of epiphysis, which is the expanded articular end of a long bone that developes from a secondary ossification center, and which during the period of growth is either entirely cartilaginous or is separated from the shaft by a cartilaginous disk.
Synonym: Abnormal shape of end part of bone

Name: Abnormal renal corticomedullary differentiation
Def: An abnormality of corticomedullary differentiation (CMD) on diagnostic imaging such as magnetic resonance imaging, computer tomography, or sonography. CMD is a difference in the visualization of cortex and medulla.
Comment: On T1-weighted magnetic resonance imaging, the signal intensity of the normal renal cortex is typically higher than medulla, resulting in easily visualized corticomedullary differentiation (CMD). Loss of CMD can be seen in disorders such as glomerulonephritis, acute tubular necrosis, end-stage chronic renal failure, obstructive hydronephrosis, and acute allograft rejection.

Name: Abnormal respiratory motile cilium morphology
Def: Abnormal arrangement of the structures of the motile cilium.

Name: Bilateral lung agenesis
Def: Bilateral lack of development of the lungs.

Name: Laryngeal obstruction
Def: Blockage of the upper airway at the level of the larynx often accompanied by respiratory distress.

Name: Ventilator dependence with inability to wean
Decreased sensitivity to hypoxemia
Def: Reduced tendency to respond to a reduced concentration of oxygen in the blood by increasing respiration.
Comment: Note that hypoxia is defined as lack of oxygen in tissues. Hypoxia is usually preceded by hypoxemia (decreased concentration of oxygen in blood).

Name: Multiple pulmonary cysts
Def: The presence of multiple lung cysts.
Comment: Emphysematous changes sometimes can be mistaken for multifocal lung cysts. In contrast to true cysts, the cystlike lucencies caused by the destruction of lung parenchyma in emphy-sema do not have walls. Nevertheless, emphysema can be accompanied by multiple cysts, such as bullae, or in association with LCH.

Name: Apneic episodes in infancy
Def: Recurrent episodes of apnea occurring during infancy.

Name: Laryngeal web
Def: A membrane-like structure that extends across the laryngeal lumen close to the level of the vocal cords.
Comment: Manifestations may appear at any age (hoarse or weak voice and frequent upper respiratory infections) but onset usually occurs during infancy (respiratory distress, stridor and an unusual cry).

Name: Anteroposteriorly shortened larynx
Def: Abnormal shortening of the larynx in the anteroposterior (front to back) axis.

Name: Impaired gluconeogenesis
Def: An impairment of gluconeogenesis.

Name: Hypoargininemia
Def: A decreased concentration of arginine in the blood.

Name: Intermittent hypothermia
Def: Episodes of reduced body termperature.

Name: Temperature instability
Def: Disordered thermoregulation characterized by an impaired ability to maintain a balance between heat production and heat loss, with resulting instability of body temperature.

Name: Respiratory acidosis
Def: Acidosis because of respiratory retention of carbon dioxide.

Name: Episodic ketoacidosis
Def: Intermittent episodes of ketoacidosis.

Name: Type II diabetes mellitus
Def: A type of diabetes mellitus initially characterized by insulin resistance and hyperinsulinemia and subsequently by glucose interolerance and hyperglycemia.
Comment: Persons with type II diabetes mellitus rarely develop ketoacidosis.

Name: Reduced phenylalanine hydroxylase activity
Def: A reduction in phenylalanine 4-monooxygenase activity.

Name: Elevated maternal serum alpha-fetoprotein
Def: An elevation of alpha-feto protein in the maternal serum.

Name: Multinodular goiter
Def: Enlargement of the thyroid gland related to multiple nodules in the thyroid gland.

Name: Congenital muscular torticollis
Def: A congenital form of torticollis resulting from shortening of the sternocleidomastoid muscle and leading to a limited range of motion in both rotation and lateral bending.
Comment: Congenital muscular torticollis is thought to result from injury to the sternocleidomastoid muscle during birth trauma, resulting in fibrosis and unilateral shortening of the sternocleidomastoid muscle. Congenital muscular torticollis is thus etiologically and phenotypically distinct from spasmodic torticollis.

Name: Redundant neck skin
Def: Excess skin around the neck, often lying in horizontal folds.
Comment: With age and increased vertical growth of the neck, excess nuchal skin may disappear and the neck may become broad or webbed. If the skin folds are vertical or paravertical, the term Neck webbing should be used.

Name: Thyroid hypoplasia
Def: Developmental hypoplasia of the thyroid gland.

Name: Nodular goiter
Def: Enlargement of the thyroid gland related to one or more nodules in the thyroid gland.

Name: Decreased adipose tissue around neck
Def: Reduced amount of adipose tissue in the region of the neck.
Synonym: Loss of adipose tissue around the neck

Name: Restricted neck movement due to contractures
Synonym: Restricted neck mobility due to contractures
Restricted neck movement due to contractures

Name: Ureteral atresia
Def: A developmental defect defined by the failure of the formation of the lumen (tube) of the ureter.

Name: Ureteral obstruction
Def: Obstruction of the flow of urine through the ureter.

Name: Hypotrophy of the small hand muscles
Broad phalanx
Def: Increased side-to-side width of one or more phalanges of the fingers or toes.

Name: Cuboidal metacarpal
Def: Severely shortened metacarpal with a cuboidal appearance.
Comment: The metacarpals are normally tubular in appearance.
Synonym: Short, cube shaped long bone of hand

Name: Widened metacarpal shaft
Synonym: Broad shaft of long bone of hand

Name: Delayed phalangeal epiphyseal ossification
Def: Delay in the process of formation and maturation of the epiphysis of one or more phalanx.
Synonym: Delayed bone maturation of end part of digital bone

Name: Metaphyseal cupping of metacarpals
Def: Metaphyseal cupping affecting the metacarpal bones.
Synonym: Cupping of wide portion of long bone of hand

Name: Cone-shaped epiphyses of phalanges 2 to 5
Synonym: Cone-shaped end part of digital bones 2 to 5

Name: Y-shaped metacarpals
Def: Y-shaped metacarpals are the result of a partial fusion of two metacarpal bones, with the two arms of the Y pointing in the distal direction. Y-shaped metacarpals may be seen in combination with polydactyly.

Name: Distal widening of metacarpals
Def: Abnormal increase in width of the distal region of the metacarpal bones.
Synonym: Wide outermost end of long bone

Name: Cone-shaped metacarpal epiphyses
Def: A cone-shaped appearance of the epiphyses of the metacarpal bones, producing a 'ball-in-a-socket' appearance. This epiphyses are located at the distal ends of the metacarpal bones.
Synonym: Cone-shaped end part of long bone

Name: Multiple carpal ossification centers
Def: A delay in the process of formation and maturation of the epiphysis of one or more long bones.

Name: Severe carpal ossification delay
Synonym: Severe delay in maturation of wrist bone

Name: Metacarpophalangeal joint contracture
Def: A chronic loss of joint motion in metacarpophalangeal joints due to structural changes in muscle, tendons, ligaments, or skin that prevents normal movement.
Comment: In the literature this has been called metacarpophalangeal camptodactyly, but the term camptodactyly should be researved for a painless flexion contracture of the proximal interphalangeal (PIP) joint.

Name: Absent proximal finger flexion creases
Def: Absence of the proximal interphalangeal flexion creases of the fingers.

Name: Malaligned carpal bone
Def: Malalignement of carpal bone angles either with respect to each other, to the corresponding metacarpals or with respect to the wrist (radius and ulna).

Name: Wide tufts of distal phalanges
Synonym: Wide tips of outermost digital bone

Name: 3-4 finger syndactyly
Def: Syndactyly with fusion of fingers three and four.

Name: Metacarpophalangeal joint hyperextensibility
Def: Increased mobility of one ore more metacarpophalangeal joint.

Name: Finger syndactyly
Def: Webbing or fusion of the fingers, involving soft parts only or including bone structure. Bony fusions are referred to as \

Name: Fingerpad telangiectases
Def: Telangiectasia (small dilated blood vessels) located in the fingerpads at the tips of the fingers.
Synonym: Small dilated blood vessels in fingerpads

Name: Tapered metacarpals
Def: Metacarpal that becomes thinner toward the distal end.

Name: Absent phalangeal crease
Def: Absence of one or more interphalangeal creases (i.e., of the transverse lines in the skin between the phalanges of the fingers).

Name: Shortening of all middle phalanges of the fingers
Def: Short, hypoplastic middle phalanx of finger, affecting all fingers.

Name: Expanded phalanges with widened medullary cavities
Multiple palmar creases
Def: The presence of multiple creases on the palm of the hand (more than the normal three major creases (distal transverse crease, proximal transverse crease, and thenar crease).

Name: Shortening of all distal phalanges of the fingers
Def: Hypoplasia of all of the distal phalanx of finger.
Synonym: Shortening of all outermost bones of the fingers

Name: Proximal tapering of metacarpals
Def: Some or all of the metacarpal bones (i.e., metacarpal II to V) have a pointed proximal appearance.
Synonym: Pointed innermost long bone of hand

Name: Acral ulceration
Def: A type of digital ulcer that manifests as an open sore on the surface of the skin at the tip of a finger or toe.

Name: Long proximal phalanx of finger
Def: Increased length of the proximal phalanx of finger.

Name: Drumstick terminal phalanges
Def: Rounding and broadening of the tufts of the distal phalanges.
Comment: This designation is supposed to refer to the widening of the meaty end of a chicken drumstick (lower leg).

Name: Enlarged metacarpal epiphyses
Def: Abnormally large size of the metaphyseal epiphyses.
Synonym: Enlarged end part of long bone of hand

Name: Premature fusion of phalangeal epiphyses
Def: Fusion of the epiphysis and metaphysis of one or more phalanges prior to the normal age or stage of growth.
Synonym: Premature fusion of end part of digital bone

Name: Shortening of all proximal phalanges of the fingers
Def: Congenital hypoplasia of proximal phalanx of finger or all fingers.
Synonym: Shortening of all innermost bones of the fingers

Name: Central Y-shaped metacarpal
Def: A central Y-shaped metacarpal is the result of a partial fusion of two central metacarpals (i.e., metacarpals 2-4) of the hand, with the two arms of the Y pointing in the distal direction. Central Y-shaped metacarpals may be seen as a result of a central polydactyly with partial fusion of the duplicated metacarpal.
Synonym: Y-shaped central long bones of hand

Name: Broad metacarpal epiphyses
Def: Increased side-to-side width of the metacarpal epiphyses.
Synonym: Broad end part of long bone of hand

Name: Swan neck-like deformities of the fingers
Def: A swan neck deformity describes a finger with a hyperextended PIP joint and a flexed DIP joint. The most common cause for a swan neck-like deformity is a disruption of the end of the extensor tendon. Conditions that loosen the PIP joint and allow it to hyperextend, for example conditions that weaken the volar plate, can produce a swan neck deformity of the finger. One example is rheumatoid arthritis. Another cause are conditions that tighten up the small (intrinsic) muscles of the hand and fingers, for example hand trauma or nerve disorders, such as cerebral palsy, Parkinson's disease, or stroke.

Name: Proximal symphalangism of hands
Def: The term proximal symphalangism refers to a bony fusion of the middle and proximal phalanges of the digits of the hand, in other words the proximal interphalangeal joint (PIJ) is missing which can be seen either on x-rays or as an absence of the proximal interphalangeal finger creases.

Name: Long phalanx of finger
Def: Increased length of multiple or a single phalanx of finger.

Name: Ulnar deviation of thumb
Def: Bending or curvature of a thumb towards the ulnar side (towards the ring finger).

Name: Mesoaxial hand polydactyly
Def: The presence of a supernumerary finger (not a thumb) involving the third or fourth metacarpal with associated osseous syndactyly.

Name: Irregular metacarpals
Def: Irregular morphology of one or more metacarpal bones.

Name: Short metacarpals with rounded proximal ends
Synonym: Short long bone of hand with rounded innermost ends

Name: Soft tissue swelling of interphalangeal joints
Synonym: Soft tissue swelling of hinge joints

Name: Tubular metacarpal bones
Synonym: Cylindrical shaped long bones of hand

Name: Chess-pawn distal phalanges
Def: A morphological abnormality of distal phalanges such that they have the appearance of chess pawns.

Name: Flattened, squared-off epiphyses of tubular bones
Synonym: Flattened, squared-off end part of tubular bones

Name: Metacarpal diaphyseal endosteal sclerosis
Def: Increase in bone density in the diaphyseal (shaft) region of a metacarpal bone.

Name: Proximal phalangeal periosteal thickening
Synonym: Thickening of connective tissue of innermost finger bone

Name: Two carpal ossification centers present at birth
Pseudoepiphyses of second metacarpal
Synonym: Extra bone on end of second long bone of hand

Name: Decreased palmar creases
Def: Poorly defined or shallow palmar creases.

Name: Deep palmar crease
Def: Excessively deep creases of the palm.

Name: Tapered phalanx of finger
Def: Phalanges of the fingers becoming thinner toward the distal end.

Name: Thimble-shaped middle phalanges of hand
Def: The middle phalanx of finger resembles a thimble, a small metal cap to protect the finger while sewing that has a broad (proximal) base and narrower top, whereby both base and top are flat.

Name: Hypermobility of distal interphalangeal joints
Synonym: Increased mobility of outermost hinge joint

Name: Decreased movement range in interphalangeal joints
Synonym: Decreased range of movement range in hinge joints

Name: Irregular phalanges
Def: Alteration of the normally smooth radiographic contour of phalanges producing an irregular appearance.

Name: Hypersegmentation of proximal phalanx of second finger
Def: Presence of an additional phalanx-like bone, producing an extra, wedge-shaped bone at the base of the proximal phalanx of the second finger.
Comment: This anomaly is characteristic for brachydactyly type C.

Name: Metaphyseal cupping of proximal phalanges
Def: Metaphyseal cupping affecting the proximal phalanges.

Name: Thin proximal phalanges with broad epiphyses of the hand
Comment: removed the logical def: 'has part' some (('decreased thickness' and ('inheres in' some 'proximal phalanx of manus') and ('has modifier' some abnormal)) and ('has part' some ('increased width' and ('inheres in' some 'epiphysis of proximal phalanx of manus'))) and ('has modifier' some abnormal))
Synonym: Thin innermost bone with broad end part of the hand bone
Thin proximal phalanges with broad epiphyses

Name: Single interphalangeal crease of fifth finger
Def: Presence of only one (instead of two, as normal) interphalangeal crease of the fifth finger.

Name: Limited mobility of proximal interphalangeal joint
Synonym: Limited mobility of innermost hinge joint

Name: Tapering pointed ends of distal finger phalanges
Def: A reduction in diameter of the distal phalanx of finger towards the distal end such that the tip of the phalanx comes to a point (this feature can be observed on radiograms).

Name: Osteoarthritis of the first carpometacarpal joint
Expanded metacarpals with widened medullary cavities
Osteoarthritis of the distal interphalangeal joint
Osteolysis involving tarsal bones
Def: An increased resorption of bone matrix by osteoclasts leading to bony defects involving the tarsal bones.

Name: Slender metacarpals
Def: Decreased width of the metacarpal bones (that is, reduced diameter).

Name: Shortening of all middle phalanges of the toes
Def: Abnormal shortening of all middle phalanges of toes.
Synonym: Shortening of all the middle bones of the toes

Name: Limited wrist movement
Def: An abnormal limitation of the mobility of the wrist.

Name: Elevated alpha-fetoprotein
Def: An increased concentration of alpha-fetoprotein.
Comment: An elevation of alpha-feto protein, which is produced by the fetal liver and the yolk sac and may be increased in the serum of pregnant women with a fetus with some types of developmental anomaly such as open neural tube defects and omphalocele.

Name: Abnormal phalangeal joint morphology of the hand
Synonym: Abnormality of phalangeal joints of the hand
Abnormality of the small joints of the hand

Name: Aplasia/Hypoplasia of the 5th finger
Def: A small/hypoplastic or absent/aplastic 5th finger.

Name: Abnormality of the epiphyses of the 2nd finger
Def: Abnormality of one or all of the epiphyses of the proximal, middle, and distal phalanges of the 2nd finger.
Synonym: Abnormality of the end part of the index finger bone

Name: Aplasia/Hypoplasia of the 2nd finger
Def: A small/hypoplastic or absent/aplastic 2nd finger.

Name: Aplasia/Hypoplasia of fingers
Def: Small/hypoplastic or absent/aplastic fingers.

Name: Small placenta
Def: Reduced size of the placenta.

Name: Large placenta
Def: Increased size of the placenta.

Name: Fluctuating splenomegaly
Def: Intermittently increased size of the spleen.

Name: Hypoplastic spleen
Def: Underdevelopment of the spleen.

Name: Pancreatic lymphangiectasis
Def: The presence of lymphangiectasis in the pancreas.

Name: Reduced pancreatic beta cells
Def: Reduced number of beta cells in the pancreatic islets of Langerhans.
Comment: The beta cells are responsible for producing insulin and amylin.

Name: Pancreatic hyperplasia
Def: Hyperplasia of the pancreas.
Comment: Hyperplasia is defined in MPATH as an increase in cell numbers in comparison to normal as a consequence of increased cell proliferation. Hyperplasia is a non -neoplastic process.

Name: Ectopic pancreatic tissue
Def: The presence of pancreatic tissue outside the normal pancreas, in many cases along the foregut and proximal midgut.

Name: Chronic pancreatitis
Def: A chronic form of pancreatitis.

Name: Generalized hypoplasia of dental enamel
Def: A generalized form of developmental hypoplasia of the dental enamel.

Name: Multiple unerupted teeth
Def: The presence of multiple embedded tooth germs which have failed to erupt.
Synonym: Failure of eruption of multiple teeth

Name: Hypomineralization of enamel
Def: A decreased amount of enamel mineralization.
Synonym: White spot lesions of tooth enamel

Name: Advanced eruption of teeth
Def: Premature tooth eruption, which can be defined as tooth eruption more than 2 SD earlier than the mean eruption age.
Comment: There are established norms for the timing of eruption in both deciduous and permanent teeth [Garn and Rohmann, [1966]; Lunt and Law, [1974]; McDonald et al. [2004]]. Eruption is defined by the appearance of a tooth that has pierced the gum.

Name: Agenesis of central incisor
Def: Agenesis of one or more central incisors, i.e., of lower secondary incisor, lower primary incisor, upper secondary incisor, or of upper central primary incisor.
Synonym: Failure of development of central incisor

Name: Discolored lateral incisors
Def: The presence of discolored lateral incisors.
Synonym: Abnormality of color of front teeth
Abnormality of color of lateral incisor
Abnormality of shade of lateral incisor

Name: Marked delay in eruption of permanent teeth
Synonym: Severe delay of eruption of adult teeth
Severe delay of eruption of permanent teeth
Very late eruption of adult teeth
Very late eruption of permanent teeth

Name: Abnormality of dental eruption
Def: An abnormality of tooth eruption.
Comment: The average ages for eruption of the primary teeth are: 6 months: lower central incisor, 7 months: upper central incisor, 8 months: upper lateral incisor, 9 months: lower lateral incisor, 12 months first molars, 18 months, canines, 2 years, second molars.

Name: Agenesis of maxillary central incisor
Def: Agenesis of upper secondary incisor or of upper central primary incisor.
Synonym: Failure of development of maxillary central incisor

Name: Hypoplasia of dental enamel
Def: Developmental hypoplasia of the dental enamel.
Comment: Note that the term enamel dysplasia was previously used for this feature but is no longer recommended.

Name: Prolonged bleeding after dental extraction
Def: Prolonged bleeding post dental extraction sufficient to require medical intervention.

Name: Dagger-shaped pulp calcifications
Def: Dagger-shaped calcifications in the dental pulp.

Name: Atrophy of alveolar ridges
Synonym: Atrophy of alveolar processes of jaw
Flattening of alveolar processes of jaw
Resorption of alveolar processes of jaw

Name: Generalized microdontia
Def: A generalized form of microdontia.

Name: Widely spaced primary teeth
Def: Increased space between the primary teeth. Note this phenotype should be distinguished from increased space due purely to microdontia.

Name: Single median maxillary incisor
Def: The presence of a single, median maxillary incisor, affecting both the primary maxillary incisor and the permanent maxillary incisor.
Comment: If a single maxillary central incisor is present but not positioned in the midline, this could be hypodontia, but this cannot be evaluated without a radiograph.
Synonym: Solitary median maxillary central incisor syndrome

Name: Irregularly spaced teeth
Def: Irregular distribution of the teeth along the dental arch, i.e., and irregular spatial pattern of teeth.

Name: Multiple non-erupting secondary teeth
Synonym: Failure of eruption of multiple adult teeth
Failure of eruption of multiple permanent teeth

Name: Premature loss of primary teeth
Def: Loss of the primary (also known as deciduous) teeth before the usual age.
Comment: The primary teeth are usually shed and replaced by the permanent teeth, usually by the age of six years. With premature loss of primary teeth, there is a delay between the loss of the primary teeth and the eruption of the permanent teeth.

Name: Buried teeth encased in mucopolysaccharide
Synonym: Failure of dental eruption due to mucopolysaccharidoses
Failure of tooth eruption due to mucopolysaccharidoses

Name: Alveolar process hypoplasia
Def: Underdevelopment of the alveolar process (also known as alveolar bone).
Comment: The alveolar process is a thickened ridge of bone that contains the tooth sockets on the mandible and maxilla.
Synonym: Decreased size of alveolar process of jaw
Deficiency of alveolar process of jaw
Underdevelopment of alveolar process of jaw

Name: Supernumerary maxillary incisor
Def: The presence of a supernumerary, i.e., extra, maxillary incisor, either the primary maxillary incisor or the permanent maxillary incisor.

Name: Crowded maxillary incisors
Def: A type of dental misalignment with crowded central incisors, i.e., of maxillary secondary incisor, or of maxillary central primary incisor.

Name: Hypoplasia of the primary teeth
Def: Developmental hypoplasia of the primary teeth.

Name: Persistence of primary teeth
Def: Persistence of the primary teeth beyond the age by which they normally are shed and replaced by the permanent teeth.
Comment: The primary teeth are usually shed and replaced by the permanent teeth, usually by the age of six years. Persistence of primary teeth may be related to agenesis of the permanent teeth. Molar primary teeth may be persistent because of the agenesis of the premolars.

Name: Short dental roots
Def: Short dental root.

Name: Premature eruption of permanent teeth
Def: Premature tooth eruption of the permanent dentition.

Name: Malformation of mandibular premolar
Def: An abnormality of the morphology of secondary premolar tooth.

Name: Conical mandibular incisor
Def: An abnormal conical morphology of the primary or permanent mandibular incisors.

Name: Peg-shaped maxillary lateral incisors
Def: Peg-shaped upper lateral secondary incisor tooth.

Name: Abnormality of primary molar morphology
Def: An abnormality of morphology of primary molar.
Synonym: Abnormality of shape of baby molar
Abnormality of shape of primary molar

Name: Screwdriver-shaped incisors
Def: An abnormality of morphology of the incisor tooth in which the tooth is shaped like a screwdriver blade, i.e., having a rhomboid shape.

Name: Microdontia of primary teeth
Def: Decreased size of the primary teeth.

Name: Agenesis of permanent teeth
Def: A congenital defect characterized by the absence of one or more permanent teeth, including oligodontia, hypodontia, and adontia of the of permanent teeth.
Synonym: Failure of development of permanent teeth
Failure of development of secondary teeth

Name: Obliteration of the pulp chamber
Def: Obliteration of the pulp chambers owing to mineralization of the dental pulp.
Synonym: Narrowing of pulp chamber of tooth
Reduced size of pulp chamber of tooth

Name: Failure of eruption of permanent teeth
Def: Lack of tooth eruption of the secondary dentition.
Synonym: Failure of eruption of adult teeth

Name: Hypoplasia of the tooth germ
Def: Developmental hypoplasia of the tooth germ, i.e., of the structure that forms in odontogenesis that will develop into a tooth.

Name: Agenesis of mandibular central incisor
Def: Agenesis of lower secondary incisor or lower primary incisor.
Synonym: Failure of development of mandibular central incisor

Name: Premature loss of permanent teeth
Def: Premature loss of the permanent teeth.

Name: Shovel-shaped maxillary central incisors
Def: Incisors with a thick marginal ridge surrounding a deep lingual fossa are termed shovel-shaped incisors.

Name: Crumpled long bones
Def: An crumpled radiographic appearance of the long bones, as if the long bone had been crushed together producing irregularities. This feature is the result of multiple fractures and repeated rounds of ineffective healing, as can be seen for instance in severe forms of osteogenesis imperfecta.

Name: Irregular patellae
Def: An alteration of the normally relatively smooth margins of the kneecap in radiographic images leading to an irregular contour.

Name: Distal ulnar epiphyseal stippling
Def: The presence of abnormal punctate (speckled, dot-like) calcifications in the distal epiphysis of the ulna.

Name: Broad long bone diaphyses
Def: Increased width of the diaphysis of long bones.

Name: Dumbbell-shaped femur
Def: The femur is shortened and displays flaring (widening) of the metaphyses.

Name: Proximal tibial hypoplasia
Comment: Removed logical definition that used anonymous class. Requested new term from UBERON: 'proximal tibia'

Name: Knee flexion contracture
Def: A bent (flexed) knee joint that cannot be straightened actively or passively.

Name: Rudimentary fibula
Def: Absent or nearly absent fibula. (Does not include aplastic)

Name: Progressive bowing of long bones
Def: Progressive bending or abnormal curvature of a long bone.

Name: Club-shaped distal femur
Def: An abnormal conformation of the femur that becomes gradually enlarged towards the distal end. This feature affects the distal femoral metaphysis and epiphysis.
Comment: previous def: 'has part' some \n(clavate and ('inheres in' some 'Distal end of femur (adult human)') and ('has modifier' some abnormal))

Name: Short lower limbs
Def: Shortening of the legs related to developmental hypoplasia of the bones of the leg.

Name: Hypoplastic distal radial epiphyses
Def: Underdevelopment of the distal epiphysis of the radius.

Name: Wide distal femoral metaphysis
Def: Increased width of the distal part of the shaft (metaphysis) of the femur.
Synonym: Broad outermost wide portion of thighbone

Name: Anterior tibial bowing
Def: An abnormal anterior bending or curvature of the tibia.

Name: Overtubulated long bones
Def: Overconstriction, or narrowness of the diaphysis and metaphysis of long bones.

Name: Increased density of long bones
Def: An abnormal increase in the bone density of the long bones.

Name: Limited pronation/supination of forearm
Def: A limitation of the ability to place the forearm in a position such that the palm faces anteriorly (supination) and to place the forearm in a position such that the palm faces posteriorly (pronation).

Name: Flat distal femoral epiphysis
Def: An abnormal flattening of the distal epiphysis of femur.
Synonym: Flat end part of outermost thighbone

Name: Club-shaped proximal femur
Def: An abnormal conformation of the femur that becomes gradually enlarged towards the proximal end. This feature affects the proximal femoral metaphysis and epiphysis.
Comment: previous def: 'has part' some \n(clavate and ('inheres in' some 'Proximal end of femur (adult human)') and ('has modifier' some abnormal))

Name: Irregular distal femoral epiphysis
Def: Anomaly of the contour of the Distal epiphysis of femur such that its normally smooth appearance is irregular.

Name: Distal tapering femur
Synonym: Tapering of outermost end of thighbone

Name: Progressive leg bowing
Def: Progressive bending or abnormal curvature of the leg.

Name: Distal tibial bowing
Def: A bending or abnormal curvature of the distal portion of the tibia.

Name: Cortically dense long tubular bones
Def: Increased density of the compact bone of long bone.
Comment: Note that compact bone and cortical bone are synonymous.

Name: Broad femoral metaphyses
Synonym: Broad wide portion of thigh bone

Name: Asymmetric radial dysplasia
Def: The presence of asymmetric developmental dysplasia of the radius.

Name: Peg-like central prominence of distal tibial metaphyses
Elongated radius
Def: Increased length of the radius.

Name: Broad femoral neck
Def: An abnormally wide femoral neck (which is the process of bone, connecting the femoral head with the femoral shaft).

Name: Proximal femoral metaphyseal abnormality
Def: An anomaly of the metaphysis of the proximal femur (close to the hip).
Synonym: Abnormal wide portion of innermost thighbone

Name: Hypoplasia of proximal radius
Def: Proximal radial shortening owing to a congenital defect of development.

Name: Disproportionate prominence of the femoral medial condyle
Enlargement of the distal femoral epiphysis
Def: An abnormal enlargement of the distal epiphysis of the femur.
Synonym: Enlargement of the outermost thighbone end part

Name: Increased density of long bone diaphyses
Synonym: Increased density of shaft of long bone

Name: Hypoplasia of proximal fibula
Def: Underdevelopment or shortening of the end of the fibula (calf bone) nearest the knee.
Synonym: Small innermost upper end of calf bone
Underdeveloped innermost upper end of calf bone

Name: Patellar aplasia
Def: Absence of the patella.

Name: Multicentric ossification of proximal femoral epiphyses
Lateral displacement of the femoral head
Def: A developmental anomaly with lateral displacement of the femoral head.

Name: Delayed patellar ossification
Def: Formation of bone in the patella later than normal.
Comment: The patella initially ossifies at between three and five years, commencing as multiple foci that rapidly coalesce. As the patellar ossification center enlarges the expanding margins may be irregular and associated with accessory ossification centers. These are most common superolaterally and may lead to the development of a bipartite patella. The bipartite patella has cartilaginous continuity despite the appearance of osseous discontinuity. The patella expands to all cartilaginous contours during late adolescence when the epiphyseal ossification centers around the knee are also in the final stages of maturation. The only cartilage not replaced is that occupying the superior two-thirds of the articular surface (the lower one-third is covered by the fat pad). The subchondral plate does not assume the actual articular contours until the late stages of osseous maturation (after ten to twelve years). Accordingly, typical measurements such as medial and lateral angulation cannot be accurately done prior to the final stages of patellar ossification expansion and maturation (PMID:6729496).
Synonym: Delayed bone maturation of the knee cap

Name: Irregular proximal tibial epiphyses
Def: Anomaly of the contour of the proximal epiphysis of the tibia such that its normally smooth appearance is irregular.

Name: Dorsal subluxation of ulna
Def: Partial dislocation of the ulna in the dorsal direction.

Name: Proximal femoral epiphysiolysis
Def: Slipped capital femoral epiphysis is defined as a posterior and inferior slippage of the proximal epiphysis of the femur onto the metaphysis (femoral neck), occurring through the physeal plate during the early adolescent growth spurt.
Synonym: Slipped end part of innermost thighbone

Name: Generalized bone demineralization
Def: A generalized decrease in bone mineral density.
Comment: The terms Osteopenia or Osteoporosis should be prefered to this term, which may be obsoleted in the future.

Name: Periosteal thickening of long tubular bones
Def: Thickening of the periosteum of long bone.

Name: Ankle flexion contracture
Def: A chronic loss of ankle joint motion due to structural changes in muscle, tendons, ligaments, or skin that prevent normal movement of the joints of the ankle.

Name: Limited shoulder movement
Def: A limitation of the range of movement of the shoulder joint.

Name: Thin long bone diaphyses
Def: Decreased width of the diaphysis of long bones.

Name: Anterior bowing of long bones
Def: An abnormal anterior curvature of a long bone.

Name: Abnormality of the pancreatic islet cells
Def: An abnormality of the islet of Langerhans, i.e., of the regions of the pancreas that contain its endocrine cells. These are the alpha cells, which produce glucagon, the beta cells, which produce insulin and amylin, the delta cells, which produce somatostatin, the PP cells, which produce pancreatic polypeptide, and the epsilon cells, which produce ghrelin.

Name: Abnormality of the alveolar ridges
Def: Any abnormality of the alveolar ridges (on the upper or lower jaws). The alveolar ridges contain the sockets (alveoli) of the teeth.
Synonym: Abnormality of alveolar processes of jaw

Name: Abnormality of the dental pulp
Def: An abnormality of the dental pulp.

Name: Premature loss of teeth
Def: Premature loss of teeth not related to trauma or neglect.

Name: Abnormality of primary teeth
Def: Any abnormality of the primary tooth.
Comment: Primary teeth are also called temporary teeth or deciduous teeth.

Name: Abnormality of dental morphology
Def: An abnormality of the morphology of the tooth.

Name: Abnormal number of teeth
Def: The presence of an altered number of of teeth.
Comment: Humans usually have 20 primary teeth (also called deciduous teeth) and 32 permanent teeth. This term comprises anomalies with too many or too few teeth.

Name: Agenesis of incisor
Def: Agenesis of incisor.
Comment: Failure of one or more incisors to develop.

Name: Abnormality of the dental root
Def: An abnormality of the dental root.

Name: Bowing of the long bones
Def: A bending or abnormal curvature of a long bone.
Comment: Curvatures of a long bone such as femur, tibia, or fibula.

Name: Bowing of the arm
Def: A bending or abnormal curvature affecting a long bone of the arm.

Name: Abnormality of the femoral metaphysis
Def: An anomaly of the femoral metaphysis.
Synonym: Abnormality of the wide portion of the femoral bone

Name: Abnormality of lower-limb metaphyses
Synonym: Abnormality of the wide portion of the lower-limb bone

Name: Abnormality of the tibial metaphysis
Synonym: Abnormality of the wide portion of shankbone
Abnormality of the wide portion of shinbone

Name: Aplasia/Hypoplasia of the fibula
Def: Absence or underdevelopment of the fibula.

Name: Aplasia/hypoplasia involving bones of the lower limbs
Def: Absence (due to failure to form) or underdevelopment of the bones of the lower limbs.

Name: Aplasia/Hypoplasia involving bones of the feet
Aplasia/Hypoplasia of the ulna
Def: Absence or underdevelopment of the ulna.
Synonym: Hypoplasia or unilateral/bilateral absence of ulna

Name: Aplasia/hypoplasia involving bones of the upper limbs
Def: Absence (due to failure to form) or underdevelopment of the bones of the upper limbs.
Synonym: Absent/small bones of the upper limbs
Absent/underdeveloped bones of the upper limbs

Name: Aplasia/Hypoplasia of the patella
Def: Absence or underdevelopment of the patella.

Name: Abnormality of femoral epiphysis
Def: An anomaly of a growth plate of a femur.

Name: Abnormality of lower limb epiphysis morphology
Def: An anomaly of one or more epiphyses of one or both legs.
Synonym: Abnormal shape of end part of lower limb end bone
Abnormality involving the epiphyses of the lower limbs

Name: Aplasia/Hypoplasia of the radius
Def: A small/hypoplastic or absent/aplastic radius.
Synonym: Absence or underdevelopment of the radius bone of the arm

Name: Aplasia/Hypoplasia involving the carpal bones
Def: Absence or underdevelopment of the carpal bones.

Name: Aplasia/hypoplasia involving forearm bones
Def: Absence (due to failure to form) or underdevelopment of one or more forearm bones.

Name: Anomaly of the limb diaphyses
Def: A structural abnormality of a diaphysis of the arm or leg.
Synonym: Abnormality involving the diaphyses of the limbs
Abnormality of shaft of long bone of the limbs

Name: Abnormality of limb epiphysis morphology
Def: An anomaly of one or more epiphyses of a limb.
Comment: An epiphysis is the expanded articular end of a long bone that developes from a secondary ossification center, and which during the period of growth is either entirely cartilaginous or is separated from the shaft by a cartilaginous disk.
Synonym: Abnormal shape of end part of limb bones
Abnormality involving the epiphyses of the limbs

Name: Aplasia/hypoplasia of the humerus
Def: Absence (due to failure to form) or underdevelopment of the humerus.
Synonym: Absent/small long bone in upper arm
Absent/underdeveloped long bone in upper arm

Name: Abnormality of tibial epiphyses
Synonym: Abnormality of end part of shinbone

Name: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease
Def: An anomaly that is characterized progressive airflow obstruction that is only partly reversible, inflammation in the airways, and systemic effects or comorbities.
Comment: COPD is usually conceptualized as a disease entity. It is heterogeneous histologically and pathogenically, and conventionally includes emphysema and chronic bronchitis, It is included as a phenotype term as COPD is often annotated as a feature of other diseases.

Name: Laryngeal stridor
Def: An abnormal high-pitched noisy sound, occurring during inhalation or exhalation caused by the incomplete obstruction in the throat.
Comment: The laryngeal stridor sound is usually heard during inspiratory phase, also called inspiratory stridor, and may accompanied by inspiratory difficulty in breathing. It may be due to abnormal flaccidity of the epiglottis or arytenoids.

Name: Alveolar proteinosis
Def: Abnormal accumulation of surfactant-like, periodic acid-schiff-positive lipoproteinaceous material in macrophages within the alveolar spaces and distal bronchioles. This results in gas exchange impairment leading to dyspnea and alveolar infiltrates.

Name: Pulmonary venous occlusion
Def: Substantial narrowing or blockage of small pulmonary veins as a result of disorganized smooth muscle hypertrophy and collagen matrix deposition.
Comment: This feature can be observed by histological examination of lung tissue. The feature can be seen in pulmonary veno-occlusive disease (PVOD). PVOD is characterised by diffuse occlusion of the pulmonary veins by fibrous tissue, pulmonary venous congestion and associated complications including severe pulmonary hypertension (pHTN), non-cardiogenic pulmonary oedema, hypoxia and right-ventricular failure. Clinical presentation is typically non-specific, including dyspnoea, fatigue and cough.

Name: Alveolar cell carcinoma
Def: Adenocarcinoma of the Bronchus.

Name: Pulmonary lymphangiectasia
Def: Abnormal dilatation of the pulmonary lymphatic vessels. Lymphatic fluid in the lung is derived from normal leakage of fluid out of the blood capillaries in the lung. In pulmonary lymphangiectasia, the pulmonary lymphatics are not properly connected and become dilated with fluid.

Name: Lymphoid interstitial pneumonia
Def: A lymphocyte-predominant infiltration of the lungs characterized by bibasilar pulmonary infiltrates with dense interstitial accumulations of lymphocytes and plasma cells.
Comment: Associated clinical manifestations often include fever, cough, and shortness of breath.

Name: Chronic lung disease
Def: According to the definitions of the American and British Thoracic Societies, including pulmonary functional tests, X-rays, and CT scans for items such as fibrosis, bronchiectasis, bullae, emphysema, nodular or lymphomatous abnormalities.

Name: Abnormal pulmonary lymphatics
Def: An abnormality of the pulmonary lymphatic chain.

Name: Interstitial pulmonary abnormality
Def: Abnormality of the lung parenchyma extending to the pulmonary interstitium and leading to diffuse pulmonary fibrosis.
Synonym: Abnormality in area between air sacs in lung

Name: Recurrent pneumonia
Def: An increased susceptibility to pneumonia as manifested by a history of recurrent episodes of pneumonia.
Comment: Recurrent pneumonia is defined as two or more episodes in a single year, or at least three episodes ever, with radiographic clearing of densities between occurrences.

Name: Recurrent intrapulmonary hemorrhage
Def: A recurrent hemorrhage occurring within the lung.

Name: Obstructive lung disease
Def: Obstruction of conducting airways of the lung.

Name: Recurrent bronchopulmonary infections
Def: An increased susceptibility to bronchopulmonary infections as manifested by a history of recurrent bronchopulmonary infections.
Synonym: Recurrent infections in bronchi and lungs

Name: Chronic obstructive airway disease from birth
Synonym: Chronic obstructive airway disease from birth

Name: Extrapulmonary sequestrum
Def: A type of pulmonary sequestration that is completely enclosed in its own pleural sac, occurring above, within, or below the diaphragm, and without communication with the tracheobronchial tree.
Comment: Extrapulmonary sequestra nearly all appear on the left side.

Name: Acute hepatic failure
Def: Hepatic failure refers to the inability of the liver to perform its normal synthetic and metabolic functions, which can result in coagulopathy and alteration in the mental status of a previously healthy individual. Hepatic failure is defined as acute if there is onset of encephalopathy within 8 weeks of the onset of symptoms in a patient with a previously healthy liver.

Name: Diffuse hepatic steatosis
Def: A diffuse form of hepatic steatosis.

Name: Decreased mitochondrial complex III activity in liver tissue
Def: Decreased activity of complex III of the mitochondrion in the liver.
Comment: Complex III, also known as ubiquinol-cytochrome c oxidoreductase or cytochrome bc1 complex, is a multisubunit integral membrane complex of the mitochondrial transport chain, which catalyzes electron transfer from ubiquinol to cytochrome c and couples this process to electrogenic translocation of protons across the mitochondrial inner membrane. Mitochondrial complex III is integrated in the inner mitochondrial membrane.

Name: Hepatic calcification
Def: The presence of abnormal calcium deposition in the liver.

Name: Biliary hyperplasia
Def: Hyperplasia of the biliary tree, as manifested by increased size of bile ducts, dilated lumen, and histologically by an increased number of epithelial cells or hyperplasia.

Name: Viral hepatitis
Def: Inflammation of the liver due to infection with a virus.

Name: Malformation of the hepatic ductal plate
Fluctuating hepatomegaly
Def: Intermittently increased size of the liver.

Name: Increased hepatocellular lipid droplets
Def: An abnormal increase in the amount of intracellular lipid droplets in hepatocytes.
Comment: Lipid droplets, rich in triglycerides and cholesterol esters, are cellular ipid storage organelles.

Name: Increased hepatic glycogen content
Def: An increase in the amount of glycogen stored in hepatocytes compared to normal.
Comment: Glycogen acts as secondary long-term energy storage in the liver and other organs. Its intracellular concentration can be increased in some disease states such as obesity.

Name: Reduced number of intrahepatic bile ducts
Def: The presence of reduced numbers of intrahepatic bile duct than normal.

Name: Acute hepatic steatosis
Def: An acute form of hepatic steatosis.

Name: Macronodular cirrhosis
Def: A type of cirrhosis characterized by the presence of large regenerative nodules.
Comment: In macronodular cirrhosis (post-necrotic cirrhosis), the nodules are larger than 3 mm.

Name: Prolonged neonatal jaundice
Def: Neonatal jaundice refers to a yellowing of the skin and other tissues of a newborn infant as a result of increased concentrations of bilirubin in the blood. Neonatal jaundice affects over half of all newborns to some extent in the first week of life. Prolonged neonatal jaundice is said to be present if the jaundice persists for longer than 14 days in term infants and 21 days in preterm infants.
Synonym: Prolonged yellowing of skin in newborn

Name: Portal fibrosis
Def: Fibroblast proliferation and fiber expansion from the portal areas to the lobule.
Comment: Portal fibrosis can be seen in viral hepatitis and other types of liver disease.

Name: Depletion of mitochondrial DNA in liver
Def: An abnormal reduction in the number of mitochondria in hepatocytes.

Name: Reye syndrome-like episodes
Def: Repeated occurrences of acute noninflammatory encephalopathy and fatty degenerative liver failure.
Comment: This feature has been observed in individuals withe mitochondrial DNA depletion syndrome-6 (MTDPS6), also known as Navajo neurohepatopathy [MIM:256810].

Name: Congenital pseudoarthrosis of the clavicle
Def: The two portions of the clavicle (corresponding to the two primary ossification centers of the clavicle) are connected by a fibrous bridge that is contiguous with the periosteum, and a synovial membrane develops, resulting in a clavicle with a bipartite appearance radiographically. Congenital pseudarthrosis of the clavicle generally presents as a painless mass or swelling over the clavicle.
Comment: In congenital pseudarthrosis of the clavicle, the two primary ossification centers fail to unite, probably due to a disruption of diaphyseal membranous ossification. See PMID:22295044, Figure 1, for the radiographic appearance of this feature.

Name: Straight clavicles
Def: An abnormally straight configuration of the clavicle, a tubular bone which normally is doubly curved .

Name: Premature sternal synostosis
Def: Prematurely closed sternal sutures.

Name: Absent glenoid fossa
Def: Lack of development of the glenoid fossa, also known as the glenoid cavity, which is the articular surface of the scapula that articulates with the head of the humerus.

Name: Scapulohumeral synostosis
Def: Bony fusion between the humerus and scapula, leading to an impairment in mobility of the affected shoulder joint.
Synonym: Fusion of shoulder blade to long bone in upper arm

Name: Diaphragmatic paralysis
Def: The presence of a paralyzed diaphragm.
Comment: Loss of the ability to move the diaphragm for respiratory motions. Patients with complete diaphragm paralysis complain of gross orthopnoea, disturbed sleep and early morning headaches. They have shortness of breath on minimal exertion and, because they sleep poorly, they experience daytime fatigue.

Name: Irregular ossification at anterior rib ends
Irregular chondrocostal junctions
Def: Irregular surface of the normally relatively smooth border between the distal part of the ribs and the costal cartilages, which are bars of hyaline cartilage that connect the ribs to the sternum.
Comment: The first seven pairs of ribs are connected with the sternum; the next three ribs are each articulated with the lower border of the cartilage of the preceding rib; the last two ribs have pointed extremities, which do not connect with the sternum.

Name: Precocious costochondral ossification
Def: Early ossification of the costochondral junction, which is the joint between the ribs and costal cartilage in the front of the rib cage.
Comment: The costal cartilage typically calcifies with advancing age and is therefore easier to identify on radiographs obtained in older patients.

Name: Midclavicular hypoplasia
Def: Underdevelopment of the middle portion of the clavicle.
Synonym: Underdeveloped middle portion of the collarbone

Name: Wide intermamillary distance
Def: A larger than usual distance between the left and right nipple.

Name: Decreased number of sternal ossification centers
Def: A less than normal number of sternal ossification centers. The sternum is initially formed from bilateral sternal plates that chondrify and begin to fuse with ribs at 10 weeks gestational age. Ossification starts in the manubrium and upper part of the sternal body at the 6th month, in the middle of the sternal body at the 7th month, in the lower part of the body during the 1st postnatal year and in the xiphoid process between years 5 and 18. The number of ossification centers vary up to six, and it is the ossification centers that are visualized by prenatal ultrasound. This term describes a reduction in the number of ossification centers compared with age-related norms.

Name: Absent in utero rib ossification
Def: Lack of formation and mineralization of the ribs in utero.

Name: Anterior rib punctate calcifications
Def: Deposition of calcium salts in point-like foci within the anterior portion of one or more ribs.

Name: Costochondral joint sclerosis
Def: Abnormal increase in density of the tissue at the costochondral junctions.

Name: Multifocal breast carcinoma
Def: Breast carcinoma that is bilateral or otherwise multifocal.

Name: Absent sternal ossification
Def: Lack of formation of mineralized bony tissue of the sternum.

Name: Hypoplastic distal segments of scapulae
Synonym: Small distal segments of the shoulder blade
Small outermost segments of shoulder blade
Underdeveloped outermost segments of shoulder blade

Name: Glenoid fossa hypoplasia
Def: Underdevelopment of the glenoid fossa, which is the cavity in the lateral part of the scapula which articulates with the head of the humerus.

Name: Osteosclerosis of ribs
Def: Osteosclerosis of ribs (increased density related to increased bone mass).

Name: Midclavicular aplasia
Def: Developmental defect resulting in congenital absence of the middle portion of the clavicle.

Name: Multiple rib fractures
Def: More than one fracture of the ribs.

Name: Thin clavicles
Def: Abnormally reduced diameter (cross section) of the clavicles.

Name: Costal cartilage calcification
Def: Calcification of the costal cartilages, which are bars of hyaline cartilage found at the anterior ends of the ribs which serve to prolong the ribs forward and contribute to the elasticity of the walls of the thorax.

Name: Costochondral pain
Def: Chest wall pain in the area of the costochondral junctions.
Comment: Costochondral pain is in the differential diagnosis of chest pain, being a relatively benign cause compared to myocardial ischemia. Costochondral pain can be caused by costochondritis.

Name: Thickening of the lateral border of the scapula
Synonym: Thickening of the lateral border of the shoulder blade

Name: Aplastic clavicle
Def: Absence of the clavicles as a developmental defect.

Name: Coat hanger sign of ribs
Def: An abnormal morphology of the ribs consisting of shorted, abnormally curved ribs. On posteroanterior chest radiography, the ribs show a curvature resembling that of a coat hanger (clothes hanger).
Comment: The coat hanger abnormality of the ribs is said to be a useful diagnostic marker of paternal uniparental disomy of chromosome 14.

Name: Prolonged QRS complex
Def: Increased time for the complex comprised of the Q wave, R wave, and S wave as measured by the electrocardiogram (EKG).. In adults, normal values are 0.06 - 0.10 sec.

Name: Granulomatous coronary arteritis
Def: Inflammation of the coronary arteries involving a granulomatous response, i.e., a non-specific inflammatory response involving granulomas, defined as a compact organized collection of mature mononuclear phagocytes including epithelioid and giant cells.
Comment: A granuloma is a compact (organized) collection of mature mononuclear phagocytes (macrophages and/or epithelioid cells) which may or may not be accompanied by accessory features such as necrosis or the infiltration of other inflammatory leukocytes (Adams DO. The granulomatous inflammatory response. Am J Pathol 1976:84:163-192).

Name: Ventricular extrasystoles
Def: Premature ventricular contractions (PVC) or ventricular extrasystoles are premature contractions of the heart that arise in response to an impulse in the ventricles rather than the normal impulse from the sinoatrial (SA) node.
Comment: A premature ventricular contraction may be perceived as a skipped beat or as palpitations.

Name: Abnormal ventricular filling
Def: An abnormality of filling of a ventricle with blood during diastole.
Comment: Two diastolic properties, the rate of ventricular relaxation and the ventricular compliance are especially important determinants of ventricular filling.

Name: Ventricular preexcitation with multiple accessory pathways
Def: A form of ventricular preexcitation due to the presence of multiple accessory pathways for cardiac conduction.

Name: Endocardial fibrosis
Def: The presence of excessive connective tissue in the endocardium.

Name: Aortic tortuosity
Def: Abnormal tortuous (i.e., twisted) form of the aorta.

Name: Bacterial endocarditis
Def: A bacterial infection of the endocardium, the inner layer of the heart, which usually involves the heart valves.

Name: Myocardial calcification
Def: Calcium deposition in the myocardium.
Comment: Calcification affecting the muscle layer of the heart.

Name: Short chordae tendineae of the tricuspid valve
Def: Abnormally short chordae tendineae of the tricuspid valve.
Comment: The chordae tendineae connect the papillary muscles to the tricuspid valve and the mitral valve.

Name: Myocardial steatosis
Def: Steatosis in the myocardium.

Name: Early progressive calcific cardiac valvular disease
Atrioventricular canal defect
Def: A defect of the atrioventricular septum of the heart.
Comment: During atrioventricular valvuloseptal morphogenesis, the endocardial cushions expand as they are infiltrated by extracellular matrix secreted from the surrounding myocardium. The cushions then fuse and are remodeled to form the atrioventricular valves and septa. Failure of this process results in AVSD, with the degree of severity dependent on the stage at which the developmental failure occurs. AVSD are a spectrum of cardiac malformations that result in a persistent common atrioventricular canal.

Name: Dilatation of the ventricular cavity
Def: A localized outpouching of ventricular cavity that is generally associated with dyskinesia and paradoxical expansion during systole.
Comment: Aneurysm is considered a severe form of dilatation. Ventricular aneurysms may have rim of calcium in the affected regions of the ventricular wall (which can become fibrotic). Thromboembolism is a potential complication. Ventricular aneurysms can be diagnosed by ventriculography.

Name: Premature atrial contractions
Def: A type of cardiac arrhythmia with premature atrial contractions or beats caused by signals originating from ectopic atrial sites.

Name: Coronary artery dissection
Def: Acute occurrence of a dissection (tear within the tunica intima and entry of blood into the tunica media) of a coronary artery.

Name: Abnormal coronary artery morphology
Def: Any structural abnormality of the coronary arteries.

Name: Abnormal atrioventricular valve morphology
Def: An abnormality of an atrioventricular valve.

Name: Abnormality of the hepatic vasculature
Def: An abnormality of the hepatic vasculature.

Name: Aplasia/Hypoplasia of the clavicles
Def: Absence or underdevelopment of the clavicles (collar bones).

Name: Aplasia/Hypoplasia involving bones of the thorax
Acute lymphoblastic leukemia
Def: A form of acute leukemia characterized by excess lympoblasts.

Name: Pancreatic adenocarcinoma
Def: The presence of an adenocarcinoma of the pancreas.

Name: T-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemias
Def: Acute lymphoblastic leukemia of T-cell origin. It comprises about 15% of childhood cases and 25% of adult cases. It is more common in males than females.

Name: Follicular thyroid carcinoma
Def: The presence of an follicular adenocarcinoma of the thyroid gland.

Name: Papillary renal cell carcinoma type 2
Def: A type of papillary renal cell carcinoma in which the papillae are covered by large eosinophilic cells with pleomorphic nuclei, prominent nucleoli, and nuclear pseudostratification.
Comment: Papillary renal cell carcinoma type 2 is a common feature of hereditary leiomyomatosis and renal cell cancer; HLRCC (OMIM 150800).

Name: Acute megakaryocytic leukemia
Def: A rare subtype of acute myeloid leukemia evolving from primitive megakaryoblasts.

Name: Renal cortical adenoma
Def: The presence of an adenoma in the cortex of the kidney.

Name: Extraadrenal pheochromocytoma
Def: Pheochromocytoma not originating from the adrenal medulla but from another source such as from chromaffin cells in or about sympathetic ganglia.

Name: Squamous cell carcinoma of the skin
Def: Squamous cell carcinoma of the skin is a malignant tumor of squamous epithelium.

Name: Transitional cell carcinoma of the bladder
Def: The presence of a carcinoma of the urinary bladder with origin in a transitional epithelial cell.

Name: Adrenocortical carcinoma
Def: A malignant neoplasm of the adrenal cortex that may produce hormones such as cortisol, aldosterone, estrogen, or testosterone.

Name: Adrenal pheochromocytoma
Def: Pheochromocytoma originating from the adrenal medulla.

Name: Neoplasm of the stomach
Def: A tumor (abnormal growth of tissue) of the stomach.

Name: Cutaneous leiomyosarcoma
Def: The presence of leiomyosarcoma of the skin.

Name: Malignant genitourinary tract tumor
Def: The presence of a malignant neoplasm of the genital system.

Name: Renal pelvic carcinoma
Def: The presence of a carcinoma in the renal pelvis.

Name: Chondrosarcoma
Def: A slowly growing malignant neoplasm derived from cartilage cells.

Name: Papillary renal cell carcinoma
Def: The presence of renal cell carcinoma in the renal papilla.

Name: Pituitary prolactin cell adenoma
Def: A type of pituitary adenoma originating in prolactin secreting cells. This kind of adenoma is characterized by overproduction of prolactin, and may cause loss of menstrual periods and breast milk production in women.

Name: Clear cell renal cell carcinoma
Def: A subtype of renal cell carcinoma thought to originate from mature renal tubular cells in the proximal tubule of the nehpron.

Name: Duodenal adenocarcinoma
Def: A malignant epithelial tumor with a glandular organization that originates in the duodenum.

Name: Renal angiomyolipoma
Def: A benign renal neoplasm composed of fat, vascular, and smooth muscle elements.
Comment: Angiomyolipoma is a benign renal neoplasm composed of fat, vascular, and smooth muscle elements.

Name: Ovarian papillary adenocarcinoma
Def: The presence of a papillary adenocarcinoma of the ovary.

Name: Multiple myeloma
Def: A malignant plasma cell tumor growing within soft tissue or within the skeleton.

Name: Benign genitourinary tract neoplasm
Def: A non-malignant neoplasm of the genitourinary system.

Name: Parathyroid carcinoma
Def: A malignancy of the parathyroid glands. Parathyroid carcinoma usually secretes parathyroid hormone, leading to hyperparathyroidism.

Name: Hurthle cell thyroid adenoma
Def: A kind of thyroid adenoma characterized by the presence of oxyphil cells.
Comment: Oxyphil cells of thyroid, defined by the Cell Ontology as oncocytes located in the thyroid, are also known as Hurthle cells.

Name: Paranasal sinus hypoplasia
Def: Underdevelopment of the paranasal sinuses.

Name: Limb-girdle muscular dystrophy
Def: Muscular dystrophy affecting the muscles of the limb girdle (the hips and shoulders).

Name: Loss of ability to walk in first decade
Synonym: Loss of ability to walk in first decade

Name: Basal ganglia cysts
Synonym: Cystic lesions in the basal ganglia

Name: Abnormal anterior horn cell morphology
Def: Any anomaly of the anterior horn cell.
Comment: Anterior horn cells are efferent neurons that passes from the central nervous system or a ganglion toward or to a muscle. They conduct nerve impulses that lead to movement of muscles.
Synonym: Abnormality of the anterior horn cell
Abnormality of the anterior horn cells
Anomaly of the anterior horn cells

Name: Cerebral hypomyelination
Def: Reduced amount of myelin in the nervous system resulting from defective myelinogenesis in the white matter of the central nervous system.

Name: White mater abnormalities in the posterior periventricular region
Aplasia/Hypoplasia of the cerebellar vermis
Def: Absence or underdevelopment of the vermis of cerebellum.

Name: 4-layered lissencephaly
Def: A form of lissencephaly in which the cortex is thickened and has four more or less disorganized layers rather than six normal layers resulting from incomplete neuronal migration during brain development. At neuropathological examination, a 4-layered cortex consists of an upper molecular layer, a second thin cellular layer containing pyramidal neurons usually observed in layer V, a third pale poorly cellular layer and a fourth thick deep layer made up of neurons which had failed to migrate. Radiologocally would manifest as agyria or pachygyria with cortical thickness greater than 10 mm.

Name: Frontal polymicrogyria
Def: A type of polymicrogyria with a gradient of severity (anterior more severe than posterior) extending from frontal poles posteriorly to precentral gyrus and inferiorly to frontal operculum.

Name: Pallor of dorsal columns of the spinal cord
Severe muscular hypotonia
Def: A severe degree of muscular hypotonia characterized by markedly reduced muscle tone.

Name: obsolete Severe neonatal hypotonia in males
Developmental stagnation at onset of seizures
Def: A cessation of the development of a child in the areas of motor skills, speech and language, cognitive skills, and social and/or emotional skills, following the onset of epilepsy.

Name: Congenital Horner syndrome
Def: A type of Horner syndrome with congenital onset.

Name: Absent patellar reflexes
Def: Absence of the knee jerk reflex, which can normally be elicited by tapping the patellar tendon with a reflex hammer just below the patella.

Name: Hypoplasia of the ventral pons
Def: Underdevelopment of the ventral portion of the pons.

Name: Symmetric spinal nerve root neurofibromas
Def: Multiple neurofibromas of the spinal nerve roots with a symmetric distribution.
Synonym: Spinal nerve root neurofibromas, symmetric, multiple

Name: Episodic generalized hypotonia
Def: The occurrence of repeated episodes of generalized muscular hypotonia.

Name: Cerebellar vermis atrophy
Def: Wasting (atrophy) of the vermis of cerebellum.
Comment: This sign can be visualized with brain MRI.

Name: Impaired distal proprioception
Def: A loss or impairment of the sensation of the relative position of parts of the body and joint position occuring at distal joints.

Name: Severe expressive language delay
Def: A severe delay in the acquisition of the ability to use language to communicate needs, wishes, or thoughts.

Name: Sensorimotor polyneuropathy affecting arms more than legs
Lobar holoprosencephaly
Def: A type of holoprosencephaly in which most of the right and left cerebral hemispheres and lateral ventricles are separated but the most rostral aspect of the telencephalon, the frontal lobes, are fused, especially ventrally.

Name: Cerebral hypoplasia
Def: Underdevelopment of the cerebrum.

Name: Symmetrical progressive peripheral demyelination
Def: A symmetric and progressive loss of myelin from the internode regions along myelinated nerve fibers of the peripheral nervous system.

Name: Pontocerebellar atrophy
Def: Atrophy affecting the pons and the cerebellum.

Name: Cerebellar hemangioblastoma
Def: A hemangioblastoma of the cerebellum.

Name: Diffuse peripheral demyelination
Def: A diffuse loss of myelin from the internode regions along myelinated nerve fibers of the peripheral nervous system.

Name: Impaired distal vibration sensation
Def: A decrease in the ability to perceive vibration in the distal portions of the limbs.

Name: Intellectual disability, progressive
Def: The term progressive intellectual disability should be used if intelligence decreases/deteriorates over time.

Name: Intellectual disability, borderline
Def: Borderline intellectual disability is defined as an intelligence quotient (IQ) in the range of 70-85.
Comment: We choose to define the concept of borderline intellectual disability onthe basis of the commonly used range of 70-85 (IQ), but note that in DSM-5, IQ boundaries are no longer part of the classification.

Name: Frontotemporal cerebral atrophy
Def: Atrophy (wasting, decrease in size of cells or tissue) affecting the frontotemporal cerebrum.

Name: Congenital intracerebral calcification
Def: The presence of calcium deposition within brain structures that is present already at the time of birth.

Name: Frontal cortical atrophy
Def: Atrophy of the frontal cortex.

Name: Intraaxonal accumulation of curvilinear autofluorescent lipopigment storage material
Def: Curvilinear intracellular accumulation of autofluorescent lipopigment storage material within axons.

Name: Abnormal aggressive, impulsive or violent behavior
Axial muscle stiffness
Def: Stiffness (a condition in which muscles cannot be moved quickly without accompanying pain or spasm) of the axial musculature.

Name: Unilateral polymicrogyria
Def: Excessive number of small gyri (convolutions) on the surface of one side of the brain.

Name: Hypoglycemic encephalopathy
Def: Brain damage related to a lowering of blood glucose below a critical level (around 30 mg/dl), which may lead to confusion, lethargy and delirium followed by seizures and coma. Prolonged hypoglycemia may lead to irreversible brain damage.

Name: Frontoparietal cortical dysplasia
Def: The presence of developmental dysplasia of the cortex of frontal lobe and the cortex of parietal lobe.

Name: Congenital nystagmus
Def: Nystagmus dating from or present at birth.

Name: Impaired distal tactile sensation
Def: A reduced sense of touch (tactile sensation) on the skin of the distal limbs. This is usually tested with a wisp of cotton or a fine camel's hair brush, by asking patients to say 'now' each time they feel the stimulus.

Name: Impaired vibration sensation at ankles
Def: A decrease in the ability to perceive vibration at the ankles. Clinically, this is usually tested with a tuning fork which vibrates at 128 Hz and is applied to the malleoli of the ankles.

Name: Abolished vibration sense
Def: A complete loss of the ability to perceive vibration.

Name: Recurrent meningitis
Def: An increased susceptibility to meningitis as manifested by a medical history of recurrent episodes of meningitis.

Name: Olivopontocerebellar hypoplasia
Def: Hypoplasia of the cerebellum, pontine nuclei, and inferior olivary nucleus.

Name: Abnormal auditory evoked potentials
Def: An abnormality of the auditory evoked potentials, which are used to trace the signal generated by a sound, from the cochlear nerve, through the lateral lemniscus, to the medial geniculate nucleus, and to the cortex.
Comment: Auditory brainstem response audiometry typically uses a click stimulus that generates a response from the basilar region of the cochlea.

Name: Proximal spinal muscular atrophy
Def: Proximal spinal muscular atrophy, i.e., muscular weakness and atrophy related to loss of the motor neurons of the spinal cord and brainstem.

Name: Choroid plexus calcification
Def: The presence of calcium deposition in the choroid plexus.

Name: Gait instability, worse in the dark
Synonym: Unstable walking, worse in the dark

Name: Necrotizing encephalopathy
Def: A type of encephalopathy (brain disease, damage, or malfunction accompanied by an altered mental state) that is characterized by evidence of necrosis of brain tissue.
Comment: The disease acute necrotizing encephalopathy is characterized by acute onset encephalopathy with rapid, progressive neurologic deterioration, seizures and symmetric multifocal brain lesions. This term is kept for convenience. For new annotations, it is recommended that the specific phenotypic abnormalities be noted.

Name: Sleep-wake cycle disturbance
Def: Any abnormal alteration of an individual's circadian rhythm that affects the timing of sleeping and being awake.

Name: Progressive leukoencephalopathy
Def: Leukoencephalopathy that gets more severe with time.

Name: Distal sensory loss of all modalities
Alobar holoprosencephaly
Def: A type of holoprosencephaly characterized by the presence of a single ventricle and no separation of the cerebral hemisphere. The single midline ventricle is often greatly enlarged.

Name: Dysplastic corpus callosum
Def: Dysplasia and dysgenesis of the corpus callosum are nonspecific descriptions that imply defective development of the corpus callosum. The term dysplasia is applied when the morphology of the corpus callosum is altered as a congenital trait. For instance, the corpus callosum may be hump-shaped, kinked, or a striped corpus callosum that lacks an anatomically distinct genu and splenium.

Name: Myelin-dependent gliosis
Def: A type of gliosis that occurs in the vicinity of injured neurons.

Name: Basal ganglia gliosis
Def: Focal proliferation of glial cells in the basal ganglia.
Comment: Gliosis refers to a proliferation of astrocytes in an area of damage of nervous tissue.

Name: Loss of Purkinje cells in the cerebellar vermis
Motor axonal neuropathy
Def: Progressive impairment of function of motor axons with muscle weakness, atrophy, and cramps. The deficits are length-dependent, meaning that muscles innervated by the longest nerves are affected first, so that for instance the arms are affected at a later age than the onset of deficits involving the lower leg.
Comment: Distal motor neuropathy is a bundled term that should not be used if more detailed information about the phenotype is available.

Name: Cavitation of the basal ganglia
Def: The formation of small cavities in the tissue of the basal ganglia.
Comment: This feature can be observed in tissue upon autopsy or in magnetic resonance tomography (MRI) images.

Name: Poor fine motor coordination
Def: An abnormality of the ability (skills) to perform a precise movement of small muscles with the intent to perform a specific act. Fine motor skills are required to mediate movements of the wrists, hands, fingers, feet, and toes.

Name: Fourth cranial nerve palsy
Def: Paralysis of the fourth cranial (trochlear) nerve manifested as weakness of the superior oblique muscle which causes vertical diplopia that is maximal when the affected eye is adducted and directed inferiorly.
Comment: The fourth cranial nerve crosses as it exits the midbrain dorsally and may be injured along its course through the intracranial space, cavernous sinus, superior orbital fissure, or orbit.

Name: Poor gross motor coordination
Def: An abnormality of the ability (skills) to perform a precise movement of large muscles with the intent to perform a specific act. Gross motor skills are required to mediate movements of the arms, legs, and other large body parts.

Name: Attention deficit hyperactivity disorder
Def: Attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) manifests at age 2-3 years or by first grade at the latest. The main symptoms are distractibility, impulsivity, hyperactivity, and often trouble organizing tasks and projects, difficulty going to sleep, and social problems from being aggressive, loud, or impatient.

Name: Pain insensitivity
Def: Inability to perceive painful stimuli.
Comment: The word Anesthesia is occasionally used to refer to lack of pain sensation, although it is more usually used to denote a medical procedure design to relieve pain.

Name: Antenatal intracerebral hemorrhage
Def: Cerebral hemorrhage that occurs before birth.

Name: Pseudobulbar paralysis
Def: Bilateral impairment of the function of the cranial nerves 9-12, which control musculature involved in eating, swallowing, and speech. Pseudobulbar paralysis is characterized clinically by dysarthria, dysphonia, and dysphagia with bifacial paralysis, and may be accompanied by Pseudobulbar behavioral symptoms such as enforced crying and laughing.

Name: Poorly formed metencephalon
Def: A morphological abnormality of the metencephalon.
Comment: The metencephalon comprises the pons and the cerebellum; contains a portion of the fourth ventricle; and the trigeminal nerve, abducens nerve, facial nerve, and a portion of the vestibulocochlear nerve. The metencephalon is part of the hindbrain.

Name: Cerebral berry aneurysm
Def: A small, sac-like aneurysm (outpouching) of a cerebral blood vessel.
Comment: Saccular aneurysms are often said to have a berry-shaped appearance, whence the name.

Name: Cerebellar dysplasia
Def: The presence of dysplasia (abnormal growth or development) of the cerebellum. Cerebellar dysplasia is a neuroimaging finding that describes abnormalities of both the cerebellar cortex and white matter and is associated with variable neurodevelopmental outcome.
Comment: Any part of the cerebellum can be dysplastic, from small focal regions within one hemisphere to abnormal foliation throughout the cerebellum. Hypoplastic cerebella are frequently also dysmorphic, as observed in tubulinopathies and cobblestone malformations.

Name: Symmetric lesions of the basal ganglia
Chronic lymphocytic meningitis
Def: Meningitis that persists for more than 4 weeks, and lymphocytes are present in the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF).

Name: Atrophy of the dentate nucleus
Def: Partial or complete wasting (loss) of dentate nucleus.

Name: Large basal ganglia
Def: Increased size of the basal ganglia.

Name: Generalized cerebral atrophy/hypoplasia
Def: Generalized atrophy or hypoplasia of the cerebrum.

Name: Aplasia of the inferior half of the cerebellar vermis
Synonym: Absent inferior half of the cerebellar vermis

Name: Progressive language deterioration
Def: Progressive loss of previously present language abilities.

Name: Disorganization of the anterior cerebellar vermis
Proximal limb muscle stiffness
Comment: Removed logical definition that used an anonymous class. Requested new term in UBERON: proximal musculature of limb

Name: Distal peripheral sensory neuropathy
