Def: Peripheral sensory neuropathy affecting primarily distal sensation.

Name: Inferior vermis hypoplasia
Def: Underdevelopment of the inferior portion of the vermis of cerebellum.

Name: Thick corpus callosum
Def: Increased vertical dimension of the corpus callosum. This feature can be visualized by sagittal sections on magnetic resonance tomography imaging of the brain.

Name: Extrapyramidal muscular rigidity
Def: Muscular rigidity (continuous contraction of muscles with constant resistance to passive movement).
Comment: This is a classic type of extrapyramidal movement disorder.

Name: Decreased amplitude of sensory action potentials
Def: A reduction in the amplitude of sensory nerve action potential. This feature is measured by nerve conduction studies.

Name: Dilated third ventricle
Def: An increase in size of the third ventricle.
Comment: The thrid ventricle is midline between the two lateral ventricles, and it communicates between them and the fourth ventricle.

Name: Facial-lingual fasciculations
Def: Fasciculations affecting the tongue muscle and the musculature of the face.

Name: Frontoparietal polymicrogyria
Def: An excessive number of small gyri (convolutions) on the surface of the brain in the frontoparietal region.

Name: Paroxysmal choreoathetosis
Def: Episodes of choreoathetosis that can occur following triggers such as quick voluntary movements.

Name: Arnold-Chiari type I malformation
Def: Arnold-Chiari type I malformation refers to a relatively mild degree of herniation of the posteroinferior region of the cerebellum (the cerebellar tonsils) into the cervical canal with little or no displacement of the fourth ventricle.

Name: Hypointensity of cerebral white matter on MRI
Def: A darker than expected signal on magnetic resonance imaging emanating from the cerebral white matter.

Name: Infantile encephalopathy
Def: Encephalopathy with onset in the infantile period.

Name: Segmental peripheral demyelination
Def: A loss of myelin from the internode regions along myelinated nerve fibers from segments of the peripheral nervous system.

Name: Demyelinating peripheral neuropathy
Def: Demyelinating neuropathy is characterized by slow nerve conduction velocities with reduced amplitudes of sensory/motor nerve conduction and prolonged distal latencies.

Name: Temporal cortical atrophy
Def: Atrophy of the temporal cortex.

Name: Subcortical dementia
Def: A particular type of dementia characterized by a pattern of mental defects consisting prominently of forgetfulness, slowness of thought processes, and personality or mood change.

Name: Proximal amyotrophy
Def: Amyotrophy (muscular atrophy) affecting the proximal musculature.
Comment: Proximal amyotrophy usually has a roughly symmetric distribution.
Synonym: Wasting of muscles near the body

Name: Acute demyelinating polyneuropathy
Def: Acute progressive areflexic weakness and mild sensory changes resulting from myelin breakdown and axonal degeneration.
Comment: This is a bundled term used to refer to the symptomatology associated with the Guillain-Barre syndrome.

Name: Pallidal degeneration
Def: Neurodegeneration involving the globus pallidus,a part of the basal ganglia that is involved in the regulation of voluntary movement.

Name: Sensorimotor neuropathy
Synonym: Nerve damage causing decreased feeling and movement

Name: Distal upper limb amyotrophy
Def: Muscular atrophy of distal arm muscles.

Name: Asymmetric limb muscle stiffness
Def: Stiffness of the limbs (a condition in which muscles cannot be moved quickly without accompanying pain or spasm) occurring in an asymmetric pattern.

Name: Progressive extrapyramidal muscular rigidity
Def: A progressive degree of muscular rigidity (continuous contraction of muscles with constant resistance to passive movement).

Name: Diffuse demyelination of the cerebral white matter
Def: A diffuse loss of myelin from nerve fibers in the central nervous system.

Name: obsolete Corticospinal tract disease in lower limbs
Periventricular heterotopia
Def: A form of gray matter heterotopia were the mislocalized gray matter is typically located periventricularly, also sometimes called subependymal heterotopia. Periventricular means beside the ventricles. This is by far the most common location for heterotopia. Subependymal heterotopia present in a wide array of variations. There can be a small single node or a large number of nodes, can exist on either or both sides of the brain at any point along the higher ventricle margins, can be small or large, single or multiple, and can form a small node or a large wavy or curved mass.
Comment: Periventricular gray matter heterotopia can be seen for example in patients with Smith-Lemli-Opitz-Syndrome.

Name: Paroxysmal dyskinesia
Def: Episodic bouts of involuntary movements with dystonic, choreic, ballistic movements, or a combination thereof. There is no loss of consciousness during the attacks.

Name: Absent smooth pursuit
Def: A complete lack of the ability to track objects with the ocular smooth pursuit system, a class of rather slow eye movements that minimizes retinal target motion.

Name: Interosseus muscle atrophy
Def: Atrophy of the interosseus muscles (including the palmar interossei that lie on the anterior aspect of the metacarpals, the dorsal interosseus muscles of the hand, which lie between the intercarpals, the plantar interosseus muscles, which lie underneath the metatarsal bones, and the dorsal interossei, which are located between the metatarsal bones.
Comment: This term needs disambiguation. Palmar, plantar, or dorsal interosseus muscles.

Name: Peripheral hypomyelination
Def: Reduced amount of myelin in the nervous system resulting from defective myelinogenesis in the peripheral nervous system.
Comment: This finding can be demonstrated by nerve biopsy.

Name: Focal T2 hyperintense basal ganglia lesion
Def: A lighter than expected T2 signal on magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) of the basal ganglia. This term refers to a localized hyperintensity affecting a particular region of the basal ganglia.
Synonym: Hyperintense lesions in the basal ganglia on MRI

Name: Focal lissencephaly
Def: A congenital absence of the convolutions of the cerebral cortex and a poorly formed sylvian fissure that affects a particular part of the cortex.

Name: Congenital facial diplegia
Def: Facial diplegia (that is, bilateral facial palsy) with congenital onset.

Name: Neuronal loss in the cerebral cortex
Generalized tonic-clonic seizures on awakening
Def: Generalized tonic-clonic seizures on awakening are a form of Generalized tonic-clonic seizures that occur upon awaking.

Name: Cerebral artery atherosclerosis
Def: Atherosclerosis (HP:0002621) of a cerebral artery.

Name: Diffuse white matter abnormalities
Comment: This finding is demonstrated by cerebral computer tomography or magnetic resonance imaging.

Name: Hemimegalencephaly
Def: Enlargement of all or parts of one cerebral hemisphere.
Comment: The affected hemisphere may have focal or diffuse neuronal migration defects, with areas of polymicrogyria, pachygyria, and heterotopia.

Name: Photosensitive tonic-clonic seizures
Def: Generalized tonic-clonic seizures that are triggered by flashing or flickering light.

Name: Irregular myelin loops
Def: Presence of irregular redundant loops of focally folded myelin in a peripheral nerve.

Name: Facial paralysis
Def: Complete loss of ability to move facial muscles innervated by the facial nerve (i.e., the seventh cranial nerve).
Comment: Facial paralysis can be caused by compression of the facial nerve.The main difference between facial paralysis and Palsy is cause for the paralysis can be identified, be it a tumor, infection, or nerve damage. Facial paralysis, in most cases, also appears more permanent than Bell's Palsy, with cases lasting for years to life if a patient doesn't seek treatment.

Name: Lower limb amyotrophy
Def: Muscular atrophy affecting the lower limb.

Name: Periodic hyperkalemic paralysis
Def: Episodes of muscle weakness associated with elevated levels of potassium in the blood.

Name: Demyelinating motor neuropathy
Def: Demyelination of peripheral motor nerves.
Comment: Demyelinating motor neuropathy demonstrates slow motor nerve conduction velocities with reduced amplitudes of motor nerve conduction and prolonged distal latencies.

Name: Macrogyria
Def: Increased size of cerebral gyri, often associated with a moderate reduction in the number of sulci of the cerebrum.

Name: Intracerebral periventricular calcifications
Def: The presence of calcium deposition in the cerebral white matter surrounding the cerebral ventricles.

Name: Decreased distal sensory nerve action potential
Def: A reduction in the amplitude of sensory nerve action potential in distal nerve segments. This feature is measured by nerve conduction studies.

Name: Spinocerebellar tract disease in lower limbs
Clusters of axonal regeneration
Def: Groups of small caliber axons in peripheral nerve biospies indicative of axonal regeneration.

Name: Progressive gait ataxia
Def: A type of gait ataxia displaying progression of clinical severity.

Name: Decreased number of small peripheral myelinated nerve fibers
Recurrent external ophthalmoplegia
Def: Alternating and recurrent weakness of the external ocular muscles.

Name: Abnormal pyramidal sign
Def: Functional neurological abnormalities related to dysfunction of the pyramidal tract.
Comment: Presence of these signs can indicate affection of the corticospinal (pyramidal) tracts.

Name: Severe demyelination of the white matter
Def: A severe loss of myelin from nerve fibers in the central nervous system.

Name: Type II lissencephaly
Def: A form of lissencephaly characterized by an uneven cortical surface with a so called 'cobblestone' appearace. There are no distinguishable cortical layers.

Name: Symmetric peripheral demyelination
Def: A symmetric loss of myelin from the internode regions along myelinated nerve fibers of the peripheral nervous system.

Name: Spinocerebellar atrophy
Def: Atrophy affecting the cerebellum and the spinocerebellar tracts of the spinal cord.

Name: Absent mesencephalon
Def: Agenesis of the midbrain.
Comment: Midbrain and mesencephalon are synonymous.

Name: Cerebral dysmyelination
Def: Defective structure and function of myelin sheaths of the white matter of the brain.

Name: Chronic axonal neuropathy
Def: An abnormality characterized by chronic impairment of the normal functioning of the axons.
Comment: This feature is assayed with sural nerve biopsy and is generally taken to be indicative of neuropathy in other peripheral nerves.

Name: Spinal muscular atrophy
Def: Muscular weakness and atrophy related to loss of the motor neurons of the spinal cord and brainstem.

Name: Atypical absence seizure
Def: An atypical absence seizure has less abrupt onset and offset of loss of awareness than typical absence seizures. They are often associated with other features such as loss of muscle tone of the head, trunk or limbs (often a gradual slump) and subtle myoclonic jerks. Atypical absence seizures often occur in individuals with intellectual impairment.The loss of awareness may be minimal with the patient continuing an activity, but more slowly or with mistakes.

Name: Recurrent bacterial meningitis
Def: An increased susceptibility to bacterial meningitis as manifested by a medical history of recurrent episodes of bacterial meningitis.

Name: Paucity of anterior horn motor neurons
Developmental stagnation
Def: A cessation of the development of a child in the areas of motor skills, speech and language, cognitive skills, and social and/or emotional skills.

Name: Facial palsy secondary to cranial hyperostosis
Def: Paralysis of the facial nerves on the basis of overgrowth of the cranial bones causing impingement upon the seventh cranial nerve.
Synonym: Facial palsy caused by enlargement of cranial bones
Facial palsy caused by excessive growth of facial bones
Facial palsy caused by overgrowth of cranial bones
Facial palsy secondary to hypertrophy of cranial bones

Name: Horizontal jerk nystagmus
Def: Nystagmus consisting of horizontal to-and-fro eye movements, in which the movement in one direction is faster than in the other.
Comment: Pendular nystagmus refers to the situation in which the eye appeared to oscillate with equal speed in either direction, in contrast to jerk nystagmus, in which the movement in one direction is faster than in the other.

Name: Limb fasciculations
Def: Fasciculations affecting the musculature of the arms and legs.

Name: Posterior fossa cyst
Def: A discrete posterior fossa cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) collection that does not communicate directly with the fourth ventricle.

Name: CNS demyelination
Def: A loss of myelin from nerve fibers in the central nervous system.
Comment: CNS demyelination affects the white matter, which consists mostly of axons with their envelope of myelin, along with two types of neuroglia: oligo-dendrocytes and astrocytes.

Name: Deep white matter hypodensities
Def: Multiple areas of darker than expected signal on magnetic resonance imaging emanating from the deep cerebral white matter.
Comment: See also defintion for "Periventricular white matter hypodensities". These two entities are in contra-distinction to each other.

Name: Generalized dystonia
Def: A type of dystonia that affects all or most of the body.

Name: Impaired pain sensation
Def: Reduced ability to perceive painful stimuli.

Name: Hemifacial seizures
Def: Focal clonic seizures affecting one side of the face.
Comment: Used to describe rolandic seizures in familial epilepsy syndromes, such as Autosomal recessive rolandic epilepsy with paroxysmal exercise-induced dystonia and writer's cramp (PMID 10072049).

Name: Hypoplasia of the frontal lobes
Def: Underdevelopment of the frontal lobe of the cerebrum.

Name: Generalized tonic-clonic seizures with focal onset
Def: Bilateral convulsive seizures are focal seizure with secondary bilateral motor phenomena, not primary generalized seizures.

Name: Recurrent encephalopathy
Def: Recurrent episodes of brain dysfunction that may be triggered by factors such as metabolic disturbances or infections.

Name: Hypermetric saccades
Def: A saccade that overshoots the target with the dynamic saccade.

Name: Lower limb muscle weakness
Def: Weakness of the muscles of the legs.
Comment: Inability to perform rapid, alternating movements.

Name: Diffuse swelling of cerebral white matter
Abnormal morphology of the limbic system
Def: Any structural anomaly of the limbic system, a set of midline structures surrounding the brainstem of the mammalian brain, originally described anatomically, e.g., hippocampal formation, amygdala, hypothalamus, cingulate cortex. Although the original designation was anatomical, the limbic system has come to be associated with the system in the brain subserving emotional functions. As such, it is very poorly defined and doesn't correspond closely to the anatomical meaning any longer. [BirnLex].

Name: Atrophy/Degeneration involving the spinal cord
Synonym: Atrophic and degenerative changes in the spinal cord

Name: Upper limb postural tremor
Def: A type of tremors that is triggered by holding an arm in a fixed position.

Name: Focal-onset seizure
Def: Seizures of which initial semiology indicates, or is consistent with, initial activation of only part of one cerebral hemisphere.
Comment: Partial seizures can be classified as simple (consciousness is maintained) or complex (consciousness is impaired or lost).
Synonym: Seizure affecting one half of brain

Name: Abnormality of the pons
Def: An abnormality of the pons.
Comment: The pons is the portion of the brainstem superior to the medulla oblongata.

Name: Atrophy/Degeneration affecting the central nervous system
Atrophy/Degeneration affecting the cerebrum
Def: The presence of atrophy (wasting) of the cerebrum, also known as the telencephalon, the largest and most highly developed part of the human brain.

Name: Aplasia/Hypoplasia of the corpus callosum
Def: Absence or underdevelopment of the corpus callosum.
Synonym: Complete or partial absence of the corpus callosum
Hypoplasia or absence of the corpus callosum

Name: Corpus callosum atrophy
Def: The presence of atrophy (wasting) of the corpus callosum.

Name: Motor neuron atrophy
Def: Wasting involving the motor neuron.

Name: Abnormality of the septum pellucidum
Def: An abnormality of the septum pellucidum, which is a thin, triangular, vertical membrane separating the lateral ventricles of the brain.

Name: Abnormality of the choroid plexus
Def: An abnormality of the choroid plexus, which is the area in the cerebral ventricles in which cerebrospinal fluid is produced by modified ependymal cells.
Comment: The choroid plexus is a structure in the ventricles of the brain where cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) is produced.

Name: Abnormality of somatosensory evoked potentials
Def: An abnormality of somatosensory evoked potentials (SSEP), i.e., of the electrical signals of sensation going from the body to the brain in response to a defined stimulus. Recording electrodes are placed over the scalp, spine, and peripheral nerves proximal to the stimulation site. Clinical studies generally use electrical stimulation of peripheral nerves to elicit potentials. SSEP testing determines whether peripheral sensory nerves are able to transmit sensory information like pain, temperature, and touch to the brain. Abnormal SSEPs can result from dysfunction at the level of the peripheral nerve, plexus, spinal root, spinal cord, brain stem, thalamocortical projections, or primary somatosensory cortex.

Name: Neoplasm of the gastrointestinal tract
Def: A tumor (abnormal growth of tissue) of the gastrointestinal tract.

Name: Neoplasm of the genitourinary tract
Def: A tumor (abnormal growth of tissue) of the genitourinary system.

Name: Facial telangiectasia
Def: Telangiectases (small dilated blood vessels) located near the surface of the skin of the face.

Name: Aplasia cutis congenita of scalp
Def: A developmental defect resulting in the congenital absence of skin on the scalp.

Name: Hypoplastic sweat glands
Def: Underdevelopment of the sweat glands.

Name: Postnatal-onset ichthyosiform erythroderma
Def: A type of ichthyosiform erythroderma with postnatal onset.

Name: Early cutaneous photosensitivity
Def: Photosensitivity of the skin occurring early in life.
Synonym: Sun sensitivity occurring early in life

Name: Axillary apocrine gland hypoplasia
Def: Developmental hypoplasia of the apocrine sweat glands in the region of the axilla.

Name: Macular atrophy
Def: Well-demarcated area(s) of partial or complete depigmentation in the macula, reflecting atrophy of the retinal pigment epithelium with associated retinal photoreceptor loss.

Name: Areas of hypopigmentation and hyperpigmentation that do not follow Blaschko lines
Excessive skin wrinkling on dorsum of hands and fingers
Synonym: Excessive skin wrinkling on back of hands and fingers

Name: Tegumentary leishmaniasis susceptibility
Def: Increased susceptibility to infection by the protozan parasite of the genus Leishmania.

Name: obsolete Absence of subcutaneous fat over entire body except buttocks, hips, and thighs
Palmoplantar hyperhidrosis
Def: An abnormally increased perspiration on palms and soles.
Synonym: Excessive sweating of palms and soles

Name: Nevus flammeus of the forehead
Def: Naevus flammeus localised in the skin of the forehead.

Name: Neonatal wrinkled skin of hands and feet
Synonym: Wrinkled skin of hands and feet in newborn

Name: Discoid lupus rash
Def: Cutaneous lesion that develops as a dry, scaly, red patch that evolves to an indurated and hyperpigmented plaque with adherent scale. Scarring may result in central white patches (loss of pigmentation) and skin atrophy.
Comment: This lesion is characterstic of discoid lupus erythematosus, but similar lesions may be observed in other diseases.

Name: Alopecia totalis
Def: Loss of all scalp hair.

Name: Spontaneous hematomas
Def: Spontaneous development of hematomas (hematoma) or bruises without significant trauma.

Name: Telangiectases of the cheeks
Def: Telangiectases (small dilated blood vessels) located near the surface of the skin of the cheeks.

Name: Telangiectasia of the oral mucosa
Def: Telangiectasia (that is, the presence of small dilated superficial blood vessels) of the oral mucosa.
Synonym: Angioectasia of the oral mucous membrane
Spider veins of the oral mucosa
Telangiectasia of the oral mucous membrane

Name: Few cafe-au-lait spots
Def: The presence of two to five cafe-au-lait macules.

Name: Generalized edema
Def: Generalized abnormal accumulation of fluid beneath the skin, or in one or more cavities of the body.

Name: Congenital ichthyosiform erythroderma
Def: An ichthyosiform abnormality of the skin with congenital onset.

Name: Plaque-like facial hemangioma
Def: Hemangioma is a benign tumor of the vascular endothelial cells. This term refers to facial hemangiomas that have a plaque-like morphology.

Name: Multiple cutaneous leiomyomas
Def: The presence of multiple leiomyomas of the skin.

Name: Mottled pigmentation of the trunk and proximal extremities
Partial albinism
Def: Absence of melanin pigment in various areas, which is found at birth and is permanent. The lesions are known as leucoderma and are often found on the face, trunk, or limbs.
Synonym: Congenital partial albinism on face, trunk, or limbs

Name: Palmoplantar blistering
Def: A type of blistering that affects the skin of the palms of the hands and the soles of the feet.

Name: Increased groin pigmentation with raindrop depigmentation
Flexural lichenification
Def: Lichenification affecting primarily flexural areas of the skin.
Comment: The parts of the skin that touch when a joint flexes (bends) are called the flexural surfaces.

Name: Prominent veins on trunk
Def: Prominent thoracic and abdominal veins.

Name: Bitot spots of the conjunctiva
Def: Keratinization of the bulbar conjunctiva near the limbus (corneoscleral junction), resulting in a raised spot.
Comment: Bitot spots can be a feature of vitamin A deficiency.

Name: Sparse facial hair
Def: Reduced number or density of facial hair.

Name: Perifollicular hyperkeratosis
Def: Increased amount of keratin (visible as white scales) surrounding hair follicles.

Name: Palmoplantar cutis gyrata
Def: Cutis gyrata of palms and soles.
Synonym: Cutis gyrata of palms and soles

Name: Periarticular subcutaneous nodules
Def: Subcutaneous nodules that are located in the vicinity of joints.

Name: Axillary and groin hyperpigmentation and hypopigmentation
Congenital bullous ichthyosiform erythroderma
Def: An ichthyosiform abnormality of the skin that presents at birth or shortly thereafter with generalized erythema, blistering, erosions, and peeling. In the subsequent months, erythema and blistering improves but patients go on to develop hyperkeratotic scaling that is especially prominent along the joint flexures, neck, hands and feet.
Comment: Epidermolytic hyperkeratosis can refer to the disease caused by mutations in the genes keratin 1 or keratin 10, but is here used to refer to the characteristic skin manifestations as a phenotypic feature.

Name: Abnormal dermatoglyphics
Def: An abnormality of dermatoglyphs (fingerprints), which are present on fingers, palms, toes, and soles.

Name: Congenital nonbullous ichthyosiform erythroderma
Def: The term collodion baby applies to newborns who appear to have an extra layer of skin (known as a collodion membrane) that has a collodion-like quality. It is a descriptive term, not a specific diagnosis or disorder (as such, it is a syndrome). Affected babies are born in a collodion membrane, a shiny waxy outer layer to the skin. This is shed 10-14 days after birth, revealing the main symptom of the disease, extensive scaling of the skin caused by hyperkeratosis. With increasing age, the scaling tends to be concentrated around joints in areas such as the groin, the armpits, the inside of the elbow and the neck. The scales often tile the skin and may resemble fish scales.

Name: Decreased sweating due to autonomic dysfunction
Absence of subcutaneous fat
Def: Lack of subcutaneous adipose tissue.
Synonym: Lack of fatty tissue below the skin

Name: Diffuse telangiectasia
Def: Telangiectases (small dilated blood vessels) with a diffuse localization.

Name: Linear arrays of macular hyperkeratoses in flexural areas
Discrete 2 to 5-mm hyper- and hypopigmented macules
Focal friction-related palmoplantar hyperkeratosis
Def: Hyperkeratosis affecting the palm of the hand and the sole of the foot in areas exposed to friction.

Name: Recurrent staphylococcal infections
Def: Increased susceptibility to staphylococcal infections, as manifested by recurrent episodes of staphylococcal infections.

Name: Decreased number of sweat glands
Def: The presence of fewer than normal sweat glands.

Name: Streaks of hyperkeratosis along each finger onto the palm
Follicular hyperkeratosis
Def: A skin condition characterized by excessive development of keratin in hair follicles, resulting in rough, cone-shaped, elevated papules resulting from closure of hair follicles with a white plug of sebum.

Name: Congenital absence of skin of limbs
Synonym: Missing skin on limbs since birth

Name: Punctate palmar hyperkeratosis
Def: Tiny bumps of thickened skin (hyperkeratosis) on the palms of the hands.

Name: Edema of the dorsum of hands
Def: An abnormal accumulation of fluid beneath the skin on the back of the hands.

Name: Redundant skin on fingers
Def: Loose and sagging skin of the fingers.

Name: Palmoplantar cutis laxa
Def: Loose, wrinkled skin of hands and feet.
Synonym: Excessive wrinkled skin of palms and soles
Increased wrinkles of palms and soles
Wrinkled skin of hands and feet

Name: obsolete Lack of subcutaneous fatty tissue
Yellow subcutaneous tissue covered by thin, scaly skin
Hypopigmented skin patches on arms
Synonym: Patchy loss of skin color on arms

Name: Congenital posterior occipital alopecia
Def: Loss of hair in the occipital region of the scalp with congenital onset.

Name: Aplasia cutis congenita of midline scalp vertex
Severe photosensitivity
Def: A severe degree of photosensitivity of the skin.

Name: Frontal cutaneous lipoma
Def: Presence of a cutaneous lipoma on the forehead.

Name: Absent pigmentation of the ventral chest
Def: Lack of skin pigmentation (coloring) of the anterior chest.

Name: Piebaldism
Def: Piebaldism is characterized by stable and persistent, well-circumscribed depigmented patches present at birth affecting the skin of the face, trunk, and extremities in a symmetrical distribution.

Name: Palmoplantar keratosis with erythema and scale
Desquamation of skin soon after birth
Hypohidrosis or hyperhidrosis
Synonym: Lack of sweating or excessive sweating

Name: Abnormal subcutaneous fat tissue distribution
Synonym: Abnormal fat tissue distribution below the skin

Name: Confetti hypopigmentation pattern of lower leg skin
Synonym: Confetti hypopigmentation pattern of lower leg skin

Name: Plantar hyperkeratosis
Def: Hyperkeratosis affecting the sole of the foot.

Name: Telangiectases in sun-exposed and nonexposed skin
Multiple cafe-au-lait spots
Def: The presence of six or more cafe-au-lait spots.
Synonym: Multiple flat light-brown marks on skin

Name: Generalized seborrheic dermatitis
Def: Seborrheic dermatitis that is not localized to any one particular region.

Name: Hyperkeratosis lenticularis perstans
Def: Hyperkeratosis lenticularis perstans (HLP), also known as Flegel disease, is a keratinization abnormality characterized by small, asymptomatic erythematous papules that leave characteristic punctate bleeding when they become detached. The lesions generally occur symmetrically along the top of the foot and on the legs, appearing more rarely on the arms, forearms, palms, and soles, and even on the oral mucosa.

Name: Late onset atopic dermatitis
Def: A form of atopic dermatitis with onset in adulthood characterized by atopic red face, chronic lichenified eczema on the trunk, subacute or psoriasiform dermatitis.

Name: Reticular hyperpigmentation
Def: Increased pigmentation of the skin with a netlike (reticular) pattern.

Name: Aplasia cutis congenita on trunk or limbs
Def: A developmental defect resulting in the congenital absence of skin on the trunk or the limbs.
Comment: In future versions of the HPO this term will be made obsolete and will be replaced by terms for Aplasia cutis congenita on trunk and a term for Aplasia cutis congenita on the limbs.

Name: Aplasia cutis congenita over posterior parietal area
Aplasia/Hypoplastia of the eccrine sweat glands
Def: Absence or developmental hypoplasia of the eccrine sweat glands.

Name: Painful subcutaneous lipomas
Def: The presence of multiple subcutaneous lipoma that cause pain.
Synonym: Painful noncancerous fat tissue tumor under the skin

Name: Bilateral single transverse palmar creases
Def: The distal and proximal transverse palmar creases are merged into a single transverse palmar crease on both hands.

Name: Hypoproteinemic edema
Def: An abnormal accumulation of fluid beneath the skin, or in one or more cavities of the body because of decreased osmotic pressure of plasma (hypoproteinemia).

Name: Spinous keratoses of palms and soles
Nevus flammeus nuchae
Def: Naevus flammeus localised in the skin of the neck. This is one of the most common birthmarks and present in approximately 25% of all newborns.
Comment: The salmon patch is the most common capillary malformation, occurring in up to 50% of all neonates. It is a pinkish macule that typically affects the back of the neck (stork bite) or the glabella (angel's kiss), although it can affect the eyelids, the nose, the upper lip, and the sacral area.

Name: Subcutaneous calcification
Def: Deposition of calcium salts in subcutaneous tissue (i.e., the the lowermost layer of the integument).

Name: Cutaneous leiomyoma
Def: The presence of leiomyoma of the skin.
Comment: Cutaneous leiomyomata are benign soft tissue neoplasms that arise from smooth muscle cells in the skin.

Name: Mandibular osteomyelitis
Def: Osteomyelitis of the lower jaw.

Name: Mandibular condyle aplasia
Synonym: Absence of the condylar head of mandible
Absence of the condylar neck of mandible
Absence of the condylar process of mandible
Agenesis of condylar head of mandible
Agenesis of condylar neck of mandible
Agenesis of condylar process of mandible
Failure of development of condylar head of mandible
Failure of development of condylar neck of mandible
Failure of development of the condylar process of mandible
Underdevelopment of condylar head of mandible
Underdevelopment of condylar neck of mandible
Underdevelopment of condylar process of mandible

Name: Mandibular condyle hypoplasia
Synonym: Decreased size of condylar process of mandible
Hypoplasia of condylar head of mandible
Hypoplasia of condylar neck of mandible
Hypoplasia of condylar process of mandible
Hypoplasia of subcondylar region of mandible

Name: Bilateral microphthalmos
Def: A developmental anomaly characterized by abnormal smallness of both eyes.
Synonym: Abnormally small eyeball on both sides
Decreased size of globes of eyes

Name: Nonarteritic anterior ischemic optic neuropathy
Def: An acute condition characterized by sudden visual loss (usually discovered in the morning), optic disc edema at onset, optic disc-related visual field defects. Nonarteritic anterior ischemic optic neuropathy can be associated with flame hemorrhages on the swollen disc or nearby neuroretinal layer, and sometimes with nearby cotton-wool exudates.
Comment: Nonarteritic anterior ischemic optic neuropathy is caused by infarction of the laminar or retrolaminar portion of the optic nerve head supplied by the short posterior ciliary arteries. Clinically NAION is characterized by sudden, usually painless, loss of vision in one or both eyes. Examination findings include decreased visual acuity, a visual field defect, decreased colour vision, a relative afferent pupillary defect, and optic disc swelling.

Name: Dyschromatopsia
Def: A form of colorblindness in which only two of the three fundamental colors can be distinguished due to a lack of one of the retinal cone pigments.

Name: Congenital stationary night blindness
Def: A nonprogressive (i.e., stationary) form of difficulties with night blindness with congenital onset.
Comment: Congenital stationary night blindness is prinicipally the result of dysfunction of the rod photoreceptors.

Name: Peripheral tractional retinal detachment
Def: Tractional retinal detachment at the periphery of the retina.
Synonym: Tractional retinal detachment at the periphery of the retina

Name: Absent lower eyelashes
Def: Lack of eyelashes on the lower lid.
Synonym: Failure of development of lower eyelashes

Name: Congenital extraocular muscle anomaly
Def: Congenital abnormality of the extraocular muscles.

Name: Punctate cataract
Def: A type of cataract with punctate opacities of the lens.

Name: Congenital hypertrophy of retinal pigment epithelium
Def: Sharply demarcated, congenital hyperpigmentation of the retinal pigment epithelium.
Comment: This feature is found in around 3-5% of the population and is of no functional significance.

Name: Eversion of lateral third of lower eyelids
Lacrimal gland aplasia
Def: A congenital defect of development characterized by absence of the lacrimal gland.

Name: Diffuse nuclear cataract
Def: Opacity of the entire lens nucleus.

Name: obsolete Decreased retinal pigmentation with dispersion
Curly eyelashes
Def: Abnormally curly or curved eyelashes.

Name: Peripheral cystoid retinal degeneration
Def: Degenerative changes of the peripheral retina consisting of close-packed tiny cystic spaces at the outer plexiform/inner nuclear retinal level. The degeneration is very common in adult eyes and starts adjacent to the ora serrata and extends circumferentially and posteriorly.

Name: Abnormal vestibulo-ocular reflex
Def: An abnormality of the vestibulo-ocular reflex (VOR). The VOR attempts to keep the image stable on the retina. Ideally passive or active head movements in one direction are compensated for by eye movements of equal magnitude.

Name: Hypoplasia of the iris
Def: Congenital underdevelopment of the iris.

Name: Vitelliform-like macular lesions
Def: Vitelliform maculopathy is a sharply demarcated lesion caused by the accumulation of material, often lipofuscin in the subretinal space underlying the macula.

Name: Lacrimal duct stenosis
Def: Narrowing of a tear duct (lacrimal duct).

Name: Abnormal pupillary function
Def: A functional abnormality of the pupil.
Comment: It is preferable to describe the functional defect precisely.

Name: Unilateral ptosis
Def: A unilateral form of ptosis.

Name: Undetectable light- and dark-adapted electroretinogram
Def: Absence of the combined rod-and-cone response on electroretinogram.
Synonym: Absent cone and rod functions by electroretinogram
Absent rod-and cone-mediated responses on ERG

Name: Abnormal pupillary light reflex
Def: An abnormality of the reflex that controls the diameter of the pupil, in response to the intensity of light that falls on the retina of the eye.

Name: Hypoplasia of the lower eyelids
Def: Underdevelopment of the lower eyelid.

Name: Ocular anterior segment dysgenesis
Def: Abnormal development (dysgenesis) of the anterior segment of the eye globe. These structures are mainly of mesenchymal origin.
Comment: In anterior segment mesenchymal ocular dysgenesis (ASMOD), multiple tissues are affected, including the iris, cornea, and lens as well as the Schlemm's canal and trabecular meshwork drainage structures located at the anterior segment angle where the iris and cornea meet. These abnormalities may result from a primary defect in the migration and/or differentiation of the mesenchymal cells that contribute to development of the cornea, iris, and drainage structures.

Name: Abnormality of retinal pigmentation
Synonym: Abnormality of the retinal pigment epithelium

Name: Paroxysmal involuntary eye movements
Def: Sudden-onset episode of abnormal, involuntary eye movements.

Name: Congenital aphakia
Def: Absence of the crystalline lens of the eye as a result of a developmental defect.

Name: Uveal melanoma
Def: A malignant melanoma originating within the eye. The tumor originates from the melanocytes in the uvea (which comprises the iris, ciliary body, and choroid).
Comment: WIth intraocular melanoma, the melanoma originates from melanocytic cells in the uveal layer, comprising the iris, ciliary body, and choroid.

Name: Chronic irritative conjunctivitis
Def: A chronic irritative conjunctivitis, which commonly presents with general irritation and redness of the eyes, with a burning, dry, or foreign-body sensation of the eyes.

Name: Flat cornea
Def: Cornea plana is an abnormally flat shape of the cornea such that the normal protrusion of the cornea from the sclera is missing. The reduced corneal curvature can lead to hyperopia, and a hazy corneal limbus and arcus lipoides may develop at an early age.

Name: Saccular conjunctival dilatations
Def: Presence of multiple dilatations (sac-like outpouchings) in the blood vessels of the conjunctiva.

Name: Retinal pigment epithelial atrophy
Def: Atrophy (loss or wasting) of the retinal pigment epithelium observed on fundoscopy or fundus imaging.

Name: Opacification of the corneal epithelium
Def: Lack of transparency of the corneal epithelium.

Name: Congenital miosis
Def: Abnormal (non-physiological) constriction of the pupil of congenital onset.

Name: Iris hypopigmentation
Def: An abnormal reduction in the amount of pigmentation of the iris.

Name: Chorioretinal dysplasia
Def: Abnormal development of the choroid and retina.

Name: Lacrimal gland hypoplasia
Def: Underdevelopment of the lacrimal gland.

Name: Enlarged lacrimal glands
Def: Abnormally big lacrimal glands.

Name: Bone spicule pigmentation of the retina
Def: Pigment migration into the retina in a bone-spicule configuration (resembling the nucleated cells within the lacuna of bone).

Name: Hypoplasia of the fovea
Def: Underdevelopment of the fovea centralis.
Comment: A dull foveal reflex is an unusual reflex of the foveal region on fundoscopy that may indicate hypoplasia of the fovea.

Name: Macular dystrophy
Def: Macular dystrophy is a nonspecific term for premature retinal cell aging and cell death, generally confied to the macula in which no clear extrinsic cause is evident.

Name: obsolete Slitlike anterior chamber angles in children
Opacification of the corneal stroma
Def: Reduced transparency of the stroma of cornea.

Name: Pericentral scotoma
Def: A scotoma (area of diminished vision within the visual field) that surrounds the central fixation point.

Name: Retinal telangiectasia
Def: Dilatation of small blood vessels of the retina.

Name: Deep anterior chamber
Def: Increased depth of the anterior chamber, i.e., the anteroposterior distance between the cornea and the iris is increased.
Comment: Deep anterior chamber can be seen in disorders such as congenital microphakia and buphthalmos.

Name: Optic disc hypoplasia
Def: Underdevelopment of the optic disc, that is of the optic nerve head, where ganglion cell axons exit the eye to form the optic nerve.

Name: Central retinal vessel vascular tortuosity
Def: The presence of an increased number of twists and turns of retinal blood vessels (arteries, arterioles, veins, venules).

Name: Impaired smooth pursuit
Def: An impairment of the ability to track objects with the ocular smooth pursuit system, a class of rather slow eye movements that minimizes retinal target motion.

Name: Vitreoretinopathy
Def: Ocular abnormality characterised by premature degeneration of the vitreous and the retina that may be associated with increased risk of retinal detachment.

Name: Hypoplasia of the ciliary body
Def: Underdevelopment of the ciliary body.

Name: Chorioretinal scar
Def: Fibrous connective tissue resulting from incomplete healing of a wound (i.e., a scar) located in the choroid and retina or the eye.

Name: Posterior retinal neovascularization
Def: A type of retinal neovascularization that affects the posterior pole of the retina.
Synonym: Neovascularization of peripheral and posterior retina

Name: Cortical pulverulent cataract
Def: A type of cataract characterized by punctate, dust-like opacities within the cortical region of the lens.

Name: obsolete Butterfly retinal pigment epithelial dystrophy
Posterior subcapsular cataract
Def: A type of cataract affecting the posterior pole of lens immediately adjacent to ('beneath') the Lens capsule.
Synonym: Posterior subcapsular opacities of the lens

Name: Patchy atrophy of the retinal pigment epithelium
Def: Wasting (atrophy) of the retinal pigment epithelium present in small, isolated areas.

Name: Granular macular appearance
Def: Mottled (spotted or blotched with different shades) pigmentary abnormality of the macula lutea.

Name: Anterior cortical cataract
Def: A cataract that affects the anterior part of the cortex of the lens.

Name: Conjunctival whitish salt-like deposits
Def: The presence of whitish deposits in the conjunctiva resembling salt. May be related to calcinosis.

Name: Increased axial length of the globe
Def: Abnormal largeness of the eye with an axial length > 2.5 standard deviations from population mean.
Synonym: Increased front to back length of eyeball

Name: Granular corneal dystrophy
Def: The presence of central, fine, whitish granular lesions in the stroma of the cornea. This type of corneal dystrophy is usually asymptomatic and begins in childhood and shows a slow progression. Later in the course, the corneal epithelium and Bowman's layer may be affected. Histologically, the cornea shows a uniform deposition of hyaline material.

Name: Monochromacy
Def: Complete color blindness, a complete inability to distinguish colors. Affected persons cannot perceive colors, but only shades of gray.
Comment: Rod monochromacy is the condition of having only rods in the retina. A rod monochromat is truly unable to see any color and can see only shades of grey.

Name: Horizontal pendular nystagmus
Def: Nystagmus consisting of horizontal to-and-fro eye movements of equal velocity.
Comment: Pendular nystagmus refers to the situation in which the eye appeared to oscillate with equal speed in either direction, in contrast to jerk nystagmus, in which the movement in one direction is faster than in the other.

Name: Herpetiform corneal ulceration
Def: The presence of one or more dendritic corneal epithelial ulcers characterized by a treelike branching linear pattern with feathery edges and terminal bulbs. Herpetiform corneal ulcers can be identified by fluorescein staining.

Name: Nongranulomatous uveitis
Def: A form of uveitis that is not associated with the formation of granulomas.

Name: Retinal pigment epithelial mottling
Def: Mottling (spots or blotches with different shades) of the retinal pigment epithelium, i.e., localized or generalized fundal pigment granularity associated with processes at the level of the retinal pigment epithelium.
Synonym: Focal hypopigmentation of the retinal pigment epithelium

Name: Abnormal distribution of retinal arterioles and venules
Horizontal supranuclear gaze palsy
Def: A supranuclear gaze palsy is an inability to look in a horizontal direction as a result of cerebral impairment. There is a loss of the voluntary aspect of eye movements, but, as the brainstem is still intact, all the reflex conjugate eye movements are normal.

Name: Central heterochromia
Def: The presence of distinct colors in the central (pupillary) zone of the iris than in the mid-peripheral (ciliary) zone.

Name: Presenile cataracts
Def: Presenile cataract is a kind of cataract that occurs in early adulthood, that is, at an age that is younger than usual.
Comment: Presenile cataract is rare. Some cases have a hereditary cause; others result from trauma or chromosomal, endocrine, metabolic, or systemic disorders. Many cases are idiopathic. The term 'presenile' is used differently in the literature. The HPO defines it to mean a cataract that is diagnosed after the age of 20 years but before old age.

Name: Lacrimal punctal atresia
Def: Congenital absence or closure of the opening of the lacrimal punctum.

Name: Total ophthalmoplegia
Def: Paralysis of both the extrinsic and intrinsic ocular muscles.

Name: obsolete Cataracts develop in second or third decade
Adult-onset night blindness
Def: Inability to see well at night or in poor light with onset in adulthood.

Name: Nonprogressive restrictive external ophthalmoplegia
Def: Nonprogressive restriction of movement of the external ocular muscles such that the eyes of affected individuals are partially or completely fixed in a strabismic position. Residual eye movements are significantly limited.

Name: Pigmentation of the sclera
Synonym: Pigmentation of the outer white part of the eyeball

Name: Progressive cataract
Def: A kind of cataract that progresses with age.

Name: Progressive ptosis
Def: A progressive form of ptosis.

Name: Long upper eyelashes
Def: Increased length of the upper eyelashes.

Name: Amyloid deposition in the vitreous humor
Def: Deposition of hyaline extracellular material (amyloid) into the vitreous humor, which can manifest as vitreous opacities and reduced visual acuity.

Name: Attenuation of retinal blood vessels
Synonym: Narrowing of blood vessels in back of eye

Name: Punctate opacification of the cornea
Def: Punctate opacification (reduced transparency) of the corneal stroma.

Name: Chorioretinal lacunae
Def: Punched out lesions in the pigmented layer of the retina.
Comment: A chorioretinal lacuna can have the appearance of a pseudodisk in the retina.

Name: Congenital horizontal nystagmus
Def: Horizontal nystagmus dating from or present at birth.

Name: Retinal calcification
Def: Deposition of calcium salts in the retina.

Name: Restrictive partial external ophthalmoplegia
Def: Fibrosis of only some of the external ocular muscles such that the eyes of affected individuals are partially or completely fixed in a strabismic position.

Name: Choroidal hemangioma
Def: The presence of multiple hemangiomas in the choroid. These are generally reddish or orange or can have increased pigmentation maiking them difficult to distinguish from choroidal melanomas.
Comment: Choroidal hemangiomas can cause hyperopia or other visual symptoms such as blurred or distorted vision. Some choroidal hemangiomas are asymptomatic.

Name: Almond-shaped palpebral fissure
Def: A shape created by an acute downward arching of the upper eyelid and upward arching of the lower eyelid, toward the medial canthus, which gives the outline of the palpebral fissures the configuration of an almond. Thus, the maximum distance between the fissures is offset from, and medial to, the center point.
Comment: The almond configuration tends to dissipate with time, as the surrounding tissues (e.g., eyelid, nasal bridge) grow.

Name: Congenital blindness
Def: Blindness with onset at birth.

Name: Allergic conjunctivitis
Def: Allergic Conjunctivitis is an allergic inflammation of the conjunctiva.

Name: Slowed horizontal saccades
Def: An abnormally slow velocity of horizontal saccadic eye movements.
Comment: Saccades are rapid eye movements that align the fovea with the target.

Name: Absent extraocular muscles
Def: Congenital absence of the extraocular muscles.

Name: Iridescent posterior subcapsular cataract
Def: A type of posterior subcapsular cataract characterized by an iridescent color.

Name: Hypoplasia of the lacrimal punctum
Def: Underdevelopment of the lacrimal puncta.

Name: Hypopigmentation of the fundus
Def: Reduced pigmentation of the fundus, typically generalised. Fundoscopy may reveal a low level pigment in both RPE and choroid with clear visibility of choroidal vessels (pale/albinoid) or low pigment level in the RPE with deep pigment in choroid so that visible choroidal vessels are separated by deeply pigmented zones (tesselated/tigroid).

Name: Retinal nonattachment
Def: Failure of attachment of the retina during development.

Name: Vitreous hemorrhage
Def: Bleeding within the vitreous compartment of the eye.
Comment: The most common causes include proliferative diabetic retinopathy, vitreous detachment with or without retinal breaks, and trauma. Less common causes include vascular occlusive disease, retinal arterial macroaneurysm, hemoglobinopathies, age-related macular degeneration, intraocular tumors, and others.

Name: Paravenous chorioretinal atrophy
Def: Chorioretinal atrophy along the retinal veins.

Name: Ocular hypertension
Def: Intraocular pressure that is 2 standard deviations above the population mean.

Name: Congenital bilateral ptosis
Synonym: Congenital drooping of both upper eyelids

Name: Reticular retinal dystrophy
Def: A type of of patterned retinal dystrophy that shows a reticular pattern of pigmentation.

Name: Polymorphous posterior corneal dystrophy
Def: This corneal dystrophy affects the posterior limiting membrane of the cornea and is characterized by polymorphous plaques of calcium deposits in the deep stromal layers of the cornea, and occasionally by vesicular lesions of the endothelium and edema of the deep corneal stroma.

Name: obsolete Small anterior lens surface opacities
Tractional retinal detachment
Def: A type of retinal detachment arising due to a combination of contracting retinal membranes, abnormal vitreoretinal adhesions, and vitreous changes. It is usually seen in the context of diseases that induce a fibrovascular response, e.g. diabetes.

Name: Slow decrease in visual acuity
Synonym: Slow decrease in sharpness of vision

Name: Lacrimal duct aplasia
Def: A congenital defect resulting in absence of the lacrimal duct.

Name: Abnormal flash visual evoked potentials
Def: Anomaly of the visual evoked potentials elicited by a flash stimulus, generally a flash of light subtending an angle of at least 20 degrees of the visual field and presented in a dimly lit room.

Name: Peripheral retinal detachment
Def: Separation of the inner layers of the retina (neural retina) from the pigment epithelium occuring near the outer limit (periphery) of the retina.

Name: Bilateral congenital mydriasis
Def: Congenital abnormal dilation of the pupil on both sides.

Name: Broad lateral eyebrow
Def: Regional increase in the width (height) of the lateral eyebrow.

Name: Restrictive external ophthalmoplegia
Def: Fibrosis of the external ocular muscles such that the eyes of affected individuals are partially or completely fixed in a strabismic position. Residual eye movements are significantly limited.

Name: Reticular pigmentary degeneration
Def: A type of retinal reticular pigmentation that forms a polygonal, netlike arrangement of hyperpigmented lines forming geometric patterns in the fundus.

Name: Blue cone monochromacy
Def: A form of monochromacy in which vision is derived from the remaining preserved blue (S) cones and rod photoreceptors.

Name: Internal ophthalmoplegia
Def: Paralysis of the iris and ciliary apparatus.
Comment: Paralysis of the internal ocular muscles, the iris and ciliary apparatus.

Name: Congenital stapes ankylosis
Def: A form of stapes ankylosis with congenital onset.

Name: Unilateral narrow palpebral fissure
Def: A fixed reduction in the vertical distance between the upper and lower eyelids with short palpebral fissures on one side only.
Synonym: Unequal size of opening between the eyelids

Name: Pericentral retinitis pigmentosa
Def: A subtype of retinitis pigmentosa in which, instead of the pathology starting in the mid-periphery like typical retinitis pigmentosa, the disease starts in the near periphery closer to the vascular arcades and tends to spare the far periphery.

Name: Dense posterior cortical cataract
Def: A type of posterior cortical cataract characterized by dense lenticular opacities.

Name: Peripapillary chorioretinal atrophy
Def: Chorioretinal atrophy concentrated around the optic papilla (i.e., the optic nerve head).

Name: Corneal opacity
Def: A reduction of corneal clarity.
Synonym: Scarring or clouding of the cornea of the eye

Name: Optic atrophy from cranial nerve compression
Pattern dystrophy of the retina
Def: A spectrum of fundoscopic appearances characterized by the development of a variety of patterns of deposits predominantly in the macular area. The deposits are typically bilateral, relatively symmetrical, yellow/white and associated with changes at the level of the retinal pigment epithelium. With time, retinal atrophy may occur. A number of pattern dystrophy subtypes have been described including butterfly-shaped dystrophy, reticular dystrophy (net-like pattern) and fundus pulverulentus (granular, mottled pigmentation).

Name: Remnants of the hyaloid vascular system
Def: Persistence of the hyaloid artery, which is the embryonic artery that runs from the optic disk to the posterior lens capsule may persist; the site of attachment may form an opacity. The hyaloid artery is a branch of the ophthalmic artery, and usually regresses completely before birth. This features results from a failure of regression of the hyaloid vessel, which supplies the primary vitreous during embryogenesis and normally regresses in the third trimester of pregnancy, leading to a particular form of posterior cataract.
Synonym: Persistent posterior fetal fibrovascular sheath of the lens

Name: Lamellar cataract
Def: A congenital cataract in which opacity is limited to layers of the lens external to the nucleus (i.e., the perinuclear region), i.e., between the nuclear and cortical layers of the lens.

Name: Retinal dysplasia
Def: The presence of developmental dysplasia of the retina.
Comment: This feature is a congenital developmental anomaly of the retina characterized by abnormal growth and differentiation. The retina contains numerous tubular structures and rosettes. Retinal dysplasia (synonym: retinal dysgenesis) is often accompanied by retinal detachment and micropthalmos, but the latter features should be coded separately.

Name: Hypometric horizontal saccades
Def: Saccadic undershoot of horizontal saccadic eye movements, i.e., a horizontal saccadic eye movement that has less than the magnitude that would be required to gain fixation of the object.

Name: Cerulean cataract
Def: Cerulean cataracts are a kind of congenital cataract having peripheral bluish and white opacifications in concentric layers with occasional central lesions arranged radially. Although the opacities may be observed during fetal development and childhood, usually visual acuity is only mildly reduced until adulthood, when lens extraction is generally necessary.

Name: Gaze-evoked horizontal nystagmus
Def: Horizontal nystagmus made apparent by looking to the right or to the left.

Name: obsolete Concentric narrowing of visual field
Electronegative electroretinogram
Def: A dark-adapted bright flash electroretinogram in which the b-wave that is of markedly lower amplitude than the associated a-wave (source: Holder GE., Inherited Chorioretinal Dystrophies: A Textbook and Atlas; 2014; p.17; ISBN 978-3-540-69466-3).
Comment: Flashes will elicit an a-wave with an initial negative deflection followed by a b-wave with positive deflection. This feature refers to a reduction in the amplitude primarily of the b-wave.
Synonym: Reduced amplitude of dark-adapted bright flash electroretinogram b-wave

Name: Retinal arteriolar occlusion
Def: Blockage of retinal arteriole, generally associated with interruption of blood flow and oxygen delivery to affected regions of the retina.

Name: Macular hypopigmentation
Def: Decreased amount of pigmentation in the macula lutea.

Name: Intraretinal exudate
Def: Retinal exudate within the retinal tissue itself.

Name: Hypoplastic iris stroma
Def: Underdevelopment of the stroma of iris.

Name: Malformed lacrimal duct
Def: Congenital malformation of the lacrimal duct associated with incomplete development of the bony nasolacrimal canal or craniofacial anomalies.

Name: Peripheral visual field loss
Def: Loss of peripheral vision with retention of central vision, resulting in a constricted circular tunnel-like field of vision.

Name: Decreased corneal reflex
Def: An abnormally reduced response to stimulation of the cornea (by touch, foreign body, blowing air). The corneal reflex (also known as the blink reflex, normally results in an involuntary blinking of the eyelids.

Name: Foveal hyperpigmentation
Def: Increased amount of pigmentation in the fovea centralis.

Name: Abnormality of macular pigmentation
Def: Abnormality of macular or foveal pigmentation.

Name: Peripheral opacification of the cornea
Def: Reduced transparency of the peripheral region of the cornea.

Name: Central fundal arteriolar microaneurysms
Def: Microscopic aneurysms of the retinal arterioles near the central part of the fundus, visible as small round dark red dots on the retinal surface (not arising from visible vessels) that are by definition less than the diameter of the major optic veins as they cross the optic disc.

Name: obsolete Depigmented lesions of the retinal pigment epithelium
Superior lens subluxation
Def: Partial dislocation of the lens in a superior direction.

Name: Cone dystrophy
Def: Inherited progressive cone degeneration.

Name: Cystoid macular degeneration
Def: A form of macular degeneration characterized by the presence of multiple cysts in the macula.

Name: Posterior Y-sutural cataract
Def: A type of sutural cataract in which the opacity follows the posterior Y suture.

Name: Abnormal iris pigmentation
Def: Abnormal pigmentation of the iris.

Name: Retinitis pigmentosa inversa
Def: Retinitis pigmentosa inversa is form of retinal degeneration characterized by areas of retinal/chorioretinal degeneration with pigment migration in the macular area (in contrast to retinitis pigmentosa which, at early disease stages, predominantly affects the retinal periphery).

Name: Absent anterior chamber of the eye
Def: Absence of the anterior chamber of the eye owing to a developmental defect.

Name: Aplastic/hypoplastic lacrimal glands
Def: Absence or underdevelopment of the lacrimal gland.

Name: Retinal arteriolar constriction
Def: Decreased retinal arteriolar diameters, which may decrease blood flow and slow oxygen delivery to regions of the retina.
Comment: Usually after the first branch, the retinal arteries contain no elastic fibers and the term retinal arteriole is more appropriate. The main changes seen in diseases such as hypertension affect mainly the retinal arterioles rather than the retinal artery.

Name: Abnormal retinal vascular morphology
Def: A structural abnormality of retinal vasculature.

Name: Abnormality of the vasculature of the eye
Abnormality of the line of Schwalbe
Def: An abnormality of the line of Schwalbe.
Comment: Schwalbe's line is the anatomical line found on the posterior surface of the cornea, delineating the outer limit of the corneal endothelium layer.

Name: Abnormality of the extraocular muscles
Def: An abnormality of an extraocular muscle.
Comment: There are six extraocular muscles that control the movements of the eye.

Name: Abnormality of the palpebral fissures
Def: An anomaly of the space between the medial and lateral canthi of the two open eyelids.
Synonym: Abnormality of the opening between the eyelids

Name: obsolete Abnormality of the retinal pigment epithelium
Retinal fold
Def: A wrinkle of retinal tissue projecting outward from the surface of the retina and visible as a line on fundoscopy.

Name: Aplasia/Hypoplasia of the iris
Def: Absence or underdevelopment of the iris.

Name: Abnormal morphology of the conjunctival vasculature
Def: Any abnormality of the blood vessels of the conjunctiva.
Synonym: Abnormal morphology of the conjunctiva vasculature
Abnormal vasculature of the conjunctiva morphology
Abnormality of the vasculature of the conjunctiva

Name: Aplasia/Hypoplasia affecting the uvea
Def: Absence or underdevelopment of the uvea, the pigmented middle layer of the eye consisting of the iris and ciliary body together with the choroid.

Name: Aplasia/Hypoplasia of the fovea
Def: Congenital absence or underdevelopment of the fovea centralis.

Name: Aplasia/Hypoplasia affecting the anterior segment of the eye
Def: Absence or underdevelopment of the anterior segment of the eye.

Name: Aplasia/Hypoplasia of the lens
Def: Absence or underdevelopment of the lens.

Name: Ichthyosis
Def: An abnormality of the skin characterized the presence of excessive amounts of dry surface scales on the skin resulting from an abnormality of keratinization.
Comment: The ichthyoses are a group of skin diseases characterized by drying and scaling of skin with the accumulation of thick scales and cracks that may be painful or bleed. The abnormality in ichthyosis lies in am imbalance in the normal lifecycle of skin in which growth is matched with dying and shedding of skin cells. In ichthyosis, skin cells reproduce at a rate faster than dead skin cells can be shed or reproduce at a normal rate with a reduction in the rate of shedding. Either abnormality leads to a build up of dry and scaly skin. Note that this term refers to the morphological abnormality of the skin and not the disorder.

Name: Abnormal blistering of the skin
Def: The presence of one or more bullae on the skin, defined as fluid-filled blisters more than 5 mm in diameter with thin walls.
Comment: A bulla is a large vesicle described as a rounded or irregularly shaped blister containing serous or seropurulent fluid, equal to or greater than 10mm.

Name: Neoplasm of the skin
Def: A tumor (abnormal growth of tissue) of the skin.

Name: Sparse hair
Def: Reduced density of hairs.
Comment: This term applies if the number of hair shafts per unit area is reduced. The term fine hair is used to describe hair with a reduced diameter.

Name: Maternal hypertension
Def: Increased blood pressure during a pregnancy.

Name: Maternal virilization in pregnancy
Def: Virilization (deepening of voice, facial hirsutism and scalp hair loss) with onset during pregnancy (usually towards the end of the first trimester) and regression several months post-partum.

Name: Low maternal serum estriol
Def: An abnormally high concentration of serum conjugated estriol as compared to normal values for gestational-age.

Name: Progressive pes cavus
Def: The development of Pes cavus that is progressive with age.

Name: Osteoporotic tarsals
Def: Reduction in bone mineral density affecting any or all of the tarsal bones, seven bones of the foot comprising the calcaneus, talus, cuboid, navicular, and the cuneiform bones.

Name: Absent fifth metatarsal
Def: A developmental abnormality characterized by the absence of the fifth metatarsal bone.
Synonym: Aplasia of the fifth metatarsal bone

Name: Hallux varus
Def: Medial deviation of the great toe owing to a deformity of the great toe joint causing the hallux to deviate medially.

Name: Pes valgus
Def: An outward deviation of the foot at the talocalcaneal or subtalar joint.
Comment: Valgus refers to the twisting outward of a bone or joint is twisted outward from the center of the body, whereas varus is a twisting toward the center of the body.

Name: Nonossified fifth metatarsal
Def: The presence of a fifth metatarsal bone that has not undergone ossification at an age when ossification is usually visible.

Name: Abnormality of the fifth metatarsal bone
Def: An anomaly of the fifth metatarsal bone.
Synonym: Abnormality of the 5th long bone of foot

Name: Short 4th toe
Def: Underdevelopment (hypoplasia) of the fourth toe.

Name: Widely spaced toes
Def: An overall widening of the spaces between the digits.
Comment: This description is based on the width of the gap between the toes. It is usually used when the width of the toes remains normal rather than to describe a situation where the toes are thin or narrow. This term should not be used for the situation where the finding is limited to a gap between T1,2 (see Sandal gap).

Name: Osteolysis of talus
Def: Osteolysis affecting the talus.

Name: Medially deviated second toe
Def: Medial deviation of the second toe.

Name: Expanded metatarsals with widened medullary cavities
Delayed tarsal ossification
Def: Delayed maturation and calcification of any of the tarsal bones, seven bones of the foot comprising the calcaneus, talus, cuboid, navicular, and the cuneiform bones.

Name: Plantar crease between first and second toes
Def: The presence of unusually deep creases (ridges/wrinkles) on the skin of sole of foot located between the first and second toe.

Name: Advanced tarsal ossification
Def: Precocious (accelerated) maturation and calcification of any of the tarsal bones, seven bones of the foot comprising the calcaneus, talus, cuboid, navicular, and the cuneiform bones.

Name: Metatarsal diaphyseal endosteal sclerosis
Def: Osteosclerosis of the endosteal surface of the diaphyses (shafts) of the metatarsal bones.

Name: Clinodactyly of the 3rd toe
Def: Bending or curvature of a third toe in the tibial direction (i.e., towards the big toe).

Name: Flexion limitation of toes
Def: Limitation of the ability to bend the toes.

Name: Calcaneonavicular fusion
Def: Synostosis of the calcaneus with the navicular bone.

Name: Talipes calcaneovarus
Def: A congenital deformity characterized by a dorsiflexed, inverted, and adducted foot, i.e., a combination of talipes calcaneus and talipes varus.

Name: Bipartite calcaneus
Def: A two-part calcaneus, a finding that probably results from delayed coalescence of two primary calcaneal centers of ossification.
Synonym: Delayed coalescence of calcaneal ossification centers

Name: Tarsal stippling
Def: The presence of abnormal punctate (speckled, dot-like) calcifications in one or more tarsal bones.

Name: Medial rotation of the medial malleolus
Irregular tarsal ossification
Def: Defective ossification in an irregular pattern of the seven bones of the foot comprising the calcaneus, talus, cuboid, navicular, and the cuneiform bones.

Name: Equinus calcaneus
Def: Abnormal plantar flexion of the calcaneus relative to the longitudinal axis of the tibia. This results in the angle between the long axis of the tibia and the long axis of the heel bone (calcaneus) being greater than 90 degrees.

Name: Delayed calcaneal ossification
Def: Delayed maturation and calcification of the calcaneus.

Name: Impaired epinephrine-induced platelet aggregation
Def: Abnormal response to epinephrine as manifested by reduced or lacking aggregation of platelets upon addition of epinephrine.

Name: Elevated serum transaminases during infections
Def: Elevations of the levels of SGOT (serum glutamic oxaloacetic transaminase) and SGPT (serum glutamic pyruvic transaminase) that occur during infections.

Name: Prolonged prothrombin time
Def: Increased time to coagulation in the prothrombin time test, which is a measure of the extrinsic pathway of coagulation. The results of the prothrombin time test are often expressed in terms of the International normalized ratio (INR), which is calculated as a ratio of the patient's prothrombin time (PT) to a control PT standardized for the potency of the thromboplastin reagent developed by the World Health Organization (WHO) using the formula: INR is equal to Patient PT divided by Control PT.
Comment: The prothrombin time (PT) and the activated partial thromboplastin time (APTT) are the most requested tests to investigate patients with congenital or acquired coagulopathies and drug monitoring. They are defined as the time (seconds) needed to clot platelet-poor plasma upon addition of coagulation triggers, such as tissue factor in complex with phospholipids and calcium chloride (in the PT), or negatively charged phospholipids-activators and calcium chloride (in the APTT). They can hence be considered as global coagulation tests sensitive to deficiencies of many coagulation factors. In brief, they are both sensitive to factor X, V, II and fibrinogen, whereas the PT is only sensitive to factor VII deficiency and the APTT is sensitive to pre-kallikrein, high molecular weight kininogen (HMWK), factor XII, XI, IX and VIII deficiencies. Normal plasma in the PT clots approximately within 10-12 s upon triggering coagulation, and the normal reference range is (usually) narrow. PT results have been reported as clotting time, percentage activity, PT-ratio (patient-to-normal clotting time) and as international normalized ratio (INR). The INR scale has been devised to harmonize results stemming from different thromboplastins from patients on treatment with vitamin K antagonists. Some recommend abandoning the approach of using percentage activity to assess PR.

Name: Periodic hypokalemic paresis
Def: Episodes of muscle weakness associated with reduced levels of potassium in the blood.

Name: Mucopolysacchariduria
Def: Excessive amounts of mucopolysaccharide in the urine.
Comment: This finding is suggestive of the diagnosis of a mucopolysaccharidosis.

Name: Hyperapobetalipoproteinemia
Def: Hyperapobetalipoproteinemia is defined as the combination of a normal low density lipoprotein (LDL) cholesterol in the face of an increased LDL apolipoprotein B (apoB) protein.

Name: 3-hydroxydicarboxylic aciduria
Def: An increase in the level of 3-hydroxydicarboxylic acid in the urine.

Name: Absent leukocyte alkaline phosphatase
Def: A decrease in alkaline phosphatase activity measured within leukocytes below detectable levels .

Name: Asymptomatic hyperammonemia
Def: An increased concentration of ammonia in the blood not associated with symptoms such as encephalopathy.

Name: Decreased circulating cortisol level
Def: Abnormally reduced concentration of cortisol in the blood.

Name: Decreased proportion circulating T-helper cells
Def: Reduced proportion of helper T cells relative to the total number of T cells.

Name: Decreased beta-galactosidase activity
Def: Abnormally decreased rate of beta-galactosidase activity. Beta-galactosidase activity can be measured in leukocyte, fibroblast, or plasma.
Synonym: Beta-galactosidase deficiency in fibroblasts and white blood cells

Name: Very long chain fatty acid accumulation
Reduced factor VII activity
Def: Reduced activity of coagulation factor VII. Factor VII is part of the extrinsic coagulation pathway, which is initiated at the site of injury in response to the release of tissue factor (fIII). Tissue factor and activated factor VII catalyze the activation of factor X.

Name: Decreased Arden ratio of electrooculogram
Def: An abnormal reduction in the Arden ratio, which is the ratio between the light peak and the dark trough of the smoothed (physiologic) EOG record.

Name: Mildly elevated creatine kinase
Comment: 'has part' some \n('increased amount' and ('inheres in' some blood) and (towards some IMR_0002602) and ('has modifier' some 'mild intensity') and ('has modifier' some abnormal))

Name: Abetalipoproteinemia
Def: An absence of low-density lipoprotein cholesterol in the blood.
Comment: Beta-lipoprotein cholesterol is a synonym for low-density lipoprotein (LDL) cholesterol.

Name: Precocious puberty in males
Def: The onset of puberty before the age of 9 years in boys.
Synonym: Early onset of puberty in males

Name: Adrenocortical cytomegaly
Def: The presence of large polyhedral cells with eosinophilic granular cytoplasm and enlarged nuclei in the adrenal cortex.
Comment: This feature is common in Beckwith Wiedemann syndrome.

Name: Absence of secondary sex characteristics
Def: No secondary sexual characteristics are present at puberty.
Synonym: No secondary sexual characteristics at puberty

Name: Insulin insensitivity
Def: Decreased sensitivity toward insulin.

Name: Thyroid agenesis
Def: The congenital absence of the thyroid gland.

Name: Multiple pancreatic beta-cell adenomas
Def: The presence of multiple pancreatic islet cell adenomas.

Name: Congenital hypoparathyroidism
Def: Deficiency of parathyroid hormone with congenital onset.

Name: Primary hyperparathyroidism
Def: A type of hyperparathyroidism caused by a primary abnormality of the parathyroid glands (e.g., adenoma, carcinoma, hyperplasia). Primary hyperparathyroidism is associated with hyercalcemia.

Name: Reduced circulating prolactin concentration
Def: A reduced level of prolactin in the blood circulation. Prolactin is a protein hormone that is secreted by lactotrophs in the anterior pituitary and that stimulates mammary gland development and milk production.

Name: Precocious puberty with Sertoli cell tumor
Insulin-dependent but ketosis-resistant diabetes
Def: Ketosis-resistant diabetes is a synonym for type II diabetes. This term thus refers to a form of type II diabetes in which patients are dependent on insulin.

Name: Primary adrenal insufficiency
Def: Insufficient production of steroid hormones (primarily cortisol) by the adrenal glands as a result of a primary defect in the glands themselves.
Comment: Deficiency of both glucocorticoids and mineralocorticoids.

Name: Parathyroid hyperplasia
Def: Hyperplasia of the parathyroid gland.
Comment: An absolute increase in the mass of the parenchymal cells of the parathyroid gland leading to an enlargement of the parathyroid glands.

Name: Premature ovarian insufficiency
Def: Amenorrhea due to loss of ovarian function before the age of 40. Primary ovarian inssuficiency (POI) is a state of female hypergonadotropic hypogonadism. It can manifest as primary amenorrhea with onset before menarche or secondary amenorrhea.
Comment: The causes of primary ovarian insuficiency (POI) include chromosomal and genetic defects, autoimmune processes, chemotherapy, radiation, infections and surgery, but many are unidentified (idiopathic). The age of 40 is set by convention but is supported by clinical observations. From a statistical point of view, the age limit of 40 is approximately two standard deviations (SD) below the average age at natural menopause (50 plus/minus 4 years).

Name: Parathyroid agenesis
Def: Aplasia of the parathyroid gland.

Name: Gonadotropin deficiency
Def: A reduced ability to secrete gonadotropins, which are protein hormones secreted by gonadotrope cells of the anterior pituitary gland, including the hormones follitropin (FSH) and luteinizing hormone (LH).

Name: Decreased serum estradiol
Def: A reduction below normal concentration of estradiol in the circulation.

Name: Adrenal gland dysgenesis
Def: Abnormal development of the adrenal gland.

Name: Adrenal hyperplasia
Def: Enlargement of the adrenal gland.

Name: Compensated hypothyroidism
Def: Condition associated with a raised serum concentration of thyroid stimulating hormone (TSH) but a normal serum free thyroxine (FT4).

Name: Androgen insufficiency
Def: Insufficient amount of androgenic activity.

Name: Pituitary resistance to thyroid hormone
Def: A condition in which the pituitary gland is partially resistant to thyroid hormone, so that it continues to secrete thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH) until the blood level of thyroid hormone rises higher than normal.

Name: Thyroid lymphangiectasia
Def: The presence of lymphangiectasis of the thyroid gland.
Comment: A stretching and widening of the lymphatic vessels of the thyroid gland.

Name: Elevated circulating follicle stimulating hormone level
Def: An elevated concentration of follicle-stimulating hormone in the blood.
Synonym: Increased circulating follicle stimulating hormone level

Name: Decreased circulating progesterone
Def: An reduced concentration of progesterone in the blood.
Comment: Progesterone is a steroid hormone secreted by the corpus luteum after ovulation during the second half of the menstrual cycle.

Name: Hypothalamic hypothyroidism
Def: A type of hypothyroidism that results from a defect in thyrotropin-releasing hormone activity.
Comment: The simultaneous occurrence a low thyroid hormone level and a normal or low serum level of thyroid stimulating hormone (TSH) in a patient with hypothyroidism establishes the diagnosis of secondary hypothyroidism. The administration of thyrotropin releasing hormone (TRH), which is normally synthesized and released by the hypothalamus, enables the physician to distinguish between pituitary and hypothalamic causes of hypothyroidism.\nTRH will normally cause the release of TSH from the pituitary gland. When the hypothalamus does not synthesize or release TRH, the administration of exogenous TRH will result in prompt rise of serum TSH. To date, the cases reported of pituitary hypothyroidism. Hypothalamic hypothyroidism, on the other hand, may either be idiopathic or result from demonstrable hypothalamic disease.

Name: Adrenal medullary hypoplasia
Def: Developmental hypoplasia of the adrenal medulla.

Name: Pseudohypoaldosteronism
Def: A state of renal tubular unresponsiveness or resistance to the action of aldosterone.
Comment: Pseudohypoaldosteronism is characterized by hyperkalemia, metabolic acidosis, and normal glomerular filtration rate. This term refers to the phenotypic finding of pseudohypoaldosteronism rather than the disease of idiopathic pseudohypoaldosteronism.

Name: Congenital adrenal hypoplasia
Def: A type of adrenal hypoplasia with congenital onset.

Name: Pituitary hypothyroidism
Def: A type of hypothyroidism that results from a defect in thyroid-stimulating hormone secretion.
Synonym: Low thyroid gland function due to abnormal pituitary gland

Name: Euthyroid hyperthyroxinemia
Def: An abnormality of thyroid physiology (HP:0002926) characterized by increased levels of thyroxine without evidence of clinical thyroid disease.
Comment: Any functional abnormality of the thyroid gland and the systems that control its rate of production of thyroid hormone (hypothalamic-pituitary-thyroid axis) and the peripheral reactivity to thyroid hormone.

Name: Thyroid hyperplasia
Def: Hyperplasia of the thyroid gland.

Name: Congenital goiter
Def: An enlargement of the thyroid gland with congenital onset.

Name: Adrenocortical adenoma
Def: Adrenocortical adenomas are benign tumors of the adrenal cortex.

Name: Congenital adrenal hyperplasia
Def: A type of adrenal hyperplasia with congenital onset.

Name: Adrenocorticotropin receptor defect
Def: Adrenal insufficiency secondary to a defect in the ACTH receptor.

Name: Pancreatic islet cell adenoma
Def: The presence of an adenoma of the pancreas with origin in a pancreatic B cell.

Name: Thyroid defect in oxidation and organification of iodide
Neutrophil inclusion bodies
Def: The presence of intracellular inclusion bodies (aggregates of stainable substances, usually proteins) in neutrophils. Cytoplasmic neutrophil inclusions (oval, basophilic) are also known as Doehle bodies.

Name: Increased red cell hemolysis by shear stress
Abnormal cartilage collagen
Def: Abnormal morphology of collagen fibers in cartilage. In cartilage, collagen II, actually a collagen II:IX:XI heterofibril, is by far the most important type of collagen. A number of abnormalities may be appreciated by electron micrography or biochemical investigations, including sparse collagen fibers in the cartilage matrix.

Name: Abnormal blood zinc concentration
Def: An abnormality of zinc ion homeostasis.

Name: Cerebellar cortical atrophy
Def: Atrophy (wasting) of the cerebellar cortex.
Comment: Cerebellar cortical atrophy may be associated with vacuolated or binucleated Purkinje cells.

Name: Acute hyperammonemia
Def: An increased concentration of ammonia in the blood with sudden onset.

Name: Unconjugated hyperbilirubinemia
Def: An increased amount of unconjugated (indirect) bilurubin in the blood.

Name: Fasting hyperinsulinemia
Def: An increased concentration of insulin in the blood in the fasting state, i.e., not as the response to food intake.
Synonym: High blood insulin levels while fasting

Name: Partial complement factor H deficiency
