Synonym: Decreased UDP-glucose 4-epimerase activity activity in plasma

Name: Abnormal uridine diphosphate glucose-4-epimerase activity in red blood cells
Def: An abnormality in uridine diphosphate glucose-4-epimerase activity in red blood cells. Uridine diphosphate glucose-4-epimerase catalyzes the reaction: UDP-glucose = UDP-galactose.
Synonym: Abnormal UDP-glucose 4-epimerase activity activity in RBCs
Abnormal UDP-glucose 4-epimerase activity activity in red blood cells

Name: Increased uridine diphosphate glucose-4-epimerase activity in red blood cells
Def: An increase in uridine diphosphate glucose-4-epimerase activity in red blood cells. Uridine diphosphate glucose-4-epimerase catalyzes the reaction: UDP-glucose = UDP-galactose.
Synonym: Increased UDP-glucose 4-epimerase activity activity in RBCs
Increased UDP-glucose 4-epimerase activity activity in red blood cells

Name: Decreased uridine diphosphate glucose-4-epimerase activity in red blood cells
Def: A decrease in uridine diphosphate glucose-4-epimerase activity in red blood cells. Uridine diphosphate glucose-4-epimerase catalyzes the reaction: UDP-glucose = UDP-galactose.
Synonym: Decreased UDP-glucose 4-epimerase activity activity in RBCs
Decreased UDP-glucose 4-epimerase activity activity in red blood cells

Name: Increased CSF urate concentration
Def: Increased concentration of urate in the cerebrospinal fluid.

Name: Positive meconium barbiturate test
Def: Detection of barbiturate metabolites such as phenobarbital in meconium.

Name: Positive hair barbiturate test
Def: Detection of barbiturate metabolites such as phenobarbital in the hair.

Name: Positive stool barbiturate test
Def: Detection of barbiturate metabolites such as phenobarbital in the stool.

Name: Positive gastric fluid barbiturate test
Def: Detection of barbiturate metabolites such as phenobarbital in the gastric fluid.

Name: Increased intestinal transit time
Def: An increase in the length of time required for food to pass through the intestines.

Name: Abnormal circulating nicotinurate level
Def: Any deviation from the normal concentration of nicotinurate in the blood.
Comment: Nicotinuric acid is an acyl glycine, which are normally minor metabolites of fatty acids. However, the excretion of certain acyl glycines is increased in several inborn errors of metabolism. In certain cases the measurement of these metabolites in body fluids can be used to diagnose disorders associated with mitochondrial fatty acid beta-oxidation. Nicotinuric acid is the major detoxification product of nicotinic acid. It may serve as a simple quantitative index of hepatic biotransformation of nicotinic acid. {xref="PMID:3243933"}

Name: Increased circulating nicotinurate level
Def: An increased amount of nicotinurate in the blood.

Name: Positive methadone plasma/serum test
Def: Detection of methadone or its metabolite 2-ethylidene-1,5-dimethyl-3,3- diphenylpyrrolidine (EDDP) in plasma or serum.
Comment: Methadone is an opioid drug that is used to treat severe pain or in the treatment of individiuals with opioid dependency.

Name: Positive plasma/serum cotinine test
Def: Detection of cotinine, an alkaloid found in tobacco and the predominant metabolite of nicotine, in plasma or serum.
Comment: Cotinine is used as a biomarker for exposure to tobacco smoke.

Name: Folate deficiency in CSF
Def: A reduced concentration of folic acid, which is also known as vitamin B9 in the cerebrospinal fluid.
Comment: Cerebral folate deficiency is usually measured as low levels of folate in the CSF, in the presence of normal folate metabolism outside the nervous system.

Name: Abnormal cord blood measurement
Def: An abnormality in any umbilical cord measurement performed after birth, such as the blood gas level.

Name: Abnormal blood gas level in cord blood
Hyperoxemia in cord blood
Def: An abnormally high level of blood oxygen in the cord blood.

Name: Hypoxemia in cord blood
Def: An abnormally low level of blood oxygen in the cord blood.

Name: Hypercapnia in cord blood
Def: Abnormally elevated blood carbon dioxide (CO2) level in the cord blood.
Synonym: High cord blood carbon dioxide level

Name: Hypocapnia in cord blood
Def: Abnormally decreased blood carbon dioxide (CO2) level in the cord blood.
Synonym: Low cord blood carbon dioxide level

Name: Abnormal blood 5-methyltetrahydrofolate level
Def: An abnormal concentration of 5-methyltetrahydrofolate in the blood.

Name: Reduced blood 5-methyltetrahydrofolate level
Def: A decreased concentration of 5-methyltetrahydrofolate in the blood.

Name: Hypoplasia of maxilla relative to mandible
Def: Abnormally small dimension of the maxilla (upper jaw) relative to the mandible (lower jaw).
Synonym: Disorder of maxillary and mandibular dental arch relationship

Name: Hypoplasia of mandible relative to maxilla
Def: Abnormally small dimension of the mandible (lower jaw) relative to the maxilla (upper jaw).
Synonym: Disorder of mandibular and maxillary dental arch relationship

Name: Increased anti-dairy protein IgE antibody level
Def: Increased level of IgE antibody against dairy proteins, including casein, alpha-lactalbumin, beta-lactoglobulin or bovine serum albumin contained in cow, sheep or goat milk and milk products.

Name: Increased anti-animal protein IgE antibody level
Def: Increased level of IgE antibody against animal proteins, such as albumins that are present in animal hair, dander, shed skin, saliva and urine.
Comment: For animal dander annotations, there is a more specific subclass of this term.
Synonym: Increased level of anti-animal protein IgE antibody

Name: Increased anti-seafood IgE antibody level
Def: Increased level of IgE antibody against seafood, including fish, shrimp, lobster, crab, squid and abalone.
Synonym: Increased level of anti-seafood IgE antibody

Name: Increased anti-dust mite IgE antibody level
Def: Increased level of IgE antibody against dust mites, such as house dust mites.
Synonym: Increased level of anti-dust mite IgE antibody

Name: Increased anti-bacteria IgE antibody level
Def: Increased level of IgE antibody against bacteria.
Synonym: Increased level of anti-bacteria IgE antibody

Name: Increased anti-drug IgE antibody level
Def: Increased level of IgE antibody against a drug or class of drugs, such as antibiotics.
Synonym: Increased level of anti-drug IgE antibody

Name: Increased anti-feather IgE antibody level
Def: Increased level of IgE antibody against feathers, which could be indicative of an allergy against feathers themselves, or mite allergens present in feathers.

Name: Increased anti-food allergen IgE antibody level
Def: Increased level of IgE antibody against proteins found in foods, such as milk, egg, soy, wheat, peanut, treenut, fish, and shellfish.
Synonym: Increased level of anti-food allergen IgE antibody

Name: Increased anti-plant based food allergen IgE antibody level
Def: Increased level of IgE antibody against a plant based food allergen, including vegetables and fruits.
Synonym: Increased level of anti-plant based food allergen IgE antibody

Name: Increased anti-gluten IgE antibody level
Def: Increased level of IgE antibody against gluten, a protein found in wheat, barley, and rye.
Synonym: Increased level of anti-gluten IgE antibody

Name: Increased anti-nut food product IgE antibody level
Def: Increased level of IgE antibody against nut food products such as peanuts or tree nuts, such as hazelnuts, walnuts, cashews, and almonds.

Name: Increased anti-egg IgE antibody level
Def: Increased level of IgE antibody against eggs, including egg whites, egg yolks, and egg proteins such as ovoalbumin and ovomucoid.

Name: Increased anti-fungi IgE antibody level
Def: Increased level of IgE antibody against fungus, such as molds like zygomycota, ascomycota and deuteromycota.

Name: Increased anti-meat allergen IgE antibody level
Def: Increased level of IgE antibody against meat, such as mammalian meat, including beef or pork, or poultry, like duck or chicken.

Name: Increased anti-parasite IgE antibody level
Def: Increased level of IgE antibody against parasites, such as helminths (parasitic worms, such as Ascaris lumbricoides, Trichuris trichiura, Ancylostoma duodenalis, Necator americanus, Strongyloides stercoralis) or parasites such as Toxoplasma gondii.

Name: Increased anti-insect IgE antibody level
Def: Increased level of IgE antibody against antigens from insects such as moths, mosquitos, or cockroaches.

Name: Increased anti-venom IgE antibody level
Def: Increased level of IgE antibody against venom from insects such as bees, wasps, hornets, yellowjackets.

Name: Increased anti-plant product IgE antibody level
Def: Increased level of IgE antibody against antigens from plants and products derived from plants, such as wood or pollen.

Name: Positive urine norcotinine test
Def: Detection of norcotinine, a metabolite of nicotine, in urine.

Name: Abnormal IgA level
Def: An abnormal deviation from normal levels of IgA immunoglobulin in blood.

Name: Abnormal IgE level
Def: An abnormal deviation from normal levels of IgE immunoglobulin in blood.

Name: Abnormal IgG level
Def: An abnormal deviation from normal levels of IgG immunoglobulin in blood.

Name: Abnormal IgM level
Def: An abnormal deviation from normal levels of IgM immunoglobulin in blood.

Name: Abnormal IgD level
Def: An abnormal deviation from normal levels of IgD immunoglobulin in blood.

Name: Decreased circulating total IgD
Def: An abnormally decreased level of immunoglobulin D (IgD) in blood.

Name: Increased circulating IgD level
Def: An abnormally increased level of immunoglobulin D in blood.

Name: Increased anti-animal dander IgE antibody level
Def: Increased level of IgE antibody against animal dander, tiny scales shed from animal skin or hair, such as from pet dogs or cats.
Synonym: Increased level of anti-dander IgE antibody

Name: Increased anti-house dust mite IgE antibody level
Def: Increased level of IgE antibody against house dust mites, a common allergen.
Synonym: Increased anti-house dust IgE antibody level
Increased level of anti-house dust IgE antibody

Name: Increased anti-alpha-gal IgE antibody level
Def: Increased level of IgE antibody against galactose-alpha-1, 3 galactose (alpha-gal), a carbohydrate found in mammalian meat.
Synonym: Increased anti-galactose-alpha-1, 3 galactose IgE antibody level

Name: Abnormal L-selectin shedding
Def: An abnormality in the cleavage of L-selectin during the process of guiding neutrophils to the site of infection. Proteolytic cleavage of L-selectin results in rapid shedding from the cell surface, which has a role in neutrophil rolling and accumulation at the site of infection.

Name: Chronic neutropenia
Def: Neutropenia with an absolute neutrophil count (ANC) less than 1,500,000,000/L lasting for more than 3 months.

Name: Chronic neutropenia in myeloid maturation arrest in bone marrow
Def: Chornic neutropenia arising from an impaired proliferation and maturation of myeloid progenitor cells in the bone marrow.

Name: Cyclic neutropenia in myeloid maturation arrest in bone marrow
Def: Cyclic neutropenia arising from an impaired proliferation and maturation of myeloid progenitor cells in the bone marrow.

Name: Transient neutropenia
Def: A transient reduction in the number of neutrophils in the peripheral blood. Transient neutropenia is most commonly associated with viral infections, but other causes include drugs and autoimmunity.

Name: Infection associated neutropenia
Def: Transient neutropenia caused by an infection, such as with a virus, bacteria or protozoan.

Name: Neutrophilia in presence of infection
Def: An increased number of neutrophils circulating in the blood during an infection, such as with a bacteria, virus or fungus.

Name: Neutrophilia in absence of infection
Def: An increased number of neutrophils circulating in the blood in the absence of an infection. Factors contributing to neutrophilia could include inflammation or congenital disorders.

Name: Hepatopulmonary fusion
Def: Fusion of the liver with the lung.

Name: Asymmetrical gluteal crease
Def: The presence of an asymmetrical gluteal crease, the horizontal crease formed by the inferior aspect of the buttocks and the posterior upper leg.

Name: Wide space between 4th and 5th toe
Def: A widely spaced gap between the fourth toe and the fifth (pinky) toe.
Synonym: Wide space between the 4th and 5th toe

Name: Lower cranial nerve dysfunction
Def: A functional abnormality affecting the lower cranial nerves, which include the paired 9th (glossopharyngeal), 10th (vagal), 11th (accessory) and 12th (hypoglossal) cranial nerves.

Name: Brain imaging abnormality
Def: An anomaly of metabolism or structure of the brain identified by imaging.

Name: Subglottic hemangioma
Def: A hemangioma, a benign tumor of the vascular endothelial cells, located in the airway, typically below the vocal chords, that can cause severe obstruction of the airway.

Name: Supraglottic hemangioma
Def: A hemangioma, a benign tumor of the vascular endothelial cells, located in the upper part of the larynx (voice box) including the epiglottis; the area above the vocal cords.

Name: Visceral hemangioma
Def: A hemangioma arising from within visceral structures, the internal organs of the body.

Name: Intestinal hemangioma
Def: A hemangioma, a benign tumor of the vascular endothelial cells, located in the intestines, which includes the bowel.

Name: Spleen hemangioma
Def: A hemangioma, a benign tumor of the vascular endothelial cells, that is located in the spleen.

Name: Labial hemangioma
Def: A hemangioma, a benign tumor of the vascular endothelial cells, that is located in the upper lip.

Name: Esophageal hemangioma
Def: A hemangioma, a benign tumor of the vascular endothelial cells, that is located in the esophagus.

Name: Laryngeal hemangioma
Def: A hemangioma, a benign tumor of the vascular endothelial cells, that is located in the glottic or supraglottic regions.

Name: Vulvar hemangioma
Def: A hemangioma, a benign tumor of the vascular endothelial cells, that is located in the vulva.

Name: Retropharyngeal hemangioma
Def: A hemangioma, a benign tumor of the vascular endothelial cells, that is located in the retropharyngeal space, the portion of the peripharyngeal space that is located posterior to the pharynx.

Name: Paraspinal hemangioma
Def: A hemangioma, a benign tumor of the vascular endothelial cells, that is located in the paraspinal muscular region, the muscles next to the spine.

Name: Lumbosacral hemangioma
Def: A spinal cord hemangioma located in the lumbosacral spine region.

Name: Supraumbilical raphe
Def: An abnormality of the sternum that presents at birth as a ventral sternal non-union defect, due to an abnormality of the fusion of the layers of the skin. It presents as a scar-like line that extends upward from the umbilicus (belly button).

Name: Sternal pit
Def: A sternal pit is a small indentation or dimple in the skin overlying the sternum of the chest. In some cases, the skin defect can be linear, extending several inches over the sternum.

Name: Pituitary gland cyst
Def: A fluid-filled sacs that develop on or near the pituitary gland.

Name: Atrophic pituitary gland
Def: Partial or complete wasting (loss) of the pituitary gland.

Name: Pediatric onset
Def: Onset of disease manifestations before adulthood, defined here as before the age of 16 years, but excluding neonatal or congenital onset.

Name: Dyspepsia
Def: A heterogeneous group of symptoms that are localized in the epigastric region. Typical dyspeptic symptoms include postprandial fullness, early satiation, epigastric pain and epigastric burning, but other upper gastrointestinal symptoms such as nausea, belching or abdominal bloating often occur.

Name: Abnormal circulating amylase level
Def: A deviation from the normal concentration of amylase in the blood, an enzyme which helps digest glycogen and starch. It is produced mainly in the pancreas and salivary glands.

Name: Positive blood acetaminophen test
Def: Detection of acetaminophen in the blood.

Name: Positive norpropoxyphene blood test
Def: Detection of norpropoxyphene in the blood, a major metabolite of the opioid analgesic drug dextropropoxyphene.

Name: Positive meconium methadone test
Def: Detection of methadone or its metabolite 2-ethylidene-1,5-dimethyl-3,3- diphenylpyrrolidine (EDDP) in meconium.

Name: Positive blood molindone test
Def: Detection of molindone in the blood, an antipyschotic used for treatment of schizophrenia.

Name: Intrathoracic hemangioma
Def: A hemangioma, a benign tumor of the vascular endothelial cells, that is located in the intrathoracic or chest region.

Name: Hyperamylasemia
Def: Increased level of amylase in the blood, an enzyme which helps digest glycogen and starch. It is produced mainly in the pancreas and salivary glands.

Name: Hypoamylasemia
Def: Decreased level of amylase in the blood, an enzyme which helps digest glycogen and starch. It is produced mainly in the pancreas and salivary glands.

Name: Positive urine norpropoxyphene test
Def: Detection of norpropoxyphene in urine.

Name: Negativism
Def: Opposing or not responding to instructions or external stimuli.

Name: Abnormal isohemagglutinin level
Def: An abnormal level of isohemagglutinin in the blood. An isohemagglutinin refers to the naturally occurring antibodies in the ABO blood group system (i.e., anti-A in a group B person, anti-B in a group A person, and anti-A, anti-B, and anti-A,B in a group O person).
Synonym: Abnormal level of natural antibody to blood group agents

Name: Absent isohemagglutinin level
Def: Absent or undetectable level of isohemagglutinin. An isohemagglutinin refers to the naturally occurring antibodies in the ABO blood group system (i.e., anti-A in a group B person, anti-B in a group A person, and anti-A, anti-B, and anti-A,B in a group O person).
Synonym: Absent natural antibody to blood group agents

Name: Decreased specific antibody response to protein vaccine
Def: A reduced ability to synthesize postvaccination antibodies against proteins in vaccines, as measured by antibody titer determination following vaccination.

Name: Complete or near-complete absence of specific antibody response to tetanus vaccine
Def: The inability to synthesize postvaccination antibodies against a tetanus antigen, as measured by antibody titer determination following vaccination.

Name: Complete or near-complete absence of specific antibody response to hepatitis B vaccine
Def: The inability to synthesize postvaccination antibodies against a hepatisis B antigen, as measured by antibody titer determination following vaccination.

Name: Partial absence of specific antibody response to tetanus vaccine
Def: A reduced ability to synthesize postvaccination antibodies against a tetanus antigen, as measured by antibody titer determination following vaccination.

Name: Partial absence of specific antibody response to hepatitis B vaccine
Def: A reduced ability to synthesize postvaccination antibodies against a hepatitis B antigen, as measured by antibody titer determination following vaccination.

Name: Decreased specific antibody response to polysaccharide vaccine
Def: A reduced ability to synthesize postvaccination antibodies against polysaccharides in vaccines, as measured by antibody titer determination following vaccination.

Name: Complete or near-complete absence of specific antibody response to pneumococcus vaccine
Def: The inability to synthesize postvaccination antibodies against a pneumococcus antigen, as measured by antibody titer determination following vaccination.

Name: Partial absence of specific antibody response to pneumococcus vaccine
Def: A reduced ability to synthesize postvaccination antibodies against a pneumococcus antigen, as measured by antibody titer determination following vaccination.

Name: Decreased specific antibody response to protein-conjugated polysaccharide vaccine
Def: A reduced ability to synthesize postvaccination antibodies against protein-conjugated polysaccharides in vaccines, as measured by antibody titer determination following vaccination.

Name: Complete or near-complete absence of specific antibody response to Haemophilus influenzae type b (Hib) vaccine
Def: The inability to synthesize postvaccination antibodies against a Haemophilus influenzae type b (Hib) antigen, as measured by antibody titer determination following vaccination.

Name: Complete or near-complete absence of specific antibody response to meningococcus vaccine
Def: The inability to synthesize postvaccination antibodies against a meningococcus antigen, as measured by antibody titer determination following vaccination.

Name: Partial absence of specific antibody response to Haemophilus influenzae type b (Hib) vaccine
Def: A reduced ability to synthesize postvaccination antibodies against a Haemophilus influenzae type b (Hib) antigen, as measured by antibody titer determination following vaccination.

Name: Partial absence of specific antibody response to meningococcus vaccine
Def: A reduced ability to synthesize postvaccination antibodies against a meningococcus antigen, as measured by antibody titer determination following vaccination.

Name: Positive stool methadone test
Def: Detection of methadone and its metabolites in the stool.

Name: Decreased specific antibody response to infection
Def: A reduced ability to synthesize antibodies against antigens from an infectious agent or pathogen (such as bacteria, viruses, parasites, etc.), as measured by antibody titer determination following infection.

Name: Alpha-aminoadipic aciduria
Def: A increased concentration of alpha-aminoadipic acid in the urine.

Name: Abnormality of neutrophil morphology in CSF
Def: An abnormal form or size of neutrophils in the cerebrospinal fluid.
Synonym: Abnormality of neutrophil morphology in cerebrospinal fluid

Name: Hyposegmentation of neutrophil nuclei in CSF
Def: Hyposegmented (hypolobulated) or bilobed neutrophil nuclei in the cerebrospinal fluid.
Synonym: Hyposegmentation of neutrophil nuclei in cerebrospinal fluid

Name: Hypersegmentation of neutrophil nuclei in CSF
Def: An excessive division of the lobes of the nucleus of a neutrophil in the cerebrospinal fluid.
Synonym: Hypersegmentation of neutrophil nuclei in cerebrospinal fluid

Name: Abnormal urinary 1-methylhistidine concentration
Def: Abnormal concentration of 1-methylhistidine in the urine.

Name: Decreased urinary 1-methylhistidine
Def: Decreased concentration of 1-methylhistidine in the urine.

Name: Increased urinary 1-methylhistidine
Def: Increased concentration of 1-methylhistidine in the urine.

Name: Abnormal urinary 3-methylhistidine concentration
Def: Abnormal concentration of 3-methylhistidine in the urine.

Name: Increased urinary 3-methylhistidine
Def: Increased concentration of 3-methylhistidine in the urine.

Name: Decreased urinary 3-methylhistidine
Def: Decreased concentration of 3-methylhistidine in the urine.

Name: Alpha-gal allergy
Def: Hypersensitivity in form of an adverse immune reaction against alpha-gal.

Name: Animal protein allergy
Def: Hypersensitivity in form of an adverse immune reaction against animal proteins.

Name: Animal dander allergy
Def: Hypersensitivity in form of an adverse immune reaction against animal dander.

Name: Bacteria allergy
Def: Hypersensitivity in form of an adverse immune reaction against bacteria.

Name: Drug allergy
Def: Hypersensitivity in form of an adverse immune reaction against drugs.

Name: Dust mite allergy
Def: Hypersensitivity in form of an adverse immune reaction against dust mites.

Name: House dust mite allergy
Def: Hypersensitivity in form of an adverse immune reaction against house dust mites.
Synonym: Immunoglobulin E-mediated house dust mite allergy

Name: Feather allergy
Def: Hypersensitivity in form of an adverse immune reaction against feathers.

Name: Dairy allergy
Def: Hypersensitivity in form of an adverse immune reaction against dairy.

Name: Egg allergy
Def: Hypersensitivity in form of an adverse immune reaction against eggs.

Name: Gluten allergy
Def: Hypersensitivity in form of an adverse immune reaction against gluten.
Comment: A gluten allergy is usually distinct from gluten sensitivity or Celiac disease.

Name: Meat allergen allergy
Def: Hypersensitivity in form of an adverse immune reaction against allergens contained in meat products.

Name: Nut food product allergy
Def: Hypersensitivity in form of an adverse immune reaction against nut food products.
Synonym: Immunoglobulin E-mediated nut food product allergy

Name: Plant based food allergy
Def: Hypersensitivity in form of an adverse immune reaction against plant based food allergens.
Synonym: Allergy to plant based food allergens
IgE-mediated plant based food allergen allergy
Immunoglobulin E-mediated plant based food allergen allergy

Name: Seafood allergy
Def: Hypersensitivity in form of an adverse immune reaction against seafood.

Name: Fungi allergy
Def: Hypersensitivity in form of an adverse immune reaction against fungus.

Name: Insect allergy
Def: Hypersensitivity in form of an adverse immune reaction against insects.

Name: Venom allergy
Def: Hypersensitivity in form of an adverse immune reaction against insect venom.

Name: Parasite allergy
Def: Hypersensitivity in form of an adverse immune reaction against parasites.

Name: Plant product allergy
Def: Hypersensitivity in form of an adverse immune reaction against plant products.

Name: Insect bite allergy
Def: Hypersensitivity in form of an adverse immune reaction against insect bites.

Name: Focal epithelial hyperplasia of oral mucosa
Def: The occurrence of multiple or unique whitish or normal in color small papules or nodules in oral cavity, especially on labial and buccal mucosa, lower lip and tongue, and less often on the upper lip, gingiva and palate.
Synonym: Focal epithelial hyperplasia of the lining of mouth

Name: Abnormal circulating heparan sulfate level
Def: An abnormal level of heparan sulfate in the blood.
Synonym: Abnormality of the concentration of heparan sulfate in the blood

Name: Increased circulating heparan sulfate level
Def: An abnormal increase in the concentration of heparan sulfate in the blood.

Name: Decreased circulating heparan sulfate level
Def: An abnormal decrease in the concentration of heparan sulfate in the blood.

Name: Shortened O-fucosylated glycan on properdin
Def: Decreased length of O-fucosylated glycans present on properdin.
Synonym: Presence of terminal O-fucose glycans on properdin

Name: Increased urinary polyhexose
Def: An abnormal increase in the concentration of polyhexose in the urine.

Name: Increased urinary galactosylated oligosaccharide
Def: An abnormal increase in the concentration of galactosylated oligosaccharides in urine.
Synonym: Increased concentration of galactosylated oligosaccharides in urine

Name: Increased urinary high-mannose-type oligosaccharide
Def: An abnormal increase in the concentration of high-mannose-type oligosaccharides in the urine.
Synonym: Increased concentration of high-mannose-type oligosaccharides in urine

Name: Increased urinary multiantennary sialylated oligosaccharide
Def: An abnormal increase in the concentration of multiantennary sialylated oligosaccharides in the urine.
Synonym: Increase concentration of multiantennary sialylated oligosaccharides in urine

Name: Decreased glycosyltransferase O-Fucosylpeptide 3-Beta-N-Acetylglucosaminyltransferase activity
Def: An abnormal decrease in glycosyltransferase O-fucosylpeptide 3-beta-N-acetylglucosaminyltransferase enzymatic activity.

Name: Increased urinary fucosylated oligosaccharide
Def: An abnormal increase in the concentrationl of small fucosylated oligosaccharides in the urine.
Synonym: Increased concentration of fucosylated oligosaccharides in urine

Name: Abnormal complex N-glycan level
Def: An abnormal concentration of complex N-glycans on glycoproteins.
Synonym: Abnormal concentration of complex N-glycans on glycoproteins

Name: Increased complex N-glycan level
Def: An abnormal increase in the concentration of complex N-glycans on glycoproteins.
Synonym: Increased concentration of complex N-glycans on glycoproteins

Name: Decreased complex N-glycan level
Def: An abnormal decrease in the concentration of complex N-glycans on glycoproteins.
Synonym: Increased truncated complex N-glycans on glycoproteins

Name: Increased sialylated N-glycan level
Def: An abnormal increase in the concentration of sialylated N-glycans on glycoproteins.
Synonym: Increased concentration of sialylated N-glycans on glycoproteins

Name: Decreased sialylated N-glycan level
Def: An abnormal decrease in the concentration of sialylated N-glycans on glycoproteins.
Synonym: Decreased concentration of sialylated N-glycans on glycoproteins

Name: Abnormal high-mannose N-glycan level
Def: An abnormal concentration of high-mannose N-glycans on glycoproteins.
Synonym: Abnormal high-mannose N-glycans on glycoprotein concentration

Name: Increased high-mannose N-glycan level
Def: An abnormal increase in the concentration of high-mannose N-glycans on glycoproteins.
Synonym: Increased high-mannose N-glycans on glycoprotein concentration

Name: Decreased high-mannose N-glycan level
Synonym: An abnormal decrease in the concentration of high-mannose N-glycans on glycoproteins.
Decreased high-mannose N-glycans on glycoprotein concentration

Name: Abnormal core 1 O-glycan level
Def: An abnormal in the concentration of core 1 O-glycans on glycoproteins.

Name: Increased core 1 O-glycan level
Def: An abnormal increase in the concentration of core 1 O-glycans on glycoproteins.

Name: Decreased core 1 O-glycan level
Def: An abnormal decrease in the concentration of core 1 O-glycans on glycoproteins.

Name: Decreased O-mannosyl glycans on alpha-dystroglycan
Def: Hypoglycosylation of alpha-dystroglycan with O-mannosyl glycans. Alpha-dystroglycan is a functional target of O-mannosyl glycosylation and functional glycosylation of alpha-DG is essential in its interaction with the extracellular matrix.

Name: Increased monosialylated core 1 O-glycan level
Def: An abnormal increase in the concentration of monosialylated core 1 O-glycans on glycoproteins.

Name: Decreased monosialylated core 1 O-glycan level
Def: An abnormal decrease in the concentration of monosialylated core 1 O-glycans on glycoproteins.

Name: Increased disialylated core 1 O-glycan level
Def: An abnormal increase in the concentration of disialylated core 1 O-glycans on glycoproteins.

Name: Increased globoside Gb4 level
Def: An abnormal increase in the concentration of globoside Gb4.

Name: Increased hepatitis A virus antibody level
Def: An abnormally increased level of immunoglobulin against hepatitis A virus in the blood.

Name: Increased globoside Gb3 level
Def: An abnormal increase in the concentration of glycolipid globoside Gb3.

Name: Increased hepatitis B virus antibody level
Def: An abnormally increased level of immunoglobulin against hepatitis B virus in the blood.

Name: Absence of ganglioside GM3
Def: The absence of ganglioside GM3.

Name: Increased hepatitis C virus antibody level
Def: An abnormally increased level of immunoglobulin against hepatitis C virus in the blood.

Name: Increased Tn-antigen level
Def: An abnormal increase in the concentration of Tn antigen on glycoproteins.

Name: Abnormal proportion of naive CD4 T cells
Def: Any abnormality in the proportion of naive CD4 T cells relative to the total number of T cells.

Name: Abnormal proportion of naive CD8 T cells
Def: Any abnormality in the proportion of naive CD8 T cells relative to the total number of T cells.

Name: Elevated proportion of naive CD4 T cells
Comment: An abnormally increased proportion of naive CD4 T cells relative to the total number of T cells. {xref="PMID:22474485"}

Name: Elevated proportion of naive CD8 T cells
Def: An abnormally increased proportion of naive CD8 T cells relative to the total number of T cells.

Name: Reduced proportion of naive CD8 T cells
Def: An abnormally reduced proportion of naive CD8 T cells relative to the total number of T cells.

Name: Reduced proportion of naive CD4 T cells
Def: An abnormally reduced proportion of naive CD4 T cells relative to the total number of T cells.

Name: Abnormal proportion of CD4-positive, alpha-beta memory T cells
Def: An abnormal proportion of CD4-positive, alpha-beta memory T cells compared to the total number of T cells in the blood. These cells have the phenotype of CD45RO-positive and CD127-positive. This cell type is also described as being CD25-negative, CD44-high, and CD122-high.

Name: Abnormal proportion of CD8-positive, alpha-beta memory T cells
Def: An abnormal proportion of CD8-positive, alpha-beta memory T cells compared to the total number of T cells in the blood. A CD8-positive, alpha-beta T cell with memory phenotype is CD45RO and CD127-positive. This cell type is also described as being CD25-negative, CD44-high, and CD122-high.
Comment: Human CD8+T cells are commonly classified into four subsets based on the surface expression of the leukocyte common antigen isoform CD45RA and the lymph node addressin CCR7. Thereby, naive TN cells (CD45RA+/CCR7+) are separated from central memory TCM (CD45RA-/CCR7+), effector memory TEM (CD45RA-/CCR7-) and TEMRA (CD45RA+/CCR7-) T cells.

Name: Abnormal proportion of central memory CD4-positive, alpha-beta T cells
Def: An abnormal proportion of central memory CD4-positive, alpha-beta memory T cells compared to the total number of T cells in the blood. These cells have the phenotype of CCR7-positive, CD127-positive, CD45RA-negative, CD45RO-positive, and CD25-negative.

Name: Abnormal proportion of effector memory CD4-positive, alpha-beta T cells
Def: An abnormal proportion of effector memory CD4-positive, alpha-beta memory T cells compared to the total number of T cells in the blood. These cells have the phenotype CCR7-negative, CD127-positive, CD45RA-negative, CD45RO-positive, and CD25-negative.

Name: Abnormal proportion of effector memory CD8-positive, alpha-beta T cells
Def: An abnormal proportion of effector memory CD8-positive, alpha-beta memory T cells compared to the total number of T cells in the blood. These cells have the phenotype of CCR7-negative, CD127-positive, CD45RA-negative, CD45RO-positive, and CD25-negative.

Name: Abnormal proportion of central memory CD8-positive, alpha-beta T cells
Def: An abnormal proportion of central memory CD8-positive, alpha-beta memory T cells compared to the total number of T cells in the blood. These cells have the phenotype CCR7-positive, CD127-positive, CD45RA-negative, CD45RO-positive, and CD25-negative.

Name: Decreased proportion of CD8-positive, alpha-beta memory T cells
Def: Decreased proportion of CD8-positive, alpha-beta memory T cells compared to the total number of T cells in the blood. A CD8-positive, alpha-beta T cell with memory phenotype is CD45RO and CD127-positive. This cell type is also described as being CD25-negative, CD44-high, and CD122-high.

Name: Decreased proportion of CD4-positive, alpha-beta memory T cells
Def: Decresaed proportion of CD4-positive, alpha-beta memory T cells compared to the total number of T cells in the blood. These cells have the phenotype of CD45RO-positive and CD127-positive. This cell type is also described as being CD25-negative, CD44-high, and CD122-high.

Name: Decreased proportion of effector memory CD4-positive, alpha-beta T cells
Def: A reduced proportion of effector memory CD4-positive, alpha-beta memory T cells compared to the total number of T cells in the blood. These cells have the phenotype CCR7-negative, CD127-positive, CD45RA-negative, CD45RO-positive, and CD25-negative.

Name: Decreased proportion of central memory CD4-positive, alpha-beta T cells
Def: A reduced proportion of central memory CD4-positive, alpha-beta memory T cells compared to the total number of T cells in the blood. These cells have the phenotype of CCR7-positive, CD127-positive, CD45RA-negative, CD45RO-positive, and CD25-negative.

Name: Decreased proportion of central memory CD8-positive, alpha-beta T cells
Def: A reduced proportion of CD8-positive, alpha-beta central memory T cells compared to the total number of T cells in the blood. These cells have the phenotype CCR7-negative, CD127-positive, CD45RA-negative, CD45RO-positive, and CD25-negative.

Name: Decreased proportion of effector memory CD8-positive, alpha-beta T cells
Def: A reduced proportion of CD8-positive, alpha-beta effector memory T cells compared to the total number of T cells in the blood. These cells have the phenotype CCR7-negative, CD127-positive, CD45RA-negative, CD45RO-positive, and CD25-negative.

Name: Increased proportion of CD4-positive, alpha-beta memory T cells
Def: An abnormally elevated proportion of CD4-positive, alpha-beta memory T cells compared to the total number of T cells in the blood. These cells have the phenotype of CD45RO-positive and CD127-positive. This cell type is also described as being CD25-negative, CD44-high, and CD122-high.

Name: Increased proportion of CD8-positive, alpha-beta memory T cells
Def: An abnormally elevated proportion of CD8-positive, alpha-beta memory T cells compared to the total number of T cells in the blood. These cells have the phenotype CD45RO and CD127-positive. This cell type is also described as being CD25-negative, CD44-high, and CD122-high.

Name: Increased proportion of central memory CD4-positive, alpha-beta T cells
Def: An abnormally elevated proportion of central memory CD4-positive, alpha-beta memory T cells compared to the total number of T cells in the blood. These cells have the phenotype of CCR7-positive, CD127-positive, CD45RA-negative, CD45RO-positive, and CD25-negative.

Name: Increased proportion of effector memory CD4-positive, alpha-beta T cells
Def: An abnormally elevated proportion of effector memory CD4-positive, alpha-beta memory T cells compared to the total number of T cells in the blood. These cells have the phenotype CCR7-negative, CD127-positive, CD45RA-negative, CD45RO-positive, and CD25-negative.

Name: Increased proportion of effector memory CD8-positive, alpha-beta T cells
Def: An increased proportion of effector memory CD8-positive, alpha-beta T cells compared to the total number of T cells in the blood. These cells have the phenotype CCR7-negative, CD127-positive, CD45RA-negative, CD45RO-positive, and CD25-negative.

Name: Increased proportion of central memory CD8-positive, alpha-beta T cells
Def: An increased proportion of central memory CD8-positive, alpha-beta T cells compared to the total number of T cells in the blood. These cells have the phenotype CCR7-positive, CD127-positive, CD45RA-negative, CD45RO-positive, and CD25-negative.

Name: Bronchiolectasis
Def: Saccular dilatation of the terminal bronchioles.

Name: Positive blood lead test
Def: Detection of lead in the blood.

Name: Absent sebaceous glands
Def: Absence of the sebaceous gland, the holocrine gland that secretes sebum into the hair follicles, or in hairless areas into ducts.

Name: Worse in evening
Def: Applies to a sign or symptom that is exacerbated in the evening as compared to the day.

Name: Abnormality of the frontal bone
Def: An abnormality of the frontal bone.
Synonym: Abnormality of the bone of the forehead

Name: Abnormality of the lacrimal bone
Def: An abnormality of the lacrimal bone.

Name: Abnormality of the palatine bone
Def: An abnormality of the palatine bone.

Name: Abnormality of ethmoid bone
Def: An abnormality of the ethmoid bone

Name: Ectopic cilia of eyelid
Def: An eyelash that emerges from the underside (conjunctiva) of the upper or lower eyelid.

Name: Symblepharon
Def: A partial or complete adhesion of the palpebral conjunctiva of the eyelid to the bulbar conjunctiva of the eyeball.
Synonym: Eyelid adhesion to globe of eye

Name: Accessory eyelid
Def: The presence of more than the normal number of eyelids.

Name: Hypoplasia of eyelid
Def: Developmental hypoplasia of the eyelid.

Name: Microblepharia
Def: Abnormal shortness of the vertical dimensions of the eyelids.

Name: Defect of palpebral conjunctiva
Def: An abnormality of the palpebral conjunctiva.

Name: Incomplete ossification of palatine bone
Def: Failure to complete ossification (maturation and calcification) of the palatine bone.

Name: Absent palatine bone ossification
Def: Lack of formation of the palatine bone.

Name: Abnormality of musculature of soft palate
Def: An abnormality of one or more of the five muscles of the soft palate.

Name: Abnormal morphology of musculature of pharynx
Def: An abnormality of any of the muscles of the pharynx.
Synonym: Abnormality of muscles of the pharynx

Name: Abnormality of tensor veli palatini muscle
Def: An abnormality of the tensor veli palatini muscle

Name: Abnormality of uvular muscle
Def: An abnormality of the uvular muscle

Name: Abnormality of nasal musculature
Def: An abnormality of the muscles of the structure of the nose.
Synonym: Abnormality of musculature of the nose

Name: Abnormality of muscle of facial expression
Def: An abnormality of any of the muscles of facial expression, which are innervated by the seventh (VII) cranial nerve and control facial expression.
Synonym: Abnormality of muscle of facial expression
Abnormality of musculature of facial expression

Name: Abnormality of levator labii superioris alaeque nasi muscle
Def: An abnormality of the levator labii superioris alaeque nasi muscle.

Name: Abnormal common carotid artery morphology
Def: An abnormality of the common carotid arteries, which provide the arterial supply to the head and neck and give rise to the internal carotid artery and the external carotid artery.
Synonym: Abnormality of the common carotid artery

Name: Abnormality of the sphenoid sinus
Def: An abnormality of the sphenoid sinus, one of the mucosa-lined, normally air-filled paranasal sinuses of the bones of the skull. The sphenoid sinus is located within the sphenoid bone.

Name: Abnormality of the maxillary sinus
Def: An abnormality of the maxillary sinus, one of the mucosa-lined, normally air-filled paranasal sinuses of the bones of the skull. The maxillary sinus is located within the skeleton of the midface, lateral to the nasal cavity.
Synonym: Abnormality of the antrum of Highmore
Abnormality of the upper jaw sinus

Name: Abnormality of external jugular vein
Def: An abnormality of an external jugular vein of the neck.

Name: Bilateral facial palsy
Def: Two-sided or bilateral weakness of the muscles of facial expression and eye closure.
Synonym: Paralysis of both sides of the face
Weakness of both sides of the face

Name: Abnormality of the shape of the midface
Def: An abnormal morphology (form) of the midface or its components, the cheeks, maxilla, zygomatic bone, malar region, and infraorbital rims.
Synonym: Abnormality of the shape of the midface

Name: Hyperplasia of the maxilla
Def: Abnormally increased dimension of the maxilla, especially relative to the mandible, resulting in a malocclusion or malalignment between the upper and lower teeth or in anterior positioning of the nasal base, increased convexity of the face, increased nasolabial angle, or increased width (transverse dimension of the maxilla.

Name: Hyperplasia of the premaxilla
Def: An abnormality of the premaxilla (the embryonic structure that forms the anterior part of the maxilla) causing it to appear relatively large in size compared to the other parts of the maxilla or other facial structures.
Synonym: Hyperplasia of the primary palate bone
Increased size of the primary palate bone

Name: Body odor
Def: A perceived unpleasant smell given off by the body.

Name: Anal pain
Def: Pain in and around the anus or rectum (perianal region).

Name: Urethritis
Def: Inflammation of the urethra.
Comment: Urethritis is characterized by discharge, dysuria and/or urethral discomfort but may be asymptomatic. Common etiologies include gonococcal urethritis as well as infection by chlamydia trachomatis, mycoplasma genitalium, ureaplasma urealyticum, trichomonas vaginalis, anaerobes, herpes simplex virus, and adenovirus.

Name: Iris flocculi
Def: Multiple cysts along the pupillary margin that appear as spherical or tear-drop-shaped pigmented lesions or wrinkled masses emerging from the pupillary border of the iris.
Comment: Iris flocculi cause little, if any, visual impairment in most cases. However, they are occasionally associated with dissecting aortic aneurysm due to a shared mutation in smooth muscle that affects both the iris and the aorta. {xref="PMID:27843899"}

Name: Cornea verticillata
Def: Golden brown or gray deposits with a clockwise, whorl-like distribution in the inferior interpalpebal portion of the cornea.
Comment: Cornea verticillata can be a feature of Fabry disease and can occur as an adverse effect of mediciations including amiodarone. {xref="HPO:probinson"}

Name: Dysplastic gangliocytoma of the cerebellum
Def: It is a rare, slowly growing tumor of the cerebellum, a gangliocytoma sometimes considered to be a hamartoma, characterized by diffuse hypertrophy of the granular layer of the cerebellum.
Comment: Often associated with Cowden syndrome. {xref="PMID:11073535"}

Name: Moon facies
Def: A rounded, puffy face with fat deposits in the temporal fossa and cheeks, a double chin.
Comment: Moon facies can occur in persons treated with high-dose corticosteroids or with Cushing disease.

Name: Abnormality of gonadotropin-releasing hormone level
Def: A deviation from the normal circulating concentration of the normal gonadotropin-releasing hormone level secreted from the pituitary gland.

Name: Lack of gonadotropin-releasing hormone pulsatility
Def: Secretion of gonadotropin-releasing hormone that does not occur in a pulsatile fashion.
Comment: The decapeptide gonadotropin-releasing hormone (GnRH) is the master hormone regulating reproduction. GnRH is released from some 1000 neurons within the hypothalamus in a pulsatile manner. Hypothalamic GnRH gene expression occurs intermittently (in a pulsatile fashion). The primary target of hypothalamic GnRH is the anterior pituitary gonadotrope, which responds to stimulation by increasing the synthesis and secretion of the gonadotropins luteinzing hormone (LH) and follicle stimulating hormone (FSH), which in turn regulate gonadal development and function.

Name: Abnormal cardiac test
Def: Abnormal test result of cardiovascular physiology.

Name: Abnormal cardiac MRI
Def: Abnormal results of a MRI for the heart.

Name: Abnormal cardiac catheterization
Def: Abnormal results from the diagnostic tests resulting from cardiac catheterization.

Name: Abnormal cardiac exercise stress test
Def: Abnormal results of exercise on heart function.

Name: Abnormal resting energy expenditure from metabolic cart test
Def: Resting energy expenditure (REE) can be measured with indirect calorimetry using a metabolic cart, which is used to measure the oxygen consumption (VO2) and carbon dioxide production (VCO2).

Name: Abnormal cardiac biomarker test
Def: Abnormal blood test results measuring creatine kinase (CK), CK-MB, troponin (TROPI), myoglobin, and/or cardiac enzymes.

Name: Reduced brain gamma-aminobutyric acid level by MRS
Def: An decreased level of gamma-aminobutyric acid in the brain identified by magnetic resonance spectroscopy (MRS).

Name: Abnormal serum dehydroepiandrosterone level
Def: A deviation from the normal concentration of dehydroepiandrosterone in the circulation.
Comment: Dehydroepiandrosterone (DHEA), which is produced in the adrenal glands and the gonads, represents the most abundant circulating steroid hormone. It is a metabolic intermediate in the biosynthesis of the androgen and estrogen sex steroids.

Name: Shoulder muscle aplasia
Def: Absence of shoulder muscles.

Name: Aplasia of the musculature of the pelvis
Def: Absence of the musculature of the pelvis.

Name: Hypoplasia of the musculature of the pelvis
Def: Underdevelopment of the musculature of the pelvis.

Name: Aplastic colon
Def: Congenital absence of the colon

Name: Cotton wool plaques
Def: Deposition of large, diffuse cotton wool amyloid plaques (CWPs) lacking a dense core and associated neuritic changes.

Name: Abnormal hepatic glycogen storage
Def: Change in normal glycogen storage content.

Name: Sclerosis of the carpal bones
Def: An elevation in bone density in one or more carpal bones of the hand.

Name: Abnormal neuron branching
Def: Abnormality of the structure and branching of the dendrites of a neuron.

Name: Abnormal natural killer subset distribution
Def: Any abnormality in the proportion natural killer subsets relative to the total number of natural killer cells.

Name: Nasolacrimal sac obstruction
Def: Blockage of the nasolacrimal sac.

Name: Nasolacrimal sac granuloma
Def: A mass of granulation tissue in response to chronic dacryocystitis as polypoid formations or they follow accidental injury, from probing and as a reaction to retained foreign bodies in the sac.

Name: Nasolacrimal sac papilloma
Def: Benign tumor of the nasolacrimal sac.

Name: Nasolacrimal sac epithelial papillary carcinoma
Def: The malignant epithelial neoplasm with papillary growths in the nasolacrimal sac.

Name: Conjunctival cicatrization
Def: An abnormality of the conjuctiva and ocular surface caused by conjunctival inflammation and associated with scarring.

Name: Dermolipoma of the conjunctiva
Def: A benign tumor composed of adipose tissue and dense connective tissue usually located near the temporal fornix.

Name: Myopic astigmatism
Def: A condition where one or both of the two principal meridians focus in the front of the retina when the eye is at rest.

Name: Latent hypermetropia
Def: A term to describe when farsightedness is masked when the accommodative muscles are used to increase the focusing power of the eye.

Name: Eyelid retraction
Def: With the eyes in primary position, the sclera is visible above the superior corneal limbus.

Name: Upper eyelid retraction
Def: An elevation of the eyelid above the normal level in the primary position.

Name: Collier's sign
Def: A unilateral or bilateral eyelid retraction due to midbrain lesions.

Name: Seborrhoeic blepharitis
Def: Inflamation of the eyelid due to overactivity of the sebaceous gland.
Comment: There is some suggestion that yeast bacterial strain called Malassezia furfur may cause seborrhoeic dermatitis. This yeast bacterial strain thrives in the oil of human skin especially in adults. {xref="PMID:10777824"}

Name: Nasolacrimal sac lymphoma
Def: A type of lymphoma that involves the nasolacrimal sac.

Name: Delayed canalization of nasolacrimal duct
Def: A very common condition in which the extreme end of the nasolacrimal duct underneath the inferior turbinate fails to complete its canalization in the newborn period.

Name: Retinopathy of prematurity
Def: An avascular or abnormally vascularized retina that occurs in premature infants and can lead to blindness.

Name: Retinopathy of prematurity stage 1
Def: The retinal vessels stop and then a linear flat white line is present that usually runs the circumference of the vascular retina.

Name: Retinopathy of prematurity stage 2
Def: The accumulating neovascularization thickens and manifests as a linear bump. The neovascularization remains along the surface of the retina and does not extend off the retina into the cortical vitreous.

Name: Retinopathy of prematurity stage 3
Def: The neovascularization accumulates at the edge of the vascularized retina and extends into the vitreous (also called extra retinal fibrosis proliferation). In cases of Zone 2 and Zone 3, this may be sausage shaped. In more posterior Zone 1 disease, the stage 3 can appear as a direct extension of the normal retinal vessels but extending tangentially over the avascular retina.

Name: Retinopathy of prematurity stage 4
Def: Scar tissue that forms a continuous sheet coming up from the edge of the vascularized retina. This scar tissue can grow toward the vitreous base/posterior lens capsule resulting in traction, distortion, and even detachment.
Comment: Stage 4 can occur after treatment (unlike stages 1-3) and may be accelerated by the absence of vascular endothelial growth factor posttreatment leading to an accelerated cicatricial phase.

Name: Retinopathy of prematurity stage 4a
Def: A detachment that involves the peripheral retina that does not extend into the macula.

Name: Retinopathy of prematurity stage 4b
Def: A detachment that involves the peripheral retina that involves the macula itself. The detachment usually starts in the temporal periphery although can also involve the nasal retina as well.

Name: Retinopathy of prematurity stage 5
Def: Funnel detachment from the retina with generally traction in all four quadrants.

Name: Retinopathy of prematurity stage 5a
Def: An open funnel detachment of the retina with generally traction in all four quadrants.

Name: Retinopathy of prematurity stage 5b
Def: A closed funnel detachment of the retina with generally traction in all four quadrants.

Name: Retinopathy of prematurity zone I
Def: Retinopathy which extends from the center of the optic disc to twice the distance from the center of the optic disc to the center of the macula.

Name: Retinopathy of prematurity zone II
Def: Retinopathy which extends centrifugally from the edge of zone I to the nasal ora serrata.

Name: Retinopathy of prematurity zone III
Def: Retinopathy which is a residual crescent of retina anterior to zone II.

Name: Retinopathy of prematurity plus
Def: Venous dilatation and arteriolar tortuosity of the posterior retinal vessels and may later increase in severity to include iris vascular engorgement, poor pupillary dilatation (rigid pupil), and vitreous haze. This definition has been further refined in the later clinical trials in which the diagnosis of plus disease could be made if sufficient vascular dilatation and tortuosity are present in at least 2 quadrants of the eye.

Name: Retinopathy of prematurity pre-plus
Def: As vascular abnormalities of the posterior pole that are insufficient for the diagnosis of plus disease but that demonstrate more arterial tortuosity and more venous dilatation than normal.
Comment: Over time, the vessel abnormalities of pre-plus may progress to frank plus disease as the vessels dilate and become more tortuous. {xref="PMID:16009843"}

Name: Retinopathy of prematurity threshold
Def: A retinopathy with a 50% likelihood of progressing to retinal detachment. Threshold disease is considered to be present when stage 3 retinopathy of prematurity (ROP) is present in either zone I or zone II, with at least 5 continuous or 8 total clock hours of disease, and the presence of plus disease.

Name: Retinopathy of prematurity prethreshold
Def: High risk patients who were in Zone 1 (no Plus or stage 3) or Zone 2 with Plus or stage 3 but not both.

Name: Latent myopia
Def: The difference between total and manifest myopia.

Name: Paralytic ectropion
Def: A type of ectropion associated with orbicularis muscle weakness caused by cranial nerve VII palsy.

Name: Conjunctival dermolipoma
Def: A conjuctival lesion composed of adipose tissue and dense connective tissue. Such choristomas of dermal elements are normally found at the outer canthus, and have a gelatinous appearance. Classically, there is an indistinct posterior border (with the lesion frequently extending into the orbit) and a well-demarcated anterior border several millimetres posterior to the limbus.

Name: Absolute eccentric fixation
Def: Eccentric fixation in which the angle of eccentricity equals the objective angle of deviation.

Name: Abnormal ocular alignment
Def: Any deviation from the normal ocular alignment.

Name: Dissociated vertical deviation
Def: An incomitant tendency for an occluded eye to elevate and extort which resolves on uncovering.
Comment: Dissociated vertical deviation (DVD ) occurs when the level of illumination received by either eye is reduced sufficiently and as a result eye deviates progressively upwards, but reverts to its original position when the level of illumination returns to normally acceptable levels. It may sometimes be so asymmetrical as to be virtually unilateral and is associated with heterotropia usually of early onset. {xref="ISBN-13:978-0199679980", xref="ORCID:0000-0003-0986-4123"}

Name: Dissociated horizontal deviation
Def: A change in horizontal ocular alignment, unrelated to accommodation, that is brought about solely by a change in the balance of visual input from the two eyes.

Name: Alternating hypertropia
Def: A type of vertical tropia in which, when one eye is fixing, the other eye is deviated upwards.

Name: Alternating hyperphoria
Def: A type of vertical phoria in which, in dissociation, the occluded eye deviates upwards.

Name: Alternating hypotropia
Def: A type of vertical tropia in which, when one eye is fixing, the other eye is deviated downwards.

Name: Alternating hypophoria
Def: A type of vertical phoria in which, in dissociation, the occluded eye deviates downwards.

Name: Pseudophakia
Def: The term pseudophakia refers to having an artificial lens implanted after the natural eye lens has been removed. During cataract surgery the natural cloudy lens is replaced by an pseudophakia intraocular lens (IOL).

Name: Optic nerve gray crescent
Def: Having a characteristic appearance of a slate gray area of pigmentation within the disc margins that commonly appears along the inferotemporal or temporal neuroretinal rim areas.
Comment: This type of disc rim pigmentation can create the impression of neuroretinal rim thinning, and thus lead to the misdiagnosis of glaucoma or "glaucoma suspect" with attendant implications for overtreatment or unnecessary close monitoring of such patients. {xref="PMID:24862768"}

Name: Peripapillary atrophy
Def: Thinning in the layers of the retina and retinal pigment epithelium around the optic nerve.

Name: Foveal depigmentation
Def: Loss of pigment in the fovea centralis.

Name: Optic nerve sheath meningioma
Def: A benign tumour of meningothelial cells of the meninges that usually occurs in middle age. It is typically unilateral and there is an association with neurofibromatosis type 2.

Name: Periocular capillary hemangioma
Def: A capillary hemangioma surrounding the eyeball but within the orbit.

Name: Lymphangioma of the orbit
Def: A hamartoma of lymph vessels that usually presents in childhood. It tends to increase in size with head-down posture and with the Valsalva manoeuvre. Superficial lesions are visible as transilluminable cystic spaces of the lid or conjunctiva that may also contain blood. Deep lesions may cause gradual proptosis or present acutely with orbital pain and reduced vision due to haemorrhage.

Name: Orbital rhabdomyosarcoma
Def: A mesenchymal tumour that is considered to be the commonest primary orbital malignancy in children. Histologically, it may be differentiated into embryonal, alveolar, and pleomorphic types. It is usually intraconal or within the superior orbit.

Name: Food allergy
Def: Primary food allergies primarily occur as a result (most likely) of gastrointestinal sensitization to predominantly stable food allergens (glycoproteins). A secondary food allergy develops after primary sensitization to airborne allergens (e. g., pollen allergens) with subsequent reactions (due to cross-reactivity) to structurally related often labile allergens in (plant) foods.

Name: Latex allergy
Def: Latex allergy is an IgE-mediated immediate hypersensitivity response to natural rubber latex (NRL) protein with a variety of clinical signs ranging from contact urticaria, angioedema, asthma, and anaphylaxis.

Name: Food-induced anaphylaxis
Def: Food-induced anaphylaxis is a severe, potentially fatal, systemic allergic reaction that occurs suddenly after contact with an allergy-causing food.

Name: Venom-induced anaphylaxis
Def: A form of anaphylaxis that is triggered by exposure to venom.

Name: Stool xenobiotic
Def: Presence of xenobiotic in stool.

Name: Meconium xenobiotic
Def: Presence of a xenobiotic in meconium.

Name: Hair xenobiotic
Def: Presence of xenobiotic in hair.

Name: Plasma/serum xenobiotic
Def: Presence of a xenobiotic in plasma and/or serum.

Name: Gastric fluid xenobiotic
Def: Presence of a xenobiotic in gastric fluid.

Name: Decreased diastolic blood pressure
Def: Abnormal decrease in diastolic blood pressure.

Name: Decreased systolic blood pressure
Def: Abnormal decrease in systolic blood pressure.

Name: Isolated systolic hypertension
Def: Elevated systolic blood pressure without an elevated blood pressure.
Comment: Isolated systolic hypertension or an elevated systolic blood pressure without an elevated diastolic blood pressure is a known risk factor for incident heart failure in older adults. {xref="PMID:21947466"}

Name: Isolated diastolic hypotension
Def: A decrease in diastolic blood pressure (<60 mmHg) without a decrease in systolic blood pressure (> or = to 100 mmHg).
Comment: Isolated diastolic hypotension is a risk factor for incident heart failure. {xref="PMID:21947466"}

Name: Positive urine cocaine test
Def: Detection of cocaine or its major metabolite, benzoylecgonine, in urine.
Comment: Cocaine is an illicit stimulant that has a high potential for abuse and addiction.

Name: Positive urine barbiturate test
Def: Detection of barbiturate metabolites such as Phenobarbital in urine.
Comment: Barbiturates are central nervous depressants. They can reduce heart rate, breathing, and blood pressure. {xref="PMID:26339207"}

Name: Positive urine cannabinoid test
Def: Detection of delta-9-tetrahydrocannabinol (THC) or other cannabinoid metabolites in urine.
Comment: Cannabis (marijuana, hashish) is the most widely used illegal drug in the world. The primary psychoactive component in cannabis is delta9-tetrahydrocannabinol (THC), which is rapidly metabolized to equipotent 11-hydroxy-THC (11-OH-THC) and non-psychoactive 11-nor-9-carboxy- delta9-tetrahydrocannabinol (THCCOOH). {xref="PMID:21134021"}

Name: Positive urine benzodiazepines test
Def: Detection of benzodiazepine metabolites, primarily nordiazepam, oxazepam, and temazepam, in urine.

Name: Positive urine amphetamine test
Def: Detection of amphetamine or its metabolites in urine.

Name: Positive urine opioid test
Def: Detection of opioids or opioid metabolites in urine.
Comment: Opiates are the natural or synthetic drugs that have a morphine-like pharmacological action. Medically, opiates are used primarily for relief of pain. Opiates include morphine and drugs structurally similar to morphine (eg, codeine, hydrocodone, hydromorphone, oxycodone).

Name: Abnormal stool urobilinogen concentration
Def: Abnormal concentration of urobilinogen present in the stool.

Name: Increased stool urobilinogen concentration
Def: An increased amount of urobilinogen present in the stool.
Comment: Urobilinogen is formed from the reduction of bilirubin. An increased amount of urobilinogen in the urine may be indicative of liver disease. {xref="HPO:probinson"}

Name: Positive blood barbiturate test
Def: Detection of barbiturate metabolites such as Phenobarbital in blood.

Name: Abnormal CSF urate concentration
Def: Abnormal concentration of urate in the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF).
Comment: Urate is largely excluded from the brain under non-inflammatory conditions but increases in particular conditions such as Guillain-Barre Syndrome and bacterial meningitis. {xref="PMID:15571231"}

Name: Hypovalinemia
Def: A decreased amount of valine in the blood.

Name: Hypotyrosinemia
Def: An decreased concentration of tyrosine in the blood.

Name: Hypertryptophanemia
Def: An increased amount of tryptophan in the blood.

Name: Hypotryptophanemia
Def: A decreased amount of tryptophan in the blood.

Name: Hypothreoninemia
Def: A decreased amount of threonine in the blood.

Name: Hyperserinemia
Def: An increased amount of serine in the blood.

Name: Hypoprolinemia
Def: A decreased amount of proline in the blood.

Name: Decreased circulating hydroxyproline concentration
Def: A decreased amount of hydroxyproline in the blood.
Synonym: Low level of hydroxyproline in the blood

Name: Hypophenylalaninemia
Def: A decreased amount of phenylalanine in the blood.

Name: Hypolysinemia
Def: A decreased amount of lysine in the blood.

Name: Hypoleucinemia
Def: Decreased amount of leucine in the blood.

Name: Hypoisoleucinemia
Def: A decreased amount of isoleucine in the blood.

Name: Hypohistidinemia
Def: A decreased amount of histidine in the blood.

Name: Hypoglutaminemia
Def: Decreased amount of glutamine in the blood.

Name: Abnormal circulating glutamate concentration
Def: Any deviation from the normal concentration of glutamate in the blood circulation.

Name: Hyperglutamatemia
Def: An increased amount of glutamate in the blood.
Comment: Under normal circumstances, plasma glutamate concentration is 5-100 microM/L, the whole blood concentration is 150-300 microM/L while in the brain's ECF it is only 0.3-2 microM/L. {xref="PMID:22949847"}

Name: Hypoglutamatemia
Def: A decreased amount of glutamate in the blood.

Name: Abnormal glossopharyngeal nerve morphology
Def: Any structural anomaly of the glossopharyngeal nerve, the ninth paired cranial nerve (CN IX).
Comment: The glossopharyngeal nerve originates in the medulla oblongata. It Innervates the oropharynx, carotid body and sinus, as well as the posterior third of the tongue (where it mediates taste sensation), the middle ear cavity and the Eustachian tube. Additionally, it innervates the stylopharyngeus muscle of the pharynx.

Name: Abnormal great auricular nerve morphology
Def: Any structural anomaly of a great auricular nerve.
Comment: The great auricular nerve originates from the cervical plexus and ascends to the posterior inferior region of the parotid gland, where it divides into several small branches. The nerve supplies sensation for an extensive area of the face including the skin over the parotid gland and the mastoid process and the surface of the external ear. The great auricular nerve winds around the posterior aspect of the sternocleidomastoid muscle. After perforating the deep fascia, it ascends upon the sternocleidomastoid muscle beneath the platysma to the parotid gland, where it divides into an anterior and a posterior branch. The anterior branch provides sensory innervation to the skin overlying the parotid gland and communicates with the facial nerve in the substance of the gland. The posterior branch innervates the skin over the mastoid and the posterior surface of the auricle except at its upper part.
